title.zh: 卷二百四十三 列傳第二 后妃下
title.raw: 卷二百四十三 列傳第二 后妃下 Volume 243 Biographies 2: Empresses and Consorts 2

sentences.zh: 神宗欽聖獻肅向皇后、欽成朱皇后、欽慈陳皇后、林賢妃、武賢妃 哲宗昭慈孟皇后、昭懷劉皇后 徽宗顯恭王皇后、鄭皇后、王貴妃、韋賢妃、喬貴妃、劉貴妃 欽宗朱皇后 高宗憲節邢皇后、憲聖慈烈吳皇后、潘賢妃、張賢妃、劉貴妃、劉婉儀、張貴妃 孝宗成穆郭皇后、成恭夏皇后、成肅謝皇后、蔡貴妃、李賢妃 光宗慈懿李皇后、黃貴妃 甯宗恭淑韓皇后、恭聖仁烈楊皇后 理宗謝皇后 度宗全皇后、楊淑妃

translations.literal: Under Emperor Shenzong: Empress Qinxian Xiansu Xiang, Empress Qincheng Zhu, Empress Qinci Chen, Worthy Consort Lin, Worthy Consort Wu. Under Emperor Zhezong: Empress Zhaoci Meng, Empress Zhaohuai Liu. Under Emperor Huizong: Empress Xiangong Wang, Empress Zheng, Imperial Noble Consort Wang, Worthy Consort Wei, Worthy Consort Qiao, Imperial Consort Liu. Under Emperor Qinzong: Empress Zhu. Under Emperor Gaozong: Empress Xianjie Xing, Empress Xiansheng Cilie Wu, Worthy Consort Pan, Worthy Consort Zhang, Imperial Consort Liu, Honored Lady Liu, Imperial Noble Consort Zhang. Under Emperor Xiaozong: Empress Chengmu Guo, Empress Chenggong Xia, Empress Chengsu Xie, Imperial Consort Cai, Worthy Consort Li. Under Emperor Guangzong: Empress Ciyi Li, Imperial Consort Huang. Under Emperor Ningzong: Empress Gongshu Han, Empress Gongsheng Renlie Yang. Under Emperor Lizong: Empress Xie. Under Emperor Duzong: Empress Quan, Imperial Concubine Yang Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The empresses and consorts treated in this volume are: for Shenzong, Empress Qinxian Xiansu Xiang, Empress Qincheng Zhu, Empress Qinci Chen, and the Worthy Consorts Lin and Wu; for Zhezong, Empress Zhaoci Meng and Empress Zhaohuai Liu; for Huizong, Empress Xiangong Wang, Empress Zheng, Imperial Noble Consort Wang, and the Worthy Consorts Wei and Qiao, together with Imperial Consort Liu; for Qinzong, Empress Zhu; for Gaozong, Empress Xianjie Xing, Empress Xiansheng Cilie Wu, the Worthy Consorts Pan and Zhang, Imperial Consort Liu, Honored Lady Liu, and Imperial Noble Consort Zhang; for Xiaozong, Empresses Chengmu Guo, Chenggong Xia, and Chengsu Xie, Imperial Consort Cai, and Worthy Consort Li; for Guangzong, Empress Ciyi Li and Imperial Consort Huang; for Ningzong, Empress Gongshu Han and Empress Gongsheng Renlie Yang; for Lizong, Empress Xie; and for Duzong, Empress Quan and Imperial Concubine Yang Shu.

sentences.zh: 欽聖獻肅向皇后

translations.literal: Empress Qinxian Xiansu Xiang
translations.idiomatic: Empress Qinxian Xiansu Xiang

sentences.zh: 神宗欽聖憲肅向皇后，河內人，故宰相敏中曾孫也。

translations.literal: Empress Qinxian Xiansu Xiang of Emperor Shenzong was a native of Henei and a great-granddaughter of the former chief councilor Minzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Qinxian Xiansu Xiang, consort of Emperor Shenzong, came from Henei and was a great-granddaughter of the former chief councilor Minzhong.

sentences.zh: 治平三年，歸於潁邸，封安國夫人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhiping, she entered the household of the Prince of Ying and was enfeoffed as Lady of the State of Anguo.
translations.idiomatic: In 1066 she married into the household of the Prince of Ying and received the title Lady of Anguo.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，立為皇后。

translations.literal: When Shenzong took the throne, she was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong ascended the throne, she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 帝不豫，后贊宣仁。

translations.literal: When the emperor fell ill, the empress supported Empress Dowager Xuanren.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor grew gravely ill, the empress backed Empress Dowager Xuanren.

sentences.zh: 后定建儲之議。

translations.literal: The empress settled the deliberation on establishing an heir.
translations.idiomatic: It was the empress who settled the question of who should succeed to the throne.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，尊為皇太后。

translations.literal: When Zhezong was enthroned, she was honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong came to the throne, she was honored as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 宣仁命葺慶壽故宮以居后，后辭曰：「安有姑居西而婦處東，瀆上下之分。」

translations.literal: Xuanren ordered the old Qing Shou Palace repaired for the empress dowager to live in, but the empress declined, saying, "How could a mother-in-law dwell in the west while a daughter-in-law sits in the east? That would violate the proper order between superior and inferior."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xuanren had the old Qing Shou Palace restored for her to live in, but the empress dowager refused, saying, "How could a mother-in-law take the west wing while a daughter-in-law occupies the east? That would overturn the proper hierarchy."

sentences.zh: 不敢徙，遂以慶壽後殿為隆祐宮居之。

translations.literal: She dared not move there and so took up residence in the rear hall of Qing Shou, which became the Longyou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: She would not move and instead made her home in the rear hall of Qing Shou, which was designated the Longyou Palace.

sentences.zh: 帝將卜后及諸王納婦，后敕向族勿以女置選中。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to choose an empress and brides for the princes, the empress dowager instructed the Xiang clan not to place their daughters in the selection.
translations.idiomatic: When the court was about to select an empress and brides for the imperial princes, she ordered her own Xiang clan not to enter their daughters in the competition.

sentences.zh: 族黨有欲援例以恩換閤職，及為選人求京秩者，且言有特旨，后曰：「吾族未省用此例，何庸以私情撓公法。」

translations.literal: Some in her clan wished to invoke precedent to exchange favor for a post in the Privy Secretariat, or to seek metropolitan rank for examination candidates, claiming there was a special edict. The empress dowager said, "Our clan has never used such precedents—why should private feeling be allowed to bend public law?"
translations.idiomatic: Clansmen tried to trade imperial favor for Secretariat posts or to secure metropolitan office for relatives in the examinations, citing a supposed special edict. She replied, "Our family has never relied on such precedents. Why should private ties be allowed to override the law?"

sentences.zh: 一不與。

translations.literal: She granted none of these requests.
translations.idiomatic: She refused every one of them.

sentences.zh: 帝倉卒晏駕，獨決策迎端王。

translations.literal: When the emperor died suddenly, she alone decided to welcome Prince Duan.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died unexpectedly, she alone resolved to bring Prince Duan to the throne.

sentences.zh: 章惇異議，不能沮。

translations.literal: Zhang Dun raised objections but could not deter her.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun objected, but he could not sway her.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，請權同處分軍國事，后以長君辭。

translations.literal: When Huizong was enthroned, he asked her to share authority over state affairs; because he was already of age, the empress dowager declined.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong took the throne, he asked her to rule jointly with him, but she declined on the ground that he was already a grown emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝泣拜，移時乃聽。

translations.literal: The emperor wept and bowed for a long while before she finally assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept and bowed to her for a long time before she at last agreed.

sentences.zh: 凡紹聖、元符以還，惇所斥逐賢大夫士，稍稍收用之。

translations.literal: All worthy grandees and gentlemen whom Zhang Dun had driven out since the Shaosheng and Yuanfu eras were gradually brought back into service.
translations.idiomatic: She gradually recalled to office the worthy officials whom Zhang Dun had banished since the Shaosheng and Yuanfu reigns.

sentences.zh: 故事有如禦正殿、避家諱、立誕節之類，皆不用。

translations.literal: Precedents such as holding court in the Main Hall, avoiding the imperial clan taboo, and establishing a birthday festival were all set aside.
translations.idiomatic: She declined the usual regal ceremonies—holding court in the Main Hall, observing name taboos, and instituting a birthday festival among them.

sentences.zh: 至聞賓召故老、寬徭息兵、愛民崇儉之舉，則喜見於色。

translations.literal: When she heard of measures such as summoning venerable elders, easing levies, halting warfare, cherishing the people, and promoting frugality, her pleasure showed in her face.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever she heard that the court was summoning elder statesmen, easing taxes, ending campaigns, caring for the people, or practicing frugality, her delight showed plainly on her face.

sentences.zh: 才六月，即還政。

translations.literal: After only six months she returned the government to him.
translations.idiomatic: After only six months she handed power back to him.

sentences.zh: 明年正月崩，年五十六。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year she died, aged fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: She died the following spring at the age of fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 帝追念不已，乃數加恩兩舅，宗良、宗回，皆位開府儀同三司，封郡王。

translations.literal: The emperor's remembrance did not cease, and he repeatedly bestowed favor on her two uncles, Zongliang and Zonghui, appointing both to the rank of Grand Preceptor with the privileges of the Three Excellencies and enfeoffing them as princes of commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not stop mourning her memory and repeatedly honored her two uncles, Zongliang and Zonghui, raising both to Grand Preceptor with Three Excellencies privileges and enfeoffing them as commandery princes.

sentences.zh: 而自敏中以上三世，亦追列王爵，非常典也。

translations.literal: For three generations above Minzhong as well, princely titles were posthumously conferred—an extraordinary departure from precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Princely rank was also conferred posthumously on three generations of her forebears above Minzhong—an honor outside normal precedent.

sentences.zh: 欽成朱皇后

translations.literal: Empress Qincheng Zhu
translations.idiomatic: Empress Qincheng Zhu

sentences.zh: 欽成朱皇后，開封人。

translations.literal: Empress Qincheng Zhu was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Qincheng Zhu came from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 父崔傑，早世；

translations.literal: Her father Cui Jie died young;
translations.idiomatic: Her father Cui Jie died while she was still young;

sentences.zh: 母李，更嫁朱士安。

translations.literal: her mother Li remarried Zhu Shi'an.
translations.idiomatic: and her mother Li remarried a man named Zhu Shi'an.

sentences.zh: 后鞠于所親任氏。

translations.literal: The empress was reared by a kinswoman of the Ren clan.
translations.idiomatic: She was brought up by a relative of the Ren family.

sentences.zh: 熙甯初，入宮為禦侍，進才人、婕妤，生哲宗及蔡王似、徐國公主，累進德妃。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xining era she entered the palace as an imperial attendant, was promoted to Talented Lady and then to Graceful Beauty, bore Zhezong as well as Prince Cai Si and the Princess of Xu, and was repeatedly promoted until she reached Virtuous Consort.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xining reign she entered the palace as an attendant, rose through Talented Lady and Graceful Beauty, gave birth to the future Zhezong, Prince Cai Si, and the Princess of Xu, and was promoted step by step to Virtuous Consort.

sentences.zh: 哲宗即位，尊為皇太妃。

translations.literal: When Zhezong took the throne she was honored as Grand Imperial Consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong ascended the throne she was honored as Grand Imperial Consort.

sentences.zh: 時宣仁、欽聖二太后皆居尊，故稱號未極。

translations.literal: At the time Empresses Dowager Xuanren and Qinsheng both held supreme standing, so her title was not yet at the highest rank.
translations.idiomatic: Empresses Dowager Xuanren and Qinsheng both still held supreme standing, so her title was not yet the highest.

sentences.zh: 宣仁詔：《春秋》之義，「母以子貴」，其尋繹故實，務致優隆。

translations.literal: Xuanren issued an edict: "By the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals, 'a mother is honored through her son'—search out the ancient precedents and strive to grant her the fullest elevation."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanren issued an edict citing the Spring and Autumn principle that "a mother is honored through her son," ordering officials to search out precedents and grant her the fullest honors.

sentences.zh: 於是輿蓋、仗衛、冠服，悉侔皇后。

translations.literal: Thereupon carriage canopies, guard escorts, and caps and robes all matched those of an empress.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter her carriage canopies, guard escorts, and ceremonial dress all matched those of an empress.

sentences.zh: 紹聖中，欽聖復命即閤建殿，改乘車為輿，出入由宣德東門，百官上箋稱「殿下」，名所居為聖瑞宮。

translations.literal: In the Shaosheng era Qinsheng again ordered a hall built at the Privy Secretariat; carriage was changed to palanquin; entry and exit were through the east gate of Xuande; the hundred officials addressed memorials to her as "Your Highness"; and her residence was named the Palace of Sagely Auspice.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaosheng reign Qinsheng ordered a hall built at the Privy Secretariat, replaced her carriage with a palanquin, had her enter and leave through Xuande East Gate, required officials to address her as "Your Highness," and named her residence the Palace of Sagely Auspice.

sentences.zh: 贈崔、任、朱三父皆至師、保。

translations.literal: The three fathers of the Cui, Ren, and Zhu clans were all posthumously raised to Grand Tutor and Grand Protector.
translations.idiomatic: The three fathers of the Cui, Ren, and Zhu clans were all posthumously made grand tutor and grand protector.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，奉禮尤謹。

translations.literal: When Huizong was enthroned she observed ritual with especial care.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong took the throne she observed ritual with especial care.

sentences.zh: 崇甯元年二月薨，年五十一。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Chongning she died, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the second month of 1102, at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 追冊為皇后，上尊諡，陪葬永裕陵。

translations.literal: She was posthumously enregistered as empress, given a posthumous title of honor, and buried beside the Yongyu Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously made empress, granted a posthumous honorific title, and interred beside the Yongyu Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 欽慈陳皇后，開封人。

translations.literal: Empress Qinci Chen was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Qinci Chen came from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 幼穎悟莊重，選入掖庭，為禦侍。

translations.literal: As a child she was clever and dignified; selected into the rear palace she became an imperial attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and dignified from childhood, she was selected for the rear palace and became an imperial attendant.

sentences.zh: 生徽宗，進美人。

translations.literal: She bore Huizong and was promoted to Beautiful Lady.
translations.idiomatic: She bore the future Huizong and was promoted to Beautiful Lady.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，守陵殿，思顧舊恩，毀瘠骨立。

translations.literal: When the emperor died she kept watch at the mausoleum hall, thinking on past kindness until she wasted away to skin and bone.
translations.idiomatic: After Shenzong died she kept vigil at the mausoleum hall, pining for past kindness until she was wasted to skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 左右進粥、藥，揮使去，曰：「得早侍先帝，願足矣！」

translations.literal: Those around her offered gruel and medicine; she waved them away, saying: "If I may soon attend the late emperor, that is all I wish!"
translations.idiomatic: Attendants brought gruel and medicine, but she waved them away, saying, "If I may soon attend the late emperor, that is enough for me!"

sentences.zh: 未幾薨，年三十二。

translations.literal: Before long she died, aged thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: She soon died, aged thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 追冊為皇太后，上尊諡，陪葬永裕陵。

translations.literal: She was posthumously enregistered as empress dowager, given a superior posthumous title, and buried beside the Yongyu Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously made empress dowager, granted a superior posthumous title, and interred beside the Yongyu Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 林賢妃，南劍人，三司使特之孫，司農卿洙之女。

translations.literal: Worthy Consort Lin, a native of Nanjian, was granddaughter of the Three Departments Commissioner Te and daughter of Minister of Finance Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy Consort Lin came from Nanjian. She was a granddaughter of the Three Departments Commissioner Te and daughter of the Minister of Finance Zhu.

sentences.zh: 幼選入宮，既長，遂得幸，封永嘉郡君，升美人。

translations.literal: Selected into the palace in youth, when she grew up she won favor, was enfeoffed Lady of Yongjia Commandery, and advanced to Beautiful Lady.
translations.idiomatic: Chosen for the palace as a girl, she later won the emperor's favor, was created Lady of Yongjia Commandery, and rose to Beautiful Lady.

sentences.zh: 生燕王俁、越王偲、邢國公主，進婕妤。

translations.literal: She bore the Prince of Yan, You; the Prince of Yue, Si; and the Princess of Xing; and was promoted to Shining Beauty.
translations.idiomatic: She bore the Princes of Yan and Yue, You and Si, and the Princess of Xing, and was promoted to Shining Beauty.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: She died.
translations.idiomatic: She died.

sentences.zh: 詔用一品禮葬，贈貴儀，又贈賢妃。

translations.literal: An edict ordered burial with first-rank rites; posthumously she was given Exalted Lady, then Worthy Consort.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered first-rank funeral rites; she was posthumously made Exalted Lady and then Worthy Consort.

sentences.zh: 武賢妃，始以選入宮。

translations.literal: Worthy Consort Wu first entered the palace through the selection process.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy Consort Wu first entered the palace as a selected candidate.

sentences.zh: 元豐五年，進才人。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanfeng she was promoted to Talented Lady.
translations.idiomatic: In 1082 she was promoted to Talented Lady.

sentences.zh: 生吳王佖、賢和公主。

translations.literal: She bore Prince Wu Bian and the Princess Xianhe.
translations.idiomatic: She gave birth to Prince Wu Bian and the Princess Xianhe.

sentences.zh: 曆美人、婕妤。

translations.literal: She passed through the ranks of Beautiful Lady and Graceful Beauty.
translations.idiomatic: She rose through the ranks of Beautiful Lady and Graceful Beauty.

sentences.zh: 徽宗即位，進昭儀、賢妃。

translations.literal: When Huizong took the throne, she was promoted to Exalted Concubine and then Worthy Consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong ascended the throne, she was promoted to Exalted Concubine and then Worthy Consort.

sentences.zh: 大觀元年薨，乘輿臨奠，輟朝三日，諡曰惠穆。

translations.literal: She died in the first year of Daguan; the emperor went in person to offer mourning, court was suspended for three days, and she was given the posthumous title Huimu.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 1107. The emperor attended her funeral in person, suspended court for three days, and gave her the posthumous title Huimu.

sentences.zh: 昭慈孟皇后

translations.literal: Empress Zhaoci Meng
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhaoci Meng

sentences.zh: 哲宗昭慈聖獻孟皇后，洺州人，眉州防禦使、馬軍都虞候、贈太尉元之孫女也。

translations.literal: Empress Zhaoci Shengxian Meng of Emperor Zhezong was a native of Mozhou and a granddaughter of Yuan, who had been Defender of Meizhou, Commandant of the Palace Cavalry, and was posthumously made Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhaoci Shengxian Meng, consort of Emperor Zhezong, came from Mozhou. She was a granddaughter of Yuan, who had served as Defender of Meizhou and Commandant of the Palace Cavalry and was posthumously honored as Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 初，哲宗既長，宣仁高太后曆選世家女百余入宮。

translations.literal: Earlier, once Zhezong had come of age, Empress Dowager Xuanren of the Gao clan had repeatedly selected more than a hundred daughters of eminent families to enter the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong reached maturity, Empress Dowager Xuanren of the Gao clan had more than a hundred daughters of prominent families brought into the palace for selection.

sentences.zh: 后年十六，宣仁及欽聖向太后皆愛之，教以女儀。

translations.literal: The empress was sixteen; both Xuanren and Empress Dowager Qinsheng Xiang favored her and instructed her in women's rites.
translations.idiomatic: She was sixteen. Both Empress Dowager Xuanren and Empress Dowager Qinsheng Xiang took a liking to her and taught her courtly deportment.

sentences.zh: 元祐七年，諭宰執：「孟氏子能執婦禮，宜正位中宮。」

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanyou she instructed the chief ministers: "The girl of the Meng clan is able to observe a wife's rites and should be installed in the central palace."
translations.idiomatic: In 1092 she told the chief ministers, "The Meng girl knows how to conduct herself as a wife and ought to be made empress."

sentences.zh: 命學士草制。

translations.literal: She ordered academicians to draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: She ordered the Hanlin academicians to draft the installation edict.

sentences.zh: 又以近世禮儀簡略，詔翰林、台諫、給舍與禮官議冊后六禮以進。

translations.literal: Because recent ritual practice had grown simplified, an edict ordered the Hanlin Academy, censorial and remonstrance officials, drafting and review officers, and ritual specialists to deliberate on the six rites of empress installation and submit their plan.
translations.idiomatic: Because court ritual had grown simplified in recent times, she also ordered the Hanlin Academy, the censorate, remonstrance officials, drafting officers, and ritual specialists to work out the six rites of empress installation and present a plan.

sentences.zh: 至是，命尚書左僕射呂大防攝太尉，充奉迎使，同知樞密院韓忠彥攝司徒副之；

translations.literal: At this time she appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Lü Dafang to act as Grand Marshal and serve as welcoming envoy, with Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Han Zhongyan acting as Minister of Education as his deputy;
translations.idiomatic: She then appointed Left Vice Director Lü Dafang to act as Grand Marshal and head the welcoming mission, with Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs Han Zhongyan acting as Minister of Education as his deputy;

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞蘇頌攝太尉，充發策使，簽書樞密院事王岩叟攝司徒副之；

translations.literal: Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs Su Song to act as Grand Marshal and serve as question-poser, with Signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs Wang Yansou acting as Minister of Education as his deputy;
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistant Director Su Song to act as Grand Marshal and conduct the questioning rite, with Signatory Wang Yansou of the Bureau of Military Affairs as Minister of Education deputy;

sentences.zh: 尚書右丞蘇轍攝太尉，充告期使，皇叔祖同知大宗正事宗景攝宗正卿副之；

translations.literal: Right Assistant Director Su Zhe to act as Grand Marshal and serve as date-announcing envoy, with the emperor's great-great-uncle, Associate Director of the Imperial Clan Court Zong Jing, acting as Director of the Imperial Clan Court as his deputy;
translations.idiomatic: Right Assistant Director Su Zhe to act as Grand Marshal and announce the wedding date, with the emperor's great-great-uncle Zong Jing of the Imperial Clan Court as deputy Director of the Imperial Clan Court;

sentences.zh: 皇伯祖判大宗正事高密郡王宗晟攝太尉，充納成使，翰林學士范百祿攝宗正卿副之；

translations.literal: the emperor's great-granduncle, Acting Director of the Imperial Clan Court and Prince of Gaomi Zong Sheng, to act as Grand Marshal and serve as completion envoy, with Hanlin Academician Fan Bailu acting as Director of the Imperial Clan Court as his deputy;
translations.idiomatic: the emperor's great-granduncle, Prince of Gaomi Zong Sheng, Director of the Imperial Clan Court, to act as Grand Marshal for the completion rite, with Hanlin Academician Fan Bailu as deputy Director of the Imperial Clan Court;

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書王存攝太尉，充納吉使，權戶部尚書劉奉世攝宗正卿副之；

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Wang Cun to act as Grand Marshal and serve as auspice-receiving envoy, with Acting Minister of Revenue Liu Fengshi acting as Director of the Imperial Clan Court as his deputy;
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Wang Cun to act as Grand Marshal for receiving the auspicious omens, with Acting Minister of Revenue Liu Fengshi as deputy Director of the Imperial Clan Court;

sentences.zh: 翰林學士梁燾攝太尉，充納采、問名使，御史中丞鄭雍攝宗正卿副之。

translations.literal: and Hanlin Academician Liang Tao to act as Grand Marshal and serve as gift-presenting and name-inquiring envoy, with Censor-in-Chief Zheng Yong acting as Director of the Imperial Clan Court as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: and Hanlin Academician Liang Tao to act as Grand Marshal for presenting the betrothal gifts and inquiring after her name, with Censor-in-Chief Zheng Yong as deputy Director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 帝親禦文德殿冊為皇后。

translations.literal: The emperor personally presided in the Wende Hall to install her as empress.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself presided in the Wende Hall to install her as empress.

sentences.zh: 宣仁太后語帝曰：「得賢內助，非細事也。」

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xuanren told the emperor, "To gain a worthy helpmate within the palace is no small matter."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xuanren told the emperor, "To win a worthy consort at your side is no small matter."

sentences.zh: 進后父閤門祗候在為宗儀使、榮州刺史，母王氏華原郡君。

translations.literal: The empress's father, Gate Attendant Zai, was promoted to Commissioner of Clan Ritual and made Prefect of Rongzhou; her mother, Lady Wang, was made Lady of Huayuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Zai, a gate attendant, was promoted to Commissioner of Clan Ritual and appointed prefect of Rongzhou, while her mother Lady Wang was ennobled as Lady of Huayuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 久之，劉婕妤有寵。

translations.literal: After some time Graceful Beauty Liu won favor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Graceful Beauty Liu came into favor.

sentences.zh: 紹聖三年，后朝景靈宮，訖事，就坐，諸嬪禦立侍，劉獨背立簾下，后閤中陳迎兒呵之，不顧，閤中皆忿。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shaosheng, when the empress paid court at the Jingling Shrine, after the rites were concluded she took her seat while the consorts stood in attendance; Liu alone stood with her back to the others beneath the curtain. Chen Ying'er of the empress's inner staff rebuked her, but she paid no heed, and all in the inner staff were angry.
translations.idiomatic: In 1096, after the empress had finished worship at the Jingling Shrine and taken her seat, the other consorts stood in attendance while Liu alone turned her back on them beneath the curtain. Chen Ying'er of the empress's staff scolded her, but she ignored the rebuke and the entire inner staff seethed with anger.

sentences.zh: 冬至日，會朝欽聖太后于隆祐宮，后御坐未髹金飾，宮中之制，惟后得之。

translations.literal: On the winter solstice they met Empress Dowager Qinsheng for audience at the Longyou Palace. The empress's throne was lacquered but not gilded—a privilege in the palace reserved for the empress alone.
translations.idiomatic: On the winter solstice they attended Empress Dowager Qinsheng at the Longyou Palace. The empress alone was entitled to a lacquered throne without gilding, a privilege reserved for her in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 婕妤在他坐，有慍色，從者為易坐，制與后等。

translations.literal: The Graceful Beauty sat on another seat and looked resentful; her attendants exchanged it for one equal in rank to the empress's.
translations.idiomatic: Graceful Beauty Liu sat on a lesser seat and looked resentful, so her attendants replaced it with one matching the empress's in rank.

sentences.zh: 眾弗能平，因傳唱曰：「皇太后出！」

translations.literal: The company could not accept this and so called out, "The empress dowager is coming forth!"
translations.idiomatic: The others could not stomach this and called out, "The empress dowager is coming!"

sentences.zh: 后起立，劉亦起，尋各復其所，或已撤婕妤坐，遂僕於地。

translations.literal: The empress rose, and Liu rose as well; presently each returned to her place, but Liu's seat had already been removed, and she fell to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The empress stood up, and Liu stood too. When each returned to her place, Liu's seat had already been taken away and she fell to the floor.

sentences.zh: 懟不復朝，泣訴於帝。

translations.literal: In anger she ceased attending court and wept her grievance before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, she refused to attend court again and wept her complaint before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 內侍郝隨謂婕妤曰：「毋以此戚戚，願為大家早生子，此坐正當為婕妤有也。」

translations.literal: The inner attendant Hao Sui said to the Graceful Beauty, "Do not grieve over this. Pray bear Our Lord a son soon—this seat ought rightly to be yours."
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Hao Sui told her, "Do not brood on this. If you bear His Majesty a son soon, that seat will rightly be yours."

sentences.zh: 會后女福慶公主疾，后有姊頗知醫，嘗已后危疾，以故出入禁掖。

translations.literal: It happened that the empress's daughter, Princess Fuqing, fell ill. The empress had an elder sister skilled in medicine who had once cured a grave illness of the empress, and for that reason was allowed to enter and leave the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress's daughter, Princess Fuqing, fell ill, her elder sister, who knew medicine and had once saved the empress from a grave illness, was permitted to come and go in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 公主藥弗效，持道家治病符水入治。

translations.literal: When the princess's medicine did not work, she brought in Daoist healing talisman-water to treat her.
translations.idiomatic: When ordinary medicine failed, she brought in Daoist talisman-water to treat the princess.

sentences.zh: 后驚曰：「姊甯知宮中禁嚴，與外間異邪？」

translations.literal: The empress said in alarm, "Sister, do you not know how strict the prohibitions of the palace are and how they differ from the world outside?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress said in alarm, "Sister, do you not know how strict palace rules are and how different they are from the world outside?"

sentences.zh: 令左右藏之；

translations.literal: She ordered her attendants to hide it;
translations.idiomatic: She had her attendants hide the talisman;

sentences.zh: 俟帝至，具言其故。

translations.literal: when the emperor arrived she explained the whole matter to him.
translations.idiomatic: and when the emperor came she told him the whole story.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此人之常情耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "This is only human feeling."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That is only human nature."

sentences.zh: 后即藝符於帝前。

translations.literal: The empress then burned the talisman before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The empress then burned the talisman in front of him.

sentences.zh: 宮禁相汀傳，厭魅之端作矣。

translations.literal: The report spread through the inner palace, and the beginnings of a sorcery case arose.
translations.idiomatic: Word spread through the inner palace, and the sorcery scandal began.

sentences.zh: 未幾，后養母聽宣夫人燕氏、尼法端與供奉官王堅為后禱祠。

translations.literal: Before long it came out that the empress's foster mother, Lady Yan of Tingxuan, the nun Faduan, and the palace attendant Wang Jian had performed prayer rites on the empress's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Soon it emerged that her foster mother Lady Yan of Tingxuan, the nun Faduan, and palace attendant Wang Jian had been praying on the empress's behalf.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔入內押班梁從政、管當禦藥院蘇珪，即皇城司鞫之，捕逮宦者、宮妾幾三十人，搒掠備至，肢體毀折，至有斷舌者。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict ordered Inner Palace Duty Officer Liang Congzheng and Superintendent of the Imperial Pharmacy Su Gui to interrogate the case immediately at the Imperial City Office. Nearly thirty eunuchs and palace women were seized; beating was applied to the full extent, limbs were broken, and some even had their tongues cut out.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, Liang Congzheng of the inner staff and Su Gui of the Imperial Pharmacy were ordered to investigate at once in the Imperial City Office. Nearly thirty eunuchs and palace women were arrested, tortured without mercy, their limbs broken, and some even had their tongues cut out.

sentences.zh: 獄成，命侍御史董敦逸覆錄，罪人過庭下，氣息僅屬，無一人能出聲者。

translations.literal: When the case was concluded, Attending Censor Dong Dunyi was ordered to review the record. The culprits were brought before the court barely breathing, and not one could speak.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was complete, Attending Censor Dong Dunyi was ordered to review the record. The prisoners were brought before the court barely alive, and not one could utter a word.

sentences.zh: 敦逸秉筆疑未下，郝隨等以言脅之。

translations.literal: Dunyi held his brush, hesitating to write the verdict, and Hao Sui and others threatened him with words.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Dunyi hesitated with brush in hand, and Hao Sui and the others threatened him.

sentences.zh: 敦逸畏禍及己，乃以奏牘上。

translations.literal: Fearing calamity for himself, Dunyi submitted the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing for his own safety, he submitted the memorial.

sentences.zh: 詔廢后，出居瑤華宮，號華陽教主、玉清妙靜仙師，法名沖真。

translations.literal: An edict deposed the empress. She was sent to live in the Yaohua Palace, styled Leader of the Huayang Teaching and Transcendent Master of Jade Clarity and Wondrous Stillness, with the religious name Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: An edict deposed her. She was sent to the Yaohua Palace and given the religious titles Leader of the Huayang Teaching and Transcendent Master of Jade Clarity and Wondrous Stillness, with the dharma name Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 初，章惇誣宣仁后有廢立計，以后逮事宣仁，惇又陰附劉賢妃，欲請建為后，遂與郝隨構成是獄，天下冤之。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhang Dun had slandered Empress Dowager Xuanren with a plot to depose and enthrone; because the empress had long served Xuanren, Zhang Dun also secretly aligned himself with Worthy Consort Liu and wished to have her installed as empress. He therefore joined Hao Sui in fabricating this case, and all under Heaven regarded it as a grievous injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun had earlier slandered Empress Dowager Xuanren with a charge of plotting deposition and enthronement. Because the empress had long been close to Xuanren, Zhang Dun secretly backed Worthy Consort Liu and hoped to make her empress. He and Hao Sui together fabricated the case, and the empire regarded it as a gross injustice.

sentences.zh: 敦逸奏言：「中宮之廢，事有所因，情有可察。

translations.literal: Dunyi memorialized, saying, "The deposition of the central palace had its causes, and the circumstances can be examined.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Dunyi memorialized, "The empress's deposition had its causes, and the circumstances deserve scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 詔下之日，天為之陰翳，是天不欲廢后也；

translations.literal: On the day the edict was issued the sky turned dark—Heaven did not wish the empress deposed;
translations.idiomatic: On the day the edict was issued the sky darkened—Heaven did not want her deposed;

sentences.zh: 人為之流涕，是人不欲廢后也。」

translations.literal: people wept for her—mankind did not wish the empress deposed."
translations.idiomatic: and people wept for her—mankind did not want her deposed either."

sentences.zh: 且言：「嘗覆錄獄事，恐得罪天下後世。」

translations.literal: He also said, "When I reviewed this case I feared offending all under Heaven and posterity."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "When I reviewed this case I feared earning the condemnation of the empire and of posterity."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「敦逸不可更在言路。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Dunyi must not remain on the remonstrance path."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Dong Dunyi must no longer serve on the remonstrance track."

sentences.zh: 曾布曰：「陛下本以皇城獄出於近習推治，故命敦逸錄問，今乃貶錄問官，何以取信中外？」

translations.literal: Zeng Bu said, "Your Majesty originally had the Imperial City case investigated by close attendants and therefore ordered Dunyi to review it. Now to demote the reviewing officer—how can trust be won within and without?"
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Bu said, "Your Majesty had the Imperial City case investigated by close attendants and appointed Dong Dunyi to review it. If you now punish the reviewer, how will the court and the empire trust the outcome?"

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: He thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented.

sentences.zh: 帝久亦悔之，曰：「章惇誤我。」

translations.literal: After a long while the emperor also came to regret it and said, "Zhang Dun misled me."
translations.idiomatic: In time the emperor came to regret the affair as well and said, "Zhang Dun misled me."

sentences.zh: 元符末，欽聖太后將復后位，適有布衣上書，以后為言者，即命以官；

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuanfu era Empress Dowager Qinsheng was about to restore the empress to her position. It happened that a commoner submitted a memorial speaking on the empress's behalf, and he was immediately given an office;
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Yuanfu era Empress Dowager Qinsheng was preparing to restore the empress. A commoner happened to submit a memorial on her behalf and was immediately given an official post;

sentences.zh: 於是詔后還內，號元祐皇后，時劉號元符皇后故也。

translations.literal: thereupon an edict ordered the empress back into the palace, styled Empress of Yuanyou, since Liu was then styled Empress of Yuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: and an edict then brought the empress back into the palace as Empress of Yuanyou, while Liu was styled Empress of Yuanfu.

sentences.zh: 崇甯初，郝隨諷蔡京再廢后，昌州判官馮澥上書言后不得復。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongning, Hao Sui urged Cai Jing to depose the empress again, and Feng Xi, magistrate of Changzhou, submitted a memorial saying the empress must not be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongning era Hao Sui urged Cai Jing to depose her again, and Feng Xi, magistrate of Changzhou, memorialized that she must not be restored.

sentences.zh: 台臣錢遹、石豫、左膚等連章論韓忠彥等信一布衣狂言，復己廢之後，以掠虛美，望斷以大義。

translations.literal: Censorial officials Qian Yi, Shi Yu, Zuo Fu, and others submitted successive memorials arguing that Han Zhongyan and others had trusted the wild words of a commoner in restoring an already deposed empress in order to seize empty praise, and they asked that the matter be decided on great principle.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Qian Yi, Shi Yu, Zuo Fu, and others submitted memorial after memorial accusing Han Zhongyan and his allies of trusting a mad commoner's words to restore an empress already deposed, all to win hollow praise, and they urged a principled decision.

sentences.zh: 蔡京與執政許將、溫益、趙挺之、張商英皆主其說。

translations.literal: Cai Jing and the chief ministers Xu Jiang, Wen Yi, Zhao Tingzhi, and Zhang Shangying all upheld this view.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing and the chief ministers Xu Jiang, Wen Yi, Zhao Tingzhi, and Zhang Shangying all sided with them.

sentences.zh: 徽宗從之，詔依紹聖詔旨，復居瑤華宮，加賜希微元通知和妙靜仙師。

translations.literal: Huizong followed them. An edict, in accordance with the Shaosheng edict, sent her back to the Yaohua Palace and additionally granted her the title Transcendent Master of Rare Subtlety, Primordial Communication, Harmonious Accord, and Wondrous Stillness.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong agreed. By edict, following the Shaosheng precedent, she was sent back to the Yaohua Palace and given the additional title Transcendent Master of Rare Subtlety, Primordial Communication, Harmonious Accord, and Wondrous Stillness.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，瑤華宮火，徙居延甯宮；

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingkang era the Yaohua Palace burned, and she moved to the Yanning Palace;
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingkang era the Yaohua Palace burned, and she moved to the Yanning Palace;

sentences.zh: 又火，出居相國寺前之私第。

translations.literal: when it burned again she left the palace to live in a private residence before the Xiangguo Temple.
translations.idiomatic: when that too burned she left the palace for a private house near the Xiangguo Temple.

sentences.zh: 金人圍汴，欽宗與近臣議再復后，尊為元祐太后。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens besieged Bian, Qinzong discussed with his close ministers restoring the empress again and honoring her as Empress Dowager of Yuanyou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens besieged Bian, Qinzong and his close advisers debated restoring her once more and honoring her as Empress Dowager of Yuanyou.

sentences.zh: 詔未下而京城陷。

translations.literal: The edict had not yet been issued when the capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: The edict had not yet been promulgated when the capital fell.

sentences.zh: 時六宮有位號者皆北遷，后以廢獨存。

translations.literal: At that time all in the six palaces who held rank were moved north; the deposed empress alone remained.
translations.idiomatic: By then every consort with a formal rank had been taken north; only the deposed empress remained behind.

sentences.zh: 張邦昌僭位尊號為宋太后，迎居延福宮，受百官朝。

translations.literal: Zhang Bangchang usurped the throne and honored her as Song Empress Dowager, welcomed her to the Yanfu Palace, and received the obeisance of the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bangchang seized power, styled her Song Empress Dowager, installed her in the Yanfu Palace, and received the court's obeisance.

sentences.zh: 胡舜陟、馬伸又言，政事當取后旨。

translations.literal: Hu Shunzhi and Ma Shen again said that government affairs should follow the empress's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shunzhi and Ma Shen again urged that state business should take its direction from the empress.

sentences.zh: 邦昌乃復上尊號元祐皇后，迎入禁中，垂簾聽政。

translations.literal: Bangchang then again bestowed the honorific title Yuanyou Empress, welcomed her into the inner palace, and had her hold court from behind the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bangchang restored her as Yuanyou Empress, brought her into the Forbidden City, and set her to rule from behind the curtain.

sentences.zh: 后聞康王在濟，遣尚書左右丞馮澥、李回及兄子忠厚持書奉迎。

translations.literal: The empress, hearing that Prince Kang was at Ji, sent the Left and Right Vice Directors of the Department of State Affairs Feng Cao and Li Hui, together with her nephew Zhonghou, bearing letters to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When she learned that Prince Kang was in Ji, she sent Vice Directors Feng Cao and Li Hui and her nephew Zhonghou with imperial messages to escort him.

sentences.zh: 命副都指揮使郭仲荀將所部扈衛，又命禦營前軍統制張俊逆於道。

translations.literal: She ordered Deputy Commander-in-Chief Guo Zhongxun to lead his troops in escort, and also ordered Front Army Commander of the Imperial Camp Zhang Jun to meet him on the road.
translations.idiomatic: She tasked Deputy Commander-in-Chief Guo Zhongxun with escorting him at the head of his command and sent Imperial Camp front-army commander Zhang Jun ahead to meet him on the route.

sentences.zh: 尋降手書，播告天下。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward a handwritten imperial letter was issued and proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: She soon issued a personal decree announcing the news to the empire.

sentences.zh: 王至南京，后遣宗室士㒟及內侍邵成章奉圭寶、乘輿、服禦迎，王即皇帝位，改元，后以是日撤簾，尊后為元祐太后。

translations.literal: When the prince reached Nanjing, the empress sent the clansman Shi and the inner attendant Shao Chengzhang bearing the jade seal and tally, the imperial carriage, and ceremonial robes to welcome him; the prince then took the throne, changed the reign title, and on that same day the empress withdrew from behind the curtain and was honored as Empress Dowager Yuanyou.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Kang reached Nanjing, she sent a royal clansman and the eunuch Shao Chengzhang with the imperial regalia to receive him; he ascended the throne and changed the era name, and that day she stepped down from regency and was honored as Empress Dowager Yuanyou.

sentences.zh: 尚書省言，「元」字犯后祖名，請易以所居宮名，遂稱隆祐太后。

translations.literal: The Department of State Affairs reported that the character yuan violated the empress's ancestral name taboo and requested replacing it with the name of the palace where she dwelled; she was therefore styled Empress Dowager Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat noted that the character "yuan" violated the empress dowager's family naming taboo and asked to substitute her palace name instead, so she was called Empress Dowager Longyou.

sentences.zh: 上將幸揚州，命仲荀衛太后先行，駐揚州州治。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to visit Yangzhou and ordered Zhongxun to escort the empress dowager there first, quartering her at the Yangzhou prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor prepared to go to Yangzhou, he sent Zhongxun ahead to guard the empress dowager at the prefectural headquarters there.

sentences.zh: 會張浚請先定六宮所居地，遂詔忠厚奉太后幸杭州，以苗傅為扈從統制。

translations.literal: As it happened Zhang Jun requested that the residence of the six palaces be settled first, so an edict was issued for Zhonghou to escort the empress dowager to Hangzhou, with Miao Fu as commander of the escort.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jun urged settling where the inner court would live first, the court ordered Zhonghou to take the empress dowager to Hangzhou, with Miao Fu commanding the escort.

sentences.zh: 逾年，傅與劉正彥作亂，請太后聽政。

translations.literal: After more than a year, Fu and Liu Zhengyan raised a rebellion and requested that the empress dowager take charge of government.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan rebelled and demanded that the empress dowager resume rule.

sentences.zh: 又請立皇子。

translations.literal: They also requested that a prince be enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: They also pressed to install an imperial prince on the throne.

sentences.zh: 太后諭之曰：「自蔡京、王黼更祖宗法，童貫起邊事，致國家禍亂。

translations.literal: The empress dowager instructed them, saying, "From the time Cai Jing and Wang Fu altered the laws of the ancestors, and Tong Guan stirred up border affairs, the state has fallen into calamity.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager told them, "Ever since Cai Jing and Wang Fu rewrote the ancestral institutions and Tong Guan provoked frontier wars, the realm has been thrown into chaos.

sentences.zh: 今皇帝無失德，止為黃潛善、汪伯彥所誤，皆已逐矣。」

translations.literal: The present emperor has committed no fault; he was only misled by Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan, who have already been driven out."
translations.idiomatic: The present emperor has done nothing wrong; he was merely misled by Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan, and both have already been dismissed."

sentences.zh: 傅等言必立皇太子，太后曰：「今強敵在外，我以婦人抱三歲小兒聽政，將何以令天下？」

translations.literal: Fu and the others said a crown prince must be enthroned. The empress dowager said, "With a powerful enemy outside our borders, how am I—a woman holding a three-year-old child in regency—to command the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: Fu and his party insisted that a crown prince must be installed. She replied, "With a formidable enemy at our gates, how can I—a woman governing with a three-year-old in my arms—command the empire?"

sentences.zh: 傅等泣請，太后力拒之。

translations.literal: Fu and the others wept as they pleaded, but the empress dowager firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: They wept and begged, but she held firm against them.

sentences.zh: 帝聞事急，詔禪位元子，太后垂簾聽政。

translations.literal: The emperor, hearing how urgent matters had become, issued an edict abdicating in favor of his eldest son, and the empress dowager held court from behind the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned how dire things were, he abdicated to his eldest son while the empress dowager assumed regency.

sentences.zh: 朱勝非請令臣僚得獨對論機事，仍日引傅黨一人上殿，以釋其疑。

translations.literal: Zhu Shengfei requested that officials be allowed private audiences to discuss urgent affairs, while each day one member of Fu's faction would be brought into the hall to dispel their suspicions.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shengfei proposed letting ministers confer privately on strategy while each day summoning one of Miao Fu's followers to court to ease their mistrust.

sentences.zh: 太后從之，每見傅等，曲加慰撫，傅等皆喜。

translations.literal: The empress dowager agreed; whenever she received Fu and the others she treated them with special soothing words, and they were all pleased.
translations.idiomatic: She agreed, and whenever she met Miao Fu and his men she spoke to them with deliberate kindness until they were reassured.

sentences.zh: 韓世忠妻梁氏在傅軍中，勝非以計脫之，太后召見，勉令世忠速來，以清岩陛。

translations.literal: Han Shizhong's wife Lady Liang was in Fu's army; Shengfei contrived her escape, the empress dowager summoned her, and urged her to have Shizhong come quickly to clear the rocky steps of the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liang, Han Shizhong's wife, was held in Miao Fu's camp; Zhu Shengfei engineered her release, and the empress dowager received her and urged Han Shizhong to hurry back and secure the palace.

sentences.zh: 梁氏馳入世忠軍，諭太后意。

translations.literal: Lady Liang galloped into Shizhong's army and conveyed the empress dowager's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liang rode at speed to Han Shizhong's camp and relayed the empress dowager's message.

sentences.zh: 世忠等遂引兵至，逆黨懼。

translations.literal: Shizhong and the others then led their troops up, and the rebels were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Han Shizhong and his allies then marched in, and the mutineers grew fearful.

sentences.zh: 朱勝非等誘以復辟，命王世修草狀進呈。

translations.literal: Zhu Shengfei and the others enticed them with the promise of restoration and ordered Wang Shixiu to draft a memorial for presentation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shengfei and his allies tempted them with restoration and had Wang Shixiu draft the memorial to be submitted.

sentences.zh: 太后喜曰：「吾責塞矣。」

translations.literal: The empress dowager said with joy, "My burden is discharged."
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager exclaimed with relief, "My obligation is fulfilled."

sentences.zh: 再以手劄趣帝還宮，即欲撤簾。

translations.literal: She again sent a handwritten note urging the emperor to return to the palace and immediately wished to withdraw the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: She sent another personal note pressing him to return and prepared at once to end her regency.

sentences.zh: 帝令勝非請太后一出禦殿，乃命撤簾。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Shengfei to request that the empress dowager come out once to the imperial hall, and only then commanded that the curtain be withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Shengfei ask her to appear once in the main hall before he ordered the curtain drawn back.

sentences.zh: 是日，上皇太后尊號。

translations.literal: On that day the honorific title of empress dowager was bestowed upon her.
translations.idiomatic: That same day she was granted a formal empress-dowager honorific.

sentences.zh: 太后聞張浚忠義，欲一見之，帝為召浚至禁中。

translations.literal: The empress dowager, hearing of Zhang Jun's loyalty and righteousness, wished to see him once; the emperor summoned Jun into the inner palace for her.
translations.idiomatic: Having heard of Zhang Jun's loyalty, she wished to meet him, and the emperor had him brought into the palace.

sentences.zh: 承議郎馮楫嘗貽書苗傅勸復辟，上未之知，太后白其事，楫得遷秩。

translations.literal: Gentleman for Discussion Feng Ji had once sent a letter to Miao Fu urging restoration; the emperor did not know of it; the empress dowager informed him of the affair, and Ji was promoted in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ji, a civil official, had secretly urged Miao Fu to restore the emperor; when the empress dowager exposed this to Gaozong, Feng was actually promoted.

sentences.zh: 帝幸建康，命簽書樞密院事鄭玨衛太后繼發，比至，帝率群臣迎於郊。

translations.literal: The emperor went to Jiankang and ordered Privy Council signatory Zheng Jue to guard the empress dowager and set out after him; when she arrived, the emperor led the hundred officials to welcome her at the outskirts.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong moved to Jiankang and sent Zheng Jue to escort the empress dowager; when she arrived, he and the entire court met her outside the city.

sentences.zh: 會防秋迫，命劉寧止制置江、浙，衛太后往洪州，百司非預軍事者悉從。

translations.literal: As the autumn defense season pressed, Liu Ningzhi was appointed commissioner for Jiang and Zhe, to escort the empress dowager to Hongzhou; all offices not concerned with military affairs were to follow.
translations.idiomatic: With the autumn defense season pressing, Liu Ningzhi was made commissioner for Jiang and Zhe to guard the empress dowager on her journey to Hongzhou, and every civil office not tied to the war effort went with her.

sentences.zh: 仍命滕康、劉玨權知三省樞密院事從行，凡四方奏讞、吏部差注、舉辟、功賞之類，皆隸焉。

translations.literal: Teng Kang and Liu Jue were also ordered to act as temporary heads of the Three Departments and Privy Council on the journey; all memorials and legal cases from the four directions, Ministry of Personnel appointments, recommendations, and merit rewards fell under them.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Kang and Liu Jue were also assigned to handle the Three Departments and Privy Council on the road, so memorials, legal cases, personnel appointments, recommendations, and rewards all passed through them.

sentences.zh: 復命四廂都指揮使楊惟忠，將兵萬人衛從。

translations.literal: Yang Weizhong, commander of the four palace-corps divisions, was again ordered to lead ten thousand troops in escort.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Weizhong, commander of the four palace-corps divisions, was also told to escort her with ten thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 帝慮敵人來侵，密諭康、玨緩急取太后旨，便宜以行。

translations.literal: The emperor, fearing enemy invasion, secretly instructed Kang and Jue that in urgency or calm they should take the empress dowager's command and act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a Jin attack, he secretly told Kang and Jue to follow the empress dowager's orders in any crisis and act on their own authority as needed.

sentences.zh: 過落星寺，舟覆，宮人溺死者十數，惟太后舟無虞。

translations.literal: Passing Luoxing Temple, a boat capsized and more than ten palace women drowned; only the empress dowager's boat was unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: Near Luoxing Temple a boat overturned and a dozen palace women drowned; the empress dowager's vessel alone escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 既至洪州，議者言：「金人自蘄、黃渡江，陸行二百餘里，即到洪州。」

translations.literal: After reaching Hongzhou, advisers said, "If the Jurchens cross the Yangzi from Qi and Huang and march overland more than two hundred li, they will reach Hongzhou."
translations.idiomatic: Once she reached Hongzhou, advisers warned that if the Jin crossed from Qi and Huang and marched overland a little more than two hundred li, they would be upon the city."

sentences.zh: 帝憂之，命劉光世屯江州。

translations.literal: The emperor was troubled and ordered Liu Guangshi to garrison Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, the emperor ordered Liu Guangshi to hold Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 光世不為備，金人遂自大冶縣徑趣洪州。

translations.literal: Guangshi made no preparations, and the Jurchens then pressed straight on Hongzhou from Daye County.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshi failed to prepare, and the Jin drove straight for Hongzhou from Daye County.

sentences.zh: 康、玨奉太后行，次吉州。

translations.literal: Kang and Jue escorted the empress dowager on the road and halted at Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kang and Jue escorted her onward and paused at Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 金人追急，太后乘舟夜行。

translations.literal: The Jurchen pursuit was pressing, and the empress dowager traveled by boat at night.
translations.idiomatic: With the Jin closing in, she fled by boat under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 質明，至太和縣，舟人景信反，楊惟忠兵潰，失宮人一百六十，康、玨俱遁，兵衛不滿百，遂往虔州。

translations.literal: At daybreak they reached Taihe County; the boatman Jing Xin turned rebel, Yang Weizhong's troops broke and fled, one hundred sixty palace women were lost, Kang and Jue both fled, and the guard numbered fewer than a hundred, so they proceeded to Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn they reached Taihe, where the boatman Jing Xin mutinied; Yang Weizhong's force collapsed, 160 palace women were lost, Kang and Jue deserted, and with fewer than 100 guards they fled to Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 太后及潘妃以農夫肩輿而行。

translations.literal: The empress dowager and Consort Pan were carried in sedan chairs on farmers' shoulders.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager and Worthy Consort Pan were borne along in sedan chairs carried by local farmers.

sentences.zh: 帝慮太后徑入閩、廣，遣使曆詢后所在，及知在虔州，遂命中書舍人李正民來朝謁。

translations.literal: The emperor, fearing the empress dowager would go straight into Fujian and Guang, sent envoys to inquire everywhere after her whereabouts; when he learned she was at Qianzhou, he then ordered Secretariat Drafter Li Zhengmin to come and pay court.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing she might press on into Fujian or Guangdong, he sent messengers to trace her; learning she was at Qianzhou, he dispatched Li Zhengmin of the Secretariat to attend her.

sentences.zh: 時虔州府庫皆空，衛軍所給，惟得沙錢，市買不售，與百姓交鬥，縱火肆掠。

translations.literal: At that time the Qianzhou prefectural treasuries were all empty; what the guard troops were paid was only inferior coin, which merchants would not accept, and they fought with the common people, set fires, and looted at will.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhou's treasuries were empty, the guards were paid only in debased coin that merchants would not take, and they brawled with civilians before looting and burning at will.

sentences.zh: 土豪陳新率眾圍城，康、玨、惟忠弗能禁。

translations.literal: The local strongman Chen Xin led a crowd to besiege the city, and Kang, Jue, and Weizhong could not restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: A local magnate named Chen Xin led a mob to besiege the city, and Kang, Jue, and Weizhong proved unable to stop them.

sentences.zh: 惟忠步將胡友自外引兵破新於城下，新乃去。

translations.literal: Weizhong's infantry commander Hu You led troops from outside to defeat Xin below the walls, and Xin then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhong's infantry commander Hu You brought troops from outside and routed Chen Xin below the walls, and Chen withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，罷康、玨，命盧益、李回代之。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he dismissed Kang and Jue and ordered Lu Yi and Li Hui to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: On learning this, the emperor removed Kang and Jue and replaced them with Lu Yi and Li Hui.

sentences.zh: 諭輔臣曰：「朕初不識太后，自迎至南京，愛朕不啻己出。

translations.literal: He instructed the chief ministers, saying, "At first I did not know the empress dowager; from the day I welcomed her at Nanjing she has loved me no less than if I were her own child.
translations.idiomatic: He told his ministers, "I did not know the empress dowager at first; from the day I welcomed her at Nanjing she has loved me as if I were her own son.

sentences.zh: 今在數千里外，兵馬驚擾，當亟奉迎，以愜朕朝夕慕念之意。」

translations.literal: Now she is several thousand li away amid the alarm of troops and horses; she should be welcomed back at once to satisfy my longing morning and evening."
translations.idiomatic: Now she is thousands of li away in the turmoil of war—I must bring her back at once to ease my constant longing."

sentences.zh: 遂遣禦營司都統辛企宗、帶禦器械潘永思迎歸。

translations.literal: He then sent Imperial Camp commander-in-chief Xin Qizong and arms-bearing attendant Pan Yongsi to welcome her back.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Imperial Camp commander Xin Qizong and arms-bearing attendant Pan Yongsi to escort her home.

sentences.zh: 太后至越，帝親迎於行宮門外，遍問所過守臣治狀。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager reached Yue, the emperor met her in person outside the gate of the traveling palace and questioned her in detail about how the guarding officials along the route had governed.
translations.idiomatic: When she reached Yue, the emperor met her in person outside the traveling palace and asked in detail how the officials along the route had governed.

sentences.zh: 入宮禁中，嘗微苦風眩。

translations.literal: After entering the inner palace, she once suffered mildly from dizziness caused by wind.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside the palace she suffered a mild bout of vertigo.

sentences.zh: 有宮人自言善符呪，疾良已。

translations.literal: A palace woman claimed skill in charms and incantations, and the illness quickly abated.
translations.idiomatic: A palace woman claimed skill in charms and incantations, and she recovered quickly.

sentences.zh: 太后驚曰：「仁吾豈敢復聞此語耶！」

translations.literal: The empress dowager said in alarm, "After Ren, how dare I hear such words again!"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager exclaimed in alarm, "After Empress Dowager Xuanren, how could I dare hear such talk again!"

sentences.zh: 立命出之。

translations.literal: She immediately ordered the woman expelled.
translations.idiomatic: She immediately ordered the woman expelled.

sentences.zh: 太后生辰，置酒宮中，從容謂帝曰：「宣仁太后之賢，古今母后未有其比。

translations.literal: On the empress dowager's birthday, wine was set out in the palace, and she said at leisure to the emperor, "The virtue of Empress Dowager Xuanren—no empress mother in antiquity or the present has equaled it.
translations.idiomatic: On her birthday she set out wine in the palace and remarked to the emperor at leisure, "Empress Dowager Xuanren's virtue—no empress mother in history has ever matched it.

sentences.zh: 昔奸臣肆為謗誣，雖嘗下詔明辨，而國史尚未刪定，豈足傳信？

translations.literal: In the past wicked ministers wantonly spread slander; although an edict was once issued to clarify the matter, the National History has not yet been revised and corrected—how could that suffice to transmit faith?
translations.idiomatic: Wicked ministers once spread slanders against her; though an edict once clarified the truth, the National History has never been corrected—is that enough to restore her reputation?

sentences.zh: 吾意在天之靈，不無望於帝也。」

translations.literal: I believe her spirit in Heaven cannot be without some expectation of the emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Surely her spirit in Heaven still looks to you for justice."

sentences.zh: 帝聞之悚然。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this he shuddered.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor shuddered when he heard this.

sentences.zh: 后乃更修《神宗》、《哲宗實錄》，始得其正，而奸臣情狀益著。

translations.literal: The empress dowager then had the Veritable Records of Shenzong and Zhezong revised anew, and at last the record was set right, while the conduct of the wicked ministers grew clearer still.
translations.idiomatic: She then had the Veritable Records of Shenzong and Zhezong revised, at last setting the record straight and exposing the wicked ministers all the more clearly.

sentences.zh: 帝事太后極孝，雖帷帳皆親視；

translations.literal: The emperor served the empress dowager with the utmost filial piety, even attending personally to her curtains and bedding;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor served her with the utmost filial devotion, even tending her curtains and bedding himself;

sentences.zh: 或得時果，必先獻太后，然後敢嘗。

translations.literal: whenever he obtained seasonal fruit he always presented it to the empress dowager first and only then dared to taste it.
translations.idiomatic: and whenever he received seasonal fruit he offered it to her first and only then tasted it himself.

sentences.zh: 宣教郎范燾與忠厚有憾，誣與太后密養欽宗子。

translations.literal: Gentleman for Discussion Fan Tao, bearing a grudge against Zhonghou, falsely accused them of secretly raising a son of Emperor Qinzong for the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Tao, a civil official who bore a grudge against Zhonghou, falsely accused them of secretly raising a son of Emperor Qinzong on the empress dowager's behalf.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕于太后如母子，安得有此。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Between the empress dowager and me it is like mother and son—how could there be such a thing?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Between the empress dowager and me it is like mother and son—how could such a thing exist?"

sentences.zh: 即治其罪。

translations.literal: He immediately punished the crime.
translations.idiomatic: He had the accuser punished at once.

sentences.zh: 紹興五年春，患風疾，帝旦暮不離左右，衣弗解帶者連夕。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year of Shaoxing she fell ill with wind ailments; the emperor morning and evening did not leave her side, and for successive nights he did not unfasten his belt.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1135 she fell ill with a wind disorder; the emperor never left her side day or night and went several nights without unfastening his belt.

sentences.zh: 四月，崩於行宮之西殿，年五十九。

translations.literal: In the fourth month she died in the west hall of the traveling palace at the age of fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month she died in the west hall of the traveling palace at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 遺命擇地攢殯，俟軍事寧，歸葬園陵。

translations.literal: Her testament ordered choosing a site for temporary enshrinement and, once military affairs were calm, returning her for burial at the imperial park tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Her will directed that a site be chosen for temporary enshrinement until the war ended, then that she be returned for burial in the imperial necropolis.

sentences.zh: 帝詔曰：「朕以繼體之重，當從重服，凡喪祭用母后臨朝禮。」

translations.literal: The emperor's edict stated, "In my weighty position as successor to the throne I should observe the full mourning; for all funeral and sacrificial rites use the ceremonies of an empress mother who ruled from behind the curtain."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor decreed, "Given the weight of my succession, I shall observe the fullest mourning and use for all funeral rites the protocol for an empress mother who ruled from behind the curtain."

sentences.zh: 上尊號曰昭慈獻烈皇太后，推恩外家凡五十人。

translations.literal: The honorific title Empress Dowager Zhaoci Xianlie was bestowed, and grace was extended to fifty persons of her maternal clan.
translations.idiomatic: She was given the posthumous title Empress Dowager Zhaoci Xianlie, and favors were extended to fifty members of her maternal family.

sentences.zh: 殯於會稽上皇村，附神主於哲宗室，位在昭懷皇后上。

translations.literal: She was enshrined at Shanghuang Village in Kuaiji, her spirit tablet placed in Zhezong's shrine above Empress Zhaohuai.
translations.idiomatic: She was temporarily enshrined at Shanghuang Village in Kuaiji, her spirit tablet placed in Zhezong's shrine above Empress Zhaohuai.

sentences.zh: 三年，改諡昭慈聖獻。

translations.literal: Three years later her posthumous title was changed to Zhaoci Shengxian.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later her posthumous title was changed to Zhaoci Shengxian.

sentences.zh: 后性節儉謙謹，有司月供千緡而止。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was by nature frugal and modest; the relevant offices supplied only one thousand strings of cash per month and no more.
translations.idiomatic: She was frugal and modest by nature, and the offices allotted her only a thousand strings of cash each month.

sentences.zh: 幸南昌，斥賣私絹三千匹充費。

translations.literal: When she visited Nanchang she sold off three thousand bolts of private silk to cover expenses.
translations.idiomatic: On her journey to Nanchang she sold three thousand bolts of her own silk to cover expenses.

sentences.zh: 尋詔文書應奏者避后父名，不許；

translations.literal: Soon an edict was issued that documents submitted to the throne should avoid her father's name, but she did not permit it;
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict ordered memorials to avoid her father's name, but she refused to allow it;

sentences.zh: 群臣請上太皇太后號，亦不許。

translations.literal: when the hundred officials requested that she be given the title Grand Empress Dowager, she again did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: and when the court asked to honor her as Grand Empress Dowager, she again refused.

sentences.zh: 忠厚直顯謨閣，台諫、給舍交章論列，后聞，即令易武，命學士院降詔，戒敕忠厚等不得預聞朝政、通貴近、至私第謁見宰執。

translations.literal: Zhonghou was promoted to the Zhimou Pavilion; censors and remonstrators together with drafting officials submitted memorials criticizing this in succession; when the empress dowager heard of it she at once had his rank changed to a military post and ordered the Academy of Scholars to issue an edict warning Zhonghou and others not to participate in court politics, consort with the powerful, or visit chief ministers at their private residences.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhonghou was promoted to the Zhimou Pavilion, censors and drafting officials protested in a stream of memorials; hearing of it, she immediately shifted him to a military post and had the Hanlin Academy issue an edict forbidding Zhonghou and his like from meddling in politics, cultivating the powerful, or calling on chief ministers at home.

sentences.zh: 以恩澤當得官者近八十員，后未嘗陳請。

translations.literal: Nearly eighty persons were due offices through imperial grace, yet the empress dowager never once petitioned on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly eighty relatives were entitled to offices through imperial favor, yet she never once petitioned for them.

sentences.zh: 初，后受冊日，宣仁太后歎曰：「斯人賢淑，惜福薄耳！

translations.literal: When she first received her investiture, Empress Dowager Xuanren sighed and said, "This person is virtuous and gentle, but her blessing is thin!
translations.idiomatic: When she was first invested, Empress Dowager Xuanren sighed and said, "This woman is virtuous and gentle, yet her allotted fortune is slight!

sentences.zh: 異日國有事變，必此人當之。」

translations.literal: When in the future the state has a crisis, it will surely fall to this woman to bear it."
translations.idiomatic: When the realm faces crisis hereafter, it will surely fall to her to bear it."

sentences.zh: 后皆如所云。

translations.literal: Everything afterward unfolded as she had said.
translations.idiomatic: Everything that followed proved her words true.

sentences.zh: 昭懷劉皇后

translations.literal: Empress Zhaohuai Liu
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhaohuai Liu

sentences.zh: 昭懷劉皇后，初為禦侍，明豔冠後庭，且多才藝。

translations.literal: Empress Zhaohuai Liu had begun as an imperial attendant; her beauty surpassed all in the rear court, and she was moreover skilled in many arts.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhaohuai Liu began as an imperial attendant; her beauty outshone every woman in the inner quarters, and she was accomplished in many arts.

sentences.zh: 由美人、婕妤進賢妃。

translations.literal: She advanced from Beautiful Lady and Brilliant Lady to Worthy Consort.
translations.idiomatic: She rose from Beautiful Lady and Brilliant Lady to Worthy Consort.

sentences.zh: 生一子二女。

translations.literal: She bore one son and two daughters.
translations.idiomatic: She bore one son and two daughters.

sentences.zh: 有盛寵，能順意奉兩宮。

translations.literal: She enjoyed great favor and could comply in serving both palaces.
translations.idiomatic: She enjoyed great favor and knew how to please both the empress and the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 時孟后位中宮，后不循列妾禮，且陰造奇語以售謗，內侍郝隨、劉友端為之用。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Meng held the central palace; Liu did not follow the ritual of a concubine in rank, and secretly fabricated strange tales to peddle slander, with eunuchs Hao Sui and Liu Youduan acting for her.
translations.idiomatic: While Empress Meng occupied the central palace, Liu refused the etiquette proper to a concubine and secretly invented bizarre stories to spread slander, aided by the eunuchs Hao Sui and Liu Youduan.

sentences.zh: 孟后既廢，后竟代焉。

translations.literal: After Empress Meng was deposed, Liu at last replaced her.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Meng was deposed, Liu finally took her place.

sentences.zh: 右正言鄒浩上疏極諫，坐竄。

translations.literal: Right Straight Remonstrator Zou Hao submitted a memorial strongly remonstrating and was banished for it.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Hao, a remonstrance official, submitted a fierce memorial of protest and was exiled for it.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，冊為元符皇后。

translations.literal: When Huizong took the throne she was installed as Yuanfu Empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong ascended the throne she was installed as Yuanfu Empress.

sentences.zh: 明年，尊為太后，名宮崇恩。

translations.literal: The next year she was honored as empress dowager, her palace named Chong'en.
translations.idiomatic: The following year she was honored as empress dowager, her residence named the Palace of Chong'en.

sentences.zh: 帝緣哲宗故，曲加恩禮，后以是頗干預外事，且以不謹聞。

translations.literal: Out of regard for Zhezong the emperor bent ritual favor toward her; she therefore often interfered in external affairs, and reports of impropriety reached the court.
translations.idiomatic: Out of regard for Zhezong the emperor showed her extraordinary favor, and she began to meddle in outside affairs until reports of misconduct reached him.

sentences.zh: 帝與輔臣議，將廢之，而后已為左右所逼，即簾鉤自縊而崩，年三十五。

translations.literal: The emperor discussed with his ministers plans to depose her, but she had already been driven by those around her to hang herself on the curtain hook and died at the age of thirty-five.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted his ministers about deposing her, but those around her had already pressed her to hang herself from a curtain hook; she died at thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 顯恭王皇后

translations.literal: Empress Xiangong Wang
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiangong Wang

sentences.zh: 徽宗顯恭王皇后，開封人，德州刺史藻之女也。

translations.literal: Empress Xiangong Wang of Huizong, a native of Kaifeng, was the daughter of Zao, prefect of Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiangong Wang of Emperor Huizong came from Kaifeng and was the daughter of Zao, prefect of Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 元符二年六月，歸於端邸，封順國夫人。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Yuanfu she married into the Heir Apparent's residence and was enfeoffed Lady of Shunguo.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of 1099 she entered the household of the Heir Apparent and was enfeoffed Lady of Shunguo.

sentences.zh: 徽宗即位，冊為皇后。

translations.literal: When Huizong took the throne she was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong ascended the throne she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 生欽宗及崇國公主。

translations.literal: She bore Qinzong and Princess Chongguo.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Emperor Qinzong and Princess Chongguo.

sentences.zh: 后性恭儉，鄭、王二妃方亢寵，后待之均平。

translations.literal: The empress was by nature respectful and frugal; when the Consorts Zheng and Wang were in full favor she treated them with equal fairness.
translations.idiomatic: She was respectful and frugal by nature; when Consorts Zheng and Wang were at the height of favor she treated them with impartial fairness.

sentences.zh: 巨閹妄意迎合，誣以暗昧。

translations.literal: A great eunuch presumptuously sought to curry favor and falsely accused her of illicit relations.
translations.idiomatic: A powerful eunuch tried to curry favor by falsely accusing her of secret misconduct.

sentences.zh: 帝命刑部侍郎周鼎即秘獄參驗，略無一跡，獄止。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Vice Minister of Justice Zhou Ding to investigate immediately in the secret prison; not a trace was found, and the case was closed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Vice Minister of Justice Zhou Ding to investigate at once in the secret prison; no evidence was found, and the case was dropped.

sentences.zh: 后見帝，未嘗一語輒及，帝幡然憐之。

translations.literal: When the empress saw the emperor she never once brought the matter up; the emperor suddenly felt pity for her.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever she met the emperor she never mentioned the accusation; struck with remorse, he pitied her.

sentences.zh: 大觀二年崩，年二十五。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daguan she died, aged twenty-five.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 1108, at the age of twenty-five.

sentences.zh: 諡曰靜和，葬裕陵之次。

translations.literal: Her posthumous title was Jinghe; she was buried beside Yuling.
translations.idiomatic: She was given the posthumous name Jinghe and interred next to Yuling, Emperor Huizong's mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 紹興中，始附徽宗廟室，改上今諡云。

translations.literal: In the Shaoxing era she was first enshrined in Huizong's temple hall, and the present posthumous title was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaoxing period she was first given a place in Huizong's ancestral shrine, when her present posthumous title was bestowed.

sentences.zh: 鄭皇后

translations.literal: Empress Zheng
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zheng

sentences.zh: 鄭皇后，開封人也。

translations.literal: Empress Zheng was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zheng came from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 父紳，始為直省官，以后貴，累封太師、樂平郡王。

translations.literal: Her father Shen was at first a direct secretariat official; through her elevation he was repeatedly enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor and Prince of Leping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Shen began as a direct secretariat official; once she rose in rank he was repeatedly promoted to Grand Preceptor and Prince of Leping.

sentences.zh: 后本欽聖殿押班，徽宗為端王，每日朝慈德宮，欽聖命鄭、王二押班供侍。

translations.literal: The empress had originally been a ward leader in the Qinsheng Hall. When Huizong was Prince of Duan he attended Cide Palace daily; Qinsheng ordered the two ward leaders Zheng and Wang to attend him.
translations.idiomatic: She had originally served as a ward leader in the Qinsheng Hall. While Huizong was still Prince of Duan he paid daily court at Cide Palace, and Empress Qinsheng assigned the ward leaders Zheng and Wang to wait on him.

sentences.zh: 及即位，遂以二人賜之。

translations.literal: When he took the throne he bestowed the two upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: After his accession he took both women into his own household as consorts.

sentences.zh: 后自入宮，好觀書，章奏能自製，帝愛其才。

translations.literal: From the time she entered the palace she loved reading; she could draft memorials herself, and the emperor valued her talent.
translations.idiomatic: Once she entered the palace she loved books and could compose memorials on her own; the emperor prized her ability.

sentences.zh: 崇甯初，封賢妃，迂貴妃有異寵。

translations.literal: Early in Chongning she was enfeoffed Virtuous Consort, then promoted to Noble Consort with special favor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chongning era she was made Virtuous Consort and soon advanced to Noble Consort, enjoying extraordinary favor.

sentences.zh: 徽宗多賚以詞章，天下歌之。

translations.literal: Huizong often bestowed literary compositions upon her, and the realm sang of it.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong frequently gifted her his own verse, and people throughout the empire celebrated the affair in song.

sentences.zh: 王皇后崩，政和元年，立為皇后。

translations.literal: When Empress Wang died, in the first year of Zhenghe she was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Wang died, she was made empress in the first year of the Zhenghe reign.

sentences.zh: 將受冊，有司創制冠服，后言國用未足，冠珠費多，請命工改制妃時舊冠。

translations.literal: As she was about to receive the investiture the relevant offices devised new cap and robes; the empress said state funds were insufficient and pearl ornaments for the cap were costly, and asked the artisans to refashion her old cap from her consort days.
translations.idiomatic: When she was about to be invested, the relevant offices designed new ceremonial dress. She said state funds were tight and the pearl ornaments for the cap were too costly, and asked artisans to refashion the old cap she had worn as consort.

sentences.zh: 又乞罷黃麾仗、小駕鹵簿等儀，從之。

translations.literal: She also asked to abolish the yellow guard escort, minor imperial procession equipage, and other such ceremonies, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: She also asked to dispense with the yellow guard escort, minor imperial procession, and similar ceremonies, and her request was granted.

sentences.zh: 恩澤皆弗陳請。

translations.literal: She never petitioned for favors.
translations.idiomatic: She never petitioned for favors for herself.

sentences.zh: 時族子居中在樞府，后奏：「外戚不當預國政，必欲用之，且令充妃職。」

translations.literal: At the time her clansman Juzhong was in the Bureau of Military Affairs; the empress memorialized: "Maternal kin ought not to take part in state affairs; if he must be used, let him serve only in a consort's office."
translations.idiomatic: Her clansman Juzhong then served in the Bureau of Military Affairs. She memorialized, "Maternal kin should not take part in state affairs; if he must be employed, let him serve only in a consort's office."

sentences.zh: 帝為罷居中。

translations.literal: The emperor removed Juzhong on her account.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor removed Juzhong from office at her request.

sentences.zh: 居中復用，后歸寧還言：「居中與父紳相往還，人皆言其招權市賄，乞禁絕，許御史奏劾。」

translations.literal: When Juzhong was again employed, after the empress returned from a visit home she said: "Juzhong and his father Shen associate with one another; everyone says they trade in power and bribes. I ask that this be forbidden and that censors be allowed to memorialize for impeachment."
