translations.idiomatic: When Juzhong was reappointed, the empress said after a visit home, "Juzhong and his father Shen keep company with one another, and everyone says they trade in power and bribes. I ask that this be forbidden and that censors be allowed to impeach them."

sentences.zh: 后性端謹，善順承帝意。

translations.literal: The empress was by nature proper and cautious and skilled at complying with the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Proper and cautious by nature, she was skilled at complying with the emperor's wishes.

sentences.zh: 劉貴妃薨，帝思之不已，將追冊為后。

translations.literal: When Imperial Consort Liu died the emperor thought of her unceasingly and was about to posthumously enregister her as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Imperial Consort Liu died the emperor could not stop thinking of her and intended to posthumously make her empress.

sentences.zh: 后即奏妃乃其養子，乞別議褒崇之禮，帝大喜。

translations.literal: The empress at once memorialized that the consort had been her adopted daughter and asked that a separate rite of praise and honor be discussed; the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The empress at once memorialized that the consort had been her adopted daughter and asked that a separate rite of honor be devised. The emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 欽宗受禪，尊為太上皇后，遷居甯德宮，稱甯德太后。

translations.literal: When Qinzong received the abdication she was honored as Grand Empress, moved to Ningde Palace, and styled Grand Empress Dowager of Ningde.
translations.idiomatic: When Qinzong accepted the throne she was elevated to Grand Empress, installed in Ningde Palace, and addressed as Grand Empress Dowager of Ningde.

sentences.zh: 從上皇幸南京，金師退，先歸。

translations.literal: She accompanied the Retired Emperor to Nanjing; when the Jin army withdrew she returned first.
translations.idiomatic: She followed the Retired Emperor to Nanjing and came back ahead of him once the Jin forces had pulled away.

sentences.zh: 時用事者言，上皇將復辟於鎮江，人情危駭。

translations.literal: At the time those in power said the Retired Emperor would restore his rule at Zhenjiang, and popular sentiment was alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Men then holding power claimed the Retired Emperor would reclaim the throne at Zhenjiang, and the people were thrown into fear.

sentences.zh: 或謂后將由端門直入禁中，內侍輩頗勸欽宗嚴備。

translations.literal: Some said the empress dowager would enter the Forbidden City straight through the Duanyang Gate; the eunuchs urged Qinzong to take strict precautions.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors held that she would march into the inner palace through the Duanyang Gate, and the palace eunuchs pressed Qinzong to mount a heavy guard.

sentences.zh: 帝不從，出郊迎后，於是兩宮歡甚洽。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen but went out of the city to welcome her; the Two Palaces were then on the most cordial terms.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to heed them and rode out to meet her in person, after which relations between the two courts grew warm and easy.

sentences.zh: 上皇聞之，即罷如洛之議。

translations.literal: When the Retired Emperor heard of it he immediately abandoned the plan to go to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of this, the Retired Emperor at once dropped the proposal to withdraw to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 汴京破，從上皇幸青城。

translations.literal: When Bianjing fell she accompanied the Retired Emperor to Qingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Bianjing she followed the Retired Emperor to Qingcheng.

sentences.zh: 北遷，留五年，崩于五國城，年五十二。

translations.literal: She was moved north, remained five years, and died at Wuguo Cheng, aged fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Carried into captivity in the north, she stayed five years and died at Wuguo Cheng at the age of fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 紹興七年，何蘇等使還，始知上皇及后崩，高宗大慟。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Shaoxing envoys He Su and others returned; only then was it learned that the Retired Emperor and the empress dowager had died; Gaozong was deeply grief-stricken.
translations.idiomatic: In 1137, when He Su and his fellow envoys came home, the court first learned that the Retired Emperor and the empress dowager were dead; Gaozong was overcome with grief.

sentences.zh: 詔立重成服，諡顯肅。

translations.literal: An edict ordered mourning garments to be established; her posthumous title was Xiansu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict set the full mourning observances and gave her the posthumous name Xiansu.

sentences.zh: 后親族各遷官有差。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's kin were each promoted in rank according to degree.
translations.idiomatic: Members of her clan were promoted in office, each according to his degree of kinship.

sentences.zh: 祔主徽宗室，以聞哀日為大忌。

translations.literal: She was enshrined in Huizong's spirit tablet hall; the day the mourning was announced became the great anniversary of death.
translations.idiomatic: Her spirit tablet was placed in Huizong's shrine, and the day the mourning news arrived was observed as the principal death anniversary.

sentences.zh: 梓宮歸，入境，承之以槨，納翬衣其中，與徽宗各攢於會稽永佑陵。

translations.literal: When the coffin returned and entered the realm it was borne on an outer coffin with feather-patterned robes placed within; she and Huizong were each entombed at Yongyou Mausoleum in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: When her remains were brought back into Song territory they were laid in an outer coffin with her feathered court robes inside, and she and Huizong were separately interred at Yongyou Mausoleum in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 先是，后至金營，訴於粘罕曰：「妾得罪當行，但妾家屬不預朝政，乞留不遣。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when the empress reached the Jin camp she pleaded to Nianhan: "This humble one has offended and must go, but my family members do not participate in court affairs; I beg they be left and not sent away."
translations.idiomatic: Before this, upon reaching the Jin camp she appealed to Nianhan: "I have offended and must go, but my relatives never took part in government; please let them stay and not be sent away."

sentences.zh: 粘罕許之，故紳得歸。

translations.literal: Nianhan agreed, and therefore Shen was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Nianhan consented, and so Shen was allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 后既行，紳亦以是年薨，諡僖靖。

translations.literal: After the empress departed, Shen also died that year; his posthumous title was Xijing.
translations.idiomatic: Once she had gone north, Shen died the same year and was posthumously titled Xijing.

sentences.zh: 家屬流寓江南，高宗憐之，詔所在尋訪賜官。

translations.literal: The family wandered in exile in Jiangnan; Gaozong pitied them and ordered officials everywhere to seek them out and grant offices.
translations.idiomatic: Her kin were scattered in exile across the south; Gaozong took pity on them and ordered local authorities to find them and award offices.

sentences.zh: 有鄭藻者，后近屬也。

translations.literal: There was one Zheng Zao, a close relation of the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Among them was Zheng Zao, a near kinsman of the empress.

sentences.zh: 紹興中帶禦器械用后祔廟恩，拜隴州防禦使；

translations.literal: In Shaoxing, while serving as Palace Armorer, he used the grace of her enshrinement and was appointed Defender of Longzhou;
translations.idiomatic: During Shaoxing, as a Palace Armorer he benefited from the favor granted when she entered the ancestral shrine and was made Defender of Longzhou;

sentences.zh: 凡四使金，曆官至保信軍節度使，加太尉。

translations.literal: in all he went four times as envoy to the Jin, rose to Military Commissioner of the Baoxin Army, and was added Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: he served four missions to the Jin in all, rose to military commissioner of the Baoxin army, and was named Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 卒，追封榮國公，諡端靖。

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Rong with posthumous title Duanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously created Duke of Rong and given the posthumous name Duanjing.

sentences.zh: 王貴妃，與鄭后俱為押班。

translations.literal: Imperial Noble Consort Wang, together with Empress Zheng, served as lead attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Noble Consort Wang served as a lead attendant together with Empress Zheng.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，封平昌郡君，進位至貴妃。

translations.literal: When Huizong was enthroned she was enfeoffed Lady of Pingchang Commandery and advanced to Imperial Noble Consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong took the throne she was created Lady of Pingchang Commandery and rose to Imperial Noble Consort.

sentences.zh: 生鄆王楷、莘王植、陳王機、惠淑康淑順德柔福沖懿帝姬。

translations.literal: She bore the Prince of Yun, Kai; the Prince of Shen, Zhi; the Prince of Chen, Ji; and the Imperial Princesses Huishu, Kangshu, Shunde, Roufu, and Chongyi.
translations.idiomatic: She bore the Princes of Yun, Shen, and Chen—Kai, Zhi, and Ji—and the princesses Huishu, Kangshu, Shunde, Roufu, and Chongyi.

sentences.zh: 九月薨，諡曰懿肅。

translations.literal: In the ninth month she died; her posthumous title was Yisu.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the ninth month and received the posthumous title Yisu.

sentences.zh: 韋賢妃，開封人，高宗母也。

translations.literal: Virtuous Consort Wei, a native of Kaifeng, was Gaozong's mother.
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous Consort Wei of Kaifeng was the mother of Emperor Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 初入宮，為侍禦。

translations.literal: When she first entered the palace she was a palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On entering the palace she began as a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 崇甯末，封平昌郡君。

translations.literal: Late in Chongning she was enfeoffed Lady of Pingchang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Chongning era she was created Lady of Pingchang.

sentences.zh: 大觀初，進婕妤，累遷婉容。

translations.literal: Early in Daguan she was promoted to Shining Beauty and cumulatively to Graceful Countenance.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Daguan reign she was raised to Shining Beauty and later advanced step by step to Graceful Countenance.

sentences.zh: 高宗在康邸出使，進封龍德宮賢妃。

translations.literal: When Gaozong was at the Prince of Kang's establishment on a mission he advanced her to Virtuous Consort of Longde Palace.
translations.idiomatic: While Gaozong was still at the Prince of Kang's residence on an imperial mission, she was promoted to Virtuous Consort of Longde Palace.

sentences.zh: 從上皇北遷。

translations.literal: She accompanied the Retired Emperor north.
translations.idiomatic: She followed the Retired Emperor into captivity in the north.

sentences.zh: 建炎改元，遙尊為宣和皇后。

translations.literal: When the Jianyan era began she was honored from afar as Empress Xuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: With the proclamation of the Jianyan era she was honored from afar as Empress Xuanhe.

sentences.zh: 封其父安道為郡王，官親屬三十人。

translations.literal: Her father Andao was enfeoffed Prince of a commandery; thirty kinsmen were given offices.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Andao was created a prince of a commandery, and thirty relatives were granted posts.

sentences.zh: 由是遣使不絕。

translations.literal: From this envoys were sent without cease.
translations.idiomatic: After that the court dispatched envoys in an unbroken stream.

sentences.zh: 紹興七年，徽宗及鄭皇后崩聞至，帝號慟，諭輔臣曰：「宣和皇后春秋高，朕思之不遑甯處，屈己請和，正為此耳。」

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Shaoxing news of the deaths of Huizong and Empress Zheng arrived; the emperor wailed and told his chief ministers: "Empress Xuanhe is advanced in years; I think of her without peace; humbling myself to sue for peace is precisely for this."
translations.idiomatic: In 1137, when word came that Huizong and Empress Zheng had died, the emperor cried aloud and told his ministers: "Empress Xuanhe is old; I cannot rest for thinking of her, and it is chiefly for her sake that I have stooped to seek peace."

sentences.zh: 翰林學士朱震引唐建中故事，請遙尊為皇太后，從之。

translations.literal: Academician Zhu Zhen cited the Jianzhong precedent of Tang and requested distant elevation to empress dowager; it was followed.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academician Zhu Zhen cited the Tang precedent of the Jianzhong era and asked that she be honored from afar as empress dowager, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 已而太常少卿吳表臣請依嘉祐、治平故事，俟三年喪畢，然後舉行。

translations.literal: Then Vice Minister of Rites Wu Biaochen requested following the Jiayou and Zhiping precedents, waiting until the three-year mourning was complete before carrying it out.
translations.idiomatic: Later Vice Minister of Rites Wu Biaochen urged that, following the Jiayou and Zhiping models, the ceremony wait until the three-year mourning had ended.

sentences.zh: 乃先降禦劄，播告天下。

translations.literal: Thereupon an imperial letter was first issued and proclaimed to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial rescript was therefore issued at once and announced throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 后三代俱追封王。

translations.literal: Three generations of the empress dowager's forebears were all posthumously enfeoffed as princes.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations of her ancestors were posthumously created princes.

sentences.zh: 帝以后久未歸，每顰蹙曰：「金人若從朕請，餘皆非所問也。」

translations.literal: Because the empress dowager had long not returned, the emperor would knit his brows and say: "If the Jin would grant my request, I would ask nothing else."
translations.idiomatic: As she still had not come home, the emperor would frown and say: "If the Jin would do this one thing for me, I would want nothing more."

sentences.zh: 王倫使回，言金人許歸后。

translations.literal: Envoy Wang Lun returned saying the Jin agreed to return the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lun returned from his mission he reported that the Jin had promised to send the empress dowager back.

sentences.zh: 未幾，金人遣蕭哲來，亦言后將歸狀。

translations.literal: Before long the Jin sent Xiao Zhe, who also spoke of the empress dowager's impending return.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Jin dispatched Xiao Zhe, who likewise said she would be returning.

sentences.zh: 遂豫作慈甯宮，命莫將、韓恕為奉迎使。

translations.literal: Thereupon Cining Palace was prepared in advance; Mo Jiang and Han Shu were appointed welcome envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Cining Palace was therefore readied ahead of time, and Mo Jiang and Han Shu were named reception envoys.

sentences.zh: 十年，以金人猶未歸后，乃遙上皇太后冊寶于慈寧殿。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, because the Jin still had not returned the empress dowager, the empress dowager's seals and regalia were remotely presented at Cining Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In 1140, since the Jin had still not released her, the empress dowager's seal and regalia were ceremonially offered from afar in Cining Hall.

sentences.zh: 是後，生辰、至、朔，皆遙行賀禮。

translations.literal: After this, birthdays, solstices, and the first of each month all had congratulatory rites performed from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter her birthday, the solstices, and the first day of each month were all celebrated with distant congratulatory ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 洪皓在燕，求得后書，遣李微持歸。

translations.literal: Hong Hao in Yan obtained a letter from the empress dowager and sent Li Wei to bring it back.
translations.idiomatic: While detained in Yan, Hong Hao secured a letter from her and sent Li Wei to carry it home.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜曰：「遣使百輩，不如一書。」

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and said: "A hundred envoys are not equal to one letter."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejoiced and said: "A hundred embassies are worth less than a single letter."

sentences.zh: 遂加微官。

translations.literal: Li Wei was thereupon promoted in office.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wei was promptly rewarded with a promotion.

sentences.zh: 金人遣蕭毅、邢具瞻來議和，帝曰：「朕有天下，而養不及親。

translations.literal: The Jin sent Xiao Yi and Xing Juzhan to negotiate peace; the emperor said: "I possess the realm yet cannot support my parent.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin dispatched Xiao Yi and Xing Juzhan to discuss peace; the emperor said: "I hold the empire but cannot care for my mother.

sentences.zh: 徽宗無及矣！

translations.literal: It is too late for Huizong!
translations.idiomatic: Nothing can be done for Huizong now!

sentences.zh: 今立誓信，當明言歸我太后，朕不恥和，不然，朕不憚用兵。」

translations.literal: Now in establishing sworn faith it must be clearly stated to return my empress dowager; I am not ashamed to make peace—otherwise I do not fear using troops."
translations.idiomatic: In making this sworn pact you must plainly promise to return my empress dowager; I am not ashamed to sue for peace, but otherwise I will not shrink from war."

sentences.zh: 毅等還，帝又語之曰：「太后果還，自當謹守誓約；

translations.literal: When Yi and the others returned the emperor again told them: "If the empress dowager indeed returns I shall strictly keep the oath;
translations.idiomatic: When Yi and his party came back the emperor told them again: "If the empress dowager truly returns, I will faithfully uphold the treaty;

sentences.zh: 如其未也，雖有誓約，徒為虛文。」

translations.literal: if she has not, though there be an oath it is empty words alone."
translations.idiomatic: if she does not, then whatever oaths we write will be nothing but empty paper."

sentences.zh: 命何鑄、曹勳報謝，召至內殿，諭之曰：「朕北望庭闈，無淚可揮。

translations.literal: He appointed He Zhu and Cao Xun to return thanks; summoning them to the inner hall he instructed: "I look north toward the parental court—no tears left to shed.
translations.idiomatic: He sent He Zhu and Cao Xun back with his thanks, called them into the inner hall, and said: "I gaze north toward my parents and have no tears left to shed.

sentences.zh: 卿見金主，當曰：'慈親之在上國，一老人耳；

translations.literal: When you see the Jin ruler you should say: 'My kindly parent in your realm is but an old person;
translations.idiomatic: When you see the Jin emperor tell him this: 'My dear mother in your land is only an old woman;

sentences.zh: 在本國，則所系甚重。

translations.literal: in our realm what is involved is very weighty.
translations.idiomatic: in our country she means everything to the throne.

sentences.zh: '以至誠說之，庶彼有感動。」

translations.literal: Speak with utmost sincerity that perhaps they may be moved.'"
translations.idiomatic: Plead with all your heart, so that perhaps they will be moved.'"

sentences.zh: 鑄等至金國，首以后歸為請。

translations.literal: He Zhu and the others reached the Jin state and first requested the empress dowager's return.
translations.idiomatic: When He Zhu and his colleagues arrived in Jin territory their first demand was her release.

sentences.zh: 金主曰：「先朝業已如此，豈可輒改？」

translations.literal: The Jin ruler said: "The prior dynasty's affair is already thus—how can it be abruptly changed?"
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor replied: "What the previous dynasty decided is already settled—how can it be changed at will?"

sentences.zh: 勳再三懇請，金主始允。

translations.literal: Cao Xun repeatedly pleaded; the Jin ruler finally consented.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xun pressed the point again and again until the Jin ruler at last agreed.

sentences.zh: 鑄等就館，館伴耶律紹文來信，金主許從所請。

translations.literal: He Zhu and the others were at the hostel when the escort Yelü Shaowen sent word that the Jin ruler agreed to the request.
translations.idiomatic: While He Zhu and his party were lodged there, their Jin host Yelü Shaowen sent word that the emperor had granted the request.

sentences.zh: 洪皓聞之，先遣人來報。

translations.literal: Hong Hao heard and first sent someone to report.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Hao learned of it and dispatched a messenger ahead with the news.

sentences.zh: 鑄等還，具言其實。

translations.literal: He Zhu and the others returned and reported in full.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhu and his colleagues returned and gave a full account.

sentences.zh: 遂命參政王次翁為奉迎使。

translations.literal: Wang Ciweng, Vice Grand Councilor, was thereupon appointed welcome envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Grand Councilor Wang Ciweng was then named chief reception envoy.

sentences.zh: 金人遣其臣高居安、完顏宗賢等扈從以行。

translations.literal: The Jin sent their ministers Gao Ju'an, Wanyan Zongxian, and others to escort her on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin dispatched Gao Ju'an, Wanyan Zongxian, and other officials to escort her on the road.

sentences.zh: 十二年四月，次燕山，自東平舟行，由清河至楚州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, fourth month, they stopped at Yanshan, traveled by boat from Dongping along the Qing River to Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of 1142 they halted at Yanshan, then went by boat from Dongping down the Qing River to Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 既渡淮，命太后弟安樂郡王韋淵、秦魯國大長公主、吳國長公主迎于道。

translations.literal: Having crossed the Huai, he ordered the empress dowager's younger brother Prince of Anle Wei Yuan, the Grand Princess of Qin and Lu, and the Princess of Wu to welcome her on the road.
translations.idiomatic: After she crossed the Huai, he sent her younger brother, Prince of Anle Wei Yuan, together with the Grand Princess of Qin and Lu and the Princess of Wu, to meet her along the route.

sentences.zh: 帝親至臨平奉迎，普安郡王、宰執、兩省、三衙管軍皆從。

translations.literal: The emperor personally went to Linping to welcome her; the Prince of Pu'an, the grand councilors, both secretariats, and the military commanders of the Three Offices all followed.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong himself went to Linping to receive her, accompanied by the Prince of Pu'an, the chief ministers, both palace secretariats, and the commanders of the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 帝初見太后，喜極而泣。

translations.literal: At his first sight of the empress dowager the emperor wept for joy.
translations.idiomatic: When he first saw her again he wept with joy.

sentences.zh: 八月，至臨安，入居慈甯宮。

translations.literal: In the eighth month they reached Lin'an and she entered Cining Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month she arrived at Lin'an and took up residence in Cining Palace.

sentences.zh: 先是，以梓宮未還，詔中外輟樂。

translations.literal: Earlier, because the coffins had not returned, an edict ordered music stopped inside and outside the court.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, while the imperial coffins were still abroad, an edict had suspended music throughout the court and the realm.

sentences.zh: 至是，慶太后壽節，始用樂。

translations.literal: At this time, celebrating the empress dowager's birthday, music was first used.
translations.idiomatic: Now, to mark her birthday, music was played for the first time.

sentences.zh: 謁家廟，親屬遷官幾二千人。

translations.literal: She visited the family temple; kin promoted in rank numbered nearly two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: She worshiped at the imperial ancestral temple, and close to two thousand of her relatives were promoted in rank.

sentences.zh: 太后聰明有智慮。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was intelligent and had foresight.
translations.idiomatic: She was clever and far-sighted.

sentences.zh: 初，金人許還三梓宮，太后恐其反覆，呼役者畢集，然后起攢。

translations.literal: Initially, when the Jin promised to return the three coffins, the empress dowager feared they would change their minds; she called all laborers together, then only began the entombment.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin first agreed to send back the three coffins she feared they might go back on their word, so she gathered every worker on the spot before allowing the remains to be coffined.

sentences.zh: 時方暑，金人憚行，太后慮有他變，乃陽稱疾，須秋涼進發。

translations.literal: It was then midsummer; the Jin feared travel; the empress dowager feared other changes and feigned illness, saying departure must wait for autumn cool.
translations.idiomatic: The season was hot and the Jin escorts were reluctant to march; suspecting further trouble, she pretended to be ill and insisted they wait until the weather turned cool.

sentences.zh: 已而稱貸于金使，得黃金三千兩以犒其眾，由是途中無間言。

translations.literal: Then she claimed to borrow from the Jin envoy and obtained three thousand taels of gold to reward their troops; thus on the road there was no dissent.
translations.idiomatic: She then borrowed three thousand taels of gold from the Jin envoys to reward their men, and so the journey passed without a murmur of complaint.

sentences.zh: 太后在北方，聞韓世忠名，次臨平，呼世忠至簾前慰勞。

translations.literal: While in the north the empress dowager had heard Han Shizhong's name; stopping at Linping she called Shizhong before the curtain to comfort and reward him.
translations.idiomatic: In captivity she had heard of Han Shizhong; when the procession paused at Linping she summoned him before her screen to praise and comfort him.

sentences.zh: 還宮，帝侍太后，或至夜分未去，太后曰：「且休矣，聽朝宜早，恐妨萬幾。」

translations.literal: Back at the palace the emperor attended the empress dowager, sometimes not leaving until midnight; she said: "Rest now; court audience should be early—lest it hinder the myriad affairs of state."
translations.idiomatic: After her return the emperor waited on her, sometimes staying until deep into the night; she would say: "That is enough—attend court early tomorrow, lest the myriad affairs of state suffer."

sentences.zh: 又嘗謂：「兩宮給使，宜令通用；

translations.literal: She also once said: "The Two Palaces' attendants should be made interchangeable;
translations.idiomatic: She also remarked: "The servants of the two palaces ought to serve both alike;

sentences.zh: 不然，則有彼我之分，而佞人間言易以入也。」

translations.literal: otherwise there will be a distinction of theirs and ours, and flatterers' divisive talk will easily enter."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise you create a yours-and-mine divide, and sycophants will find it easy to sow trouble between you."

sentences.zh: 時皇后未立，太后屢為帝言，帝請降手書，太后曰：「我但知家事，外庭非所當預。」

translations.literal: The empress had not yet been installed; the empress dowager repeatedly spoke to the emperor about it; he requested a lowered hand edict; she said: "I only know household affairs—the outer court is not for me to intervene in."
translations.idiomatic: The empress had still not been appointed, and the empress dowager often raised the matter with the emperor; he asked her to issue a personal edict, but she replied: "I understand only family matters; the outer court is no concern of mine."

sentences.zh: 將行冊命，承平典禮，悉能記之。

translations.literal: When the investiture was to be performed, the peaceful-era rituals—she could recall them all.
translations.idiomatic: When the installation rites were prepared, she remembered every detail of the ceremonies from the peaceful years.

sentences.zh: 帝先意承志，惟恐不及，或一食稍減，輒不勝憂懼。

translations.literal: The emperor anticipated her wishes and feared falling short; if one meal was slightly less he could not bear the worry.
translations.idiomatic: He tried to read her mind and dreaded disappointing her; if she ate even a little less at one meal he was overcome with anxiety.

sentences.zh: 常戒宮人曰：「太后年已六十，惟優遊無事，起居適意，即壽考康寧；

translations.literal: He often admonished palace women: "The empress dowager is already sixty; only idle ease without affairs, comfort in daily life—that is longevity and peace;
translations.idiomatic: He often warned the palace women: "The empress dowager is already sixty; let her wander at leisure with nothing to trouble her, and keep her daily life comfortable—that is how she will live long and well;

sentences.zh: 事有所闕，懼母令太后知，第來白朕。」

translations.literal: if something is lacking, fearing Mother might let the empress dowager know—just come tell me."
translations.idiomatic: if anything goes wrong, do not let Mother hear of it and worry her—report to me first."

sentences.zh: 十九年，太后年七十，正月朔，即宮中行慶壽禮，親屬各遷官一等。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the empress dowager was seventy; on the first day of the first month the longevity celebration was held in the palace; kin were each promoted one grade.
translations.idiomatic: In 1149, when she turned seventy, a birthday celebration was held in the palace on the first day of the first month, and every relative was promoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 太后微恙，累月不出殿門，會牡丹盛開，帝入白，太后欣然步至花所，因留宴，竟日盡歡。

translations.literal: The empress dowager had a slight illness and for many months did not leave the hall; peonies bloomed in profusion; the emperor entered to report; she gladly walked to the flowers and stayed for a banquet, enjoying the whole day.
translations.idiomatic: She had been mildly unwell and had not stepped outside her hall for months; when the peonies came into full bloom the emperor came in to tell her, and she happily walked out to the flowers, stayed for a feast, and rejoiced the whole day long.

sentences.zh: 忌日，以諭宰執。

translations.literal: On death anniversaries she used the occasion to instruct the grand councilors.
translations.idiomatic: On days of mourning commemoration she took the opportunity to admonish the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 后苦目疾，募得醫皇甫坦，治即愈。

translations.literal: The empress dowager suffered from eye disease; a physician Huangfu Tan was recruited; after treatment she was quickly cured.
translations.idiomatic: She was troubled by an eye ailment; a doctor named Huangfu Tan was found, and once he treated her she recovered at once.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，太后壽登八十，復行慶禮。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year the empress dowager's longevity reached eighty; the celebration rites were performed again.
translations.idiomatic: In 1159, when she turned eighty, the court again held longevity celebration ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 親屬進官一等；

translations.literal: Relatives were promoted one office grade;
translations.idiomatic: Her relatives were each promoted one rank in office;

sentences.zh: 庶人等九十、宗子女若貢士已上父母年八十者，悉官封之。

translations.literal: commoners aged ninety, and children of the imperial clan or offspring whose parents held Presented Scholar rank or above and were eighty—all were granted office titles and seals.
translations.idiomatic: all commoners aged ninety, and all offspring of the imperial clan or of Presented Scholars and above whose parents had reached eighty, were granted official titles and honorary seals.

sentences.zh: 九月，得疾，上不視朝，敕輔臣祈禱天地、宗廟、社稷，赦天下，減租稅。

translations.literal: In the ninth month she fell ill; the emperor suspended court; he ordered chief ministers to pray to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple, and the altars of soil and grain; he proclaimed a general amnesty and reduced rents and taxes.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month she took ill; the emperor ceased holding court and ordered his chief ministers to pray at the temples of Heaven, Earth, the imperial ancestors, and the state altars; he declared an empire-wide amnesty and cut rents and taxes.

sentences.zh: 俄崩于慈甯宮，諡曰顯仁。

translations.literal: Soon she died at Cining Palace; her posthumous title was Xianren.
translations.idiomatic: Before long she died in Cining Palace and was given the posthumous epithet Xianren.

sentences.zh: 攢於永佑陵之西，祔神主太廟徽宗室。

translations.literal: She was buried west of Yongyou Mausoleum; her spirit tablet was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple in Emperor Huizong's shrine.
translations.idiomatic: She was interred west of Yongyou Mausoleum, and her spirit tablet was placed in Huizong's shrine in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 親屬進秩者十四人，授官者三人。

translations.literal: Fourteen relatives received advancement in rank; three were granted office.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen of her kin were advanced in rank and three were appointed to office.

sentences.zh: 太后性節儉，有司進金唾壺，太后易，令用塗金。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was frugal by nature; when the offices presented a gold spittoon, she had it exchanged and ordered gilt to be used instead.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was naturally thrifty: when officials offered her a solid gold spittoon, she had it swapped for a gilded one.

sentences.zh: 宮中賜予不過三數千，所得供進財帛，多積於庫。

translations.literal: Palace grants did not exceed a few thousand; tribute wealth and silks she received were largely stored in the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Her gifts within the palace rarely exceeded a few thousand cash, and most of the valuables and silks presented to her were hoarded in the storehouses.

sentences.zh: 至是，喪葬之費，皆仰給焉。

translations.literal: By this time the expenses of her funeral all drew upon these accumulations.
translations.idiomatic: When she died, the entire cost of her funeral was met from those savings.

sentences.zh: 然好佛、老。

translations.literal: Yet she was fond of Buddhism and Daoism.
translations.idiomatic: Yet she was devoted to Buddhism and Daoism.

sentences.zh: 初，高宗出使，有小妾言，見四金甲人執刀劍以衛。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gaozong went on embassy, a minor concubine said she saw four men in golden armor holding swords and blades to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, when Gaozong was sent on a diplomatic mission, a concubine of his reported seeing four warriors in golden armor bearing swords to protect him.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「我祠四聖謹甚，必其陰助。」

translations.literal: The empress dowager said: "I worship the Four Sages with great care—they must be helping him in secret."
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "I worship the Four Sages most devoutly; they must be aiding him from afar."

sentences.zh: 既北遷，常設祭；

translations.literal: After the move north she regularly set out offerings;
translations.idiomatic: After the court fled north she continued to hold sacrifices for them;

sentences.zh: 及歸，立祠西湖上。

translations.literal: and after the return she established a shrine on West Lake.
translations.idiomatic: and once they returned south she built a shrine for them on West Lake.

sentences.zh: 喬貴妃

translations.literal: Worthy Consort Qiao
translations.idiomatic: Worthy Consort Qiao

sentences.zh: 喬貴妃，初與高宗母韋妃俱侍鄭皇后，結為姊妹，約先貴者毋相忘。

translations.literal: Worthy Consort Qiao had at first attended Empress Zheng together with Gaozong's mother Lady Wei; they became sworn sisters and promised that whoever rose first would not forget the other.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy Consort Qiao had first served Empress Zheng alongside Gaozong's mother, Lady Wei; the two became sworn sisters and agreed that whichever of them won favor first would not forget the other.

sentences.zh: 既而貴妃得幸徽宗，遂引韋氏，二人愈相得。

translations.literal: Later the consort won Emperor Huizong's favor and thus introduced the Wei clan; the two became still closer.
translations.idiomatic: When the consort later won Huizong's favor she brought Lady Wei to court, and the bond between the two women grew still stronger.

sentences.zh: 二帝北遷，貴妃與韋氏俱。

translations.literal: When the two emperors were taken north, the consort and Lady Wei went together.
translations.idiomatic: When the two captive emperors were marched north, the consort and Lady Wei shared the ordeal.

sentences.zh: 至是，韋妃將還，貴妃以金五十兩贈高居安，曰：「薄物不足為禮，願好護送姊還江南。」

translations.literal: At this time Lady Wei was about to return; the consort gave Gao Ju'an fifty taels of gold, saying: "This trifle is unworthy as a gift—see that you escort my elder sister safely back to the south."
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Wei was finally to be sent home, the consort gave Gao Ju'an fifty taels of gold, saying, "This is a poor token, but see that you escort my elder sister safely back to Jiangnan."

sentences.zh: 復舉酒酌韋氏曰：「姊善重保護，歸即為皇太后；

translations.literal: She again raised a cup to Lady Wei and said: "Sister, take good care of yourself on the road home—you will at once become empress dowager;
translations.idiomatic: She raised another cup to Lady Wei and said, "Sister, guard your health on the journey; once you are home you will be empress dowager at once;

sentences.zh: 妹無還期，終死於朔漠矣！」

translations.literal: for me there is no hope of return—I shall end my days in the northern deserts!"
translations.idiomatic: but I shall never return and will die in the northern wastes!"

sentences.zh: 遂大慟以別。

translations.literal: She then wailed greatly and they parted.
translations.idiomatic: They then took leave of one another amid loud lamentation.

sentences.zh: 劉貴妃

translations.literal: Imperial Consort Liu
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Consort Liu

sentences.zh: 劉貴妃，其出單微。

translations.literal: Imperial Consort Liu came from a very humble family.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Consort Liu came from a family of the lowest standing.

sentences.zh: 入宮，即大幸，由才人七遷至貴妃。

translations.literal: Upon entering the palace she at once enjoyed great favor, rising through seven ranks from Talented Lady to Imperial Consort.
translations.idiomatic: No sooner had she entered the palace than she won extraordinary favor, advancing through seven ranks from Talented Lady to Imperial Consort.

sentences.zh: 生濟陽郡王棫、祁王模、信王榛。

translations.literal: She bore the Prince of Jiyang County, Shu; the Prince of Qi, Mo; and the Prince of Xin, Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: She bore the Princes of Jiyang, Qi, and Xin—Shu, Mo, and Zhen.

sentences.zh: 政和三年秋，薨。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year of Zhenghe she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the autumn of 1113, the third year of the Zhenghe reign.

sentences.zh: 先是，妃手植芭蕉於庭曰：「是物長，吾不及見矣！」

translations.literal: Beforehand the consort had planted plantains in the courtyard, saying: "When this plant grows tall I shall no longer be here to see it!"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier she had planted a banana tree in the courtyard, saying, "By the time this grows tall I shall no longer be alive to see it!"

sentences.zh: 已而果然。

translations.literal: Before long it proved so.
translations.idiomatic: Events unfolded exactly as she had foretold.

sentences.zh: 左右奔千告帝，帝初以其微疾，不經意，趣幸之，已薨矣，始大悲惻。

translations.literal: Attendants ran in thousands to tell the emperor; at first he paid no heed, thinking it a minor illness, and hurried to visit her—but she was already dead; only then was he overcome with deep grief.
translations.idiomatic: Servants rushed to tell the emperor, but he at first treated it as a passing ailment and hurried to her side only to find her already dead; then he was stricken with the deepest grief.

sentences.zh: 特加緊四字諡曰明達懿文。

translations.literal: She was specially granted the tight four-character posthumous title Mingda Yiwen.
translations.idiomatic: She was uniquely honored with the four-character posthumous name Mingda Yiwen.

sentences.zh: 敘其平生，弦諸樂府。

translations.literal: Her life's story was set to music in the Music Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Her life story was versified and entered into the palace repertoire.

sentences.zh: 又欲踵溫成故事追崇，使皇后表請，因冊贈為后，而以明達諡焉。

translations.literal: He also wished to follow the precedent of Worthy Consort Wen Cheng and exalt her posthumously, having the empress submit a memorial requesting it; thus she was enfeoffed as empress with the posthumous designation Mingda.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong also wished to follow the precedent of Worthy Consort Wen Cheng and elevate her posthumously, so he had the empress petition on his behalf; she was then canonized as empress under the posthumous name Mingda.

sentences.zh: 時又有安妃劉氏者，本酒保家女。

translations.literal: At this time there was also Worthy Consort An, Lady Liu, who was originally the daughter of a wine-shop keeper.
translations.idiomatic: About the same time there was also Worthy Consort An, née Liu, originally the daughter of a tavern keeper.

sentences.zh: 初事崇轉宮，宮罷，出居宦者何聽家。

translations.literal: She first served at Chongzhuan Palace; when the palace was abolished she went out to live at the eunuch He Ting's household.
translations.idiomatic: She had first served in Chongzhuan Palace; when that establishment was shut she lived with the eunuch He Ting.

sentences.zh: 內侍楊戩譽其美，復召入。

translations.literal: The inner attendant Yang Zhan praised her beauty and she was summoned back in.
translations.idiomatic: The palace eunuch Yang Zhan commended her beauty and she was recalled.

sentences.zh: 妃以同姓養為女，遂有寵，為才人，進至淑妃。

translations.literal: The consort adopted her as a daughter because they shared a surname; she thereby won favor, became a Talented Lady, and advanced to Shuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Consort Liu adopted her as a daughter on account of their common surname; she thus gained favor, rose to Talented Lady, and was promoted to Shuyi.

sentences.zh: 生建安郡王楧、嘉國公椅、英國公楒、和福帝姬。

translations.literal: She bore the Prince of Jian'an, Chuan; the Duke of Jia, Yi; the Duke of Ying, Si; and the Imperial Princess Hefu.
translations.idiomatic: She bore the Prince of Jian'an, Chuan; the Duke of Jia, Yi; the Duke of Ying, Si; and Princess Hefu.

sentences.zh: 政和四年，加貴妃。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenghe she was elevated to Imperial Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In 1114 she was raised to Imperial Consort.

sentences.zh: 朝夕得侍上，擅愛顓席，嬪禦為之稀進。

translations.literal: Morning and evening she attended the emperor; she monopolized his pillow and rare was the day other consorts gained access.
translations.idiomatic: She attended the emperor day and night, kept his company to herself, and the other palace women rarely saw him.

sentences.zh: 擢其父劉宗元節度使。

translations.literal: Her father Liu Zongyuan was promoted to military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Liu Zongyuan was made a military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 妃天資警司，解迎意合旨，雅善塗飾，每制一服，外間即傚之。

translations.literal: The consort was by nature alert and clever, understood how to meet intent and accord with the emperor's wishes, and was skilled at adornment; whenever she devised a garment the outer world at once imitated it.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and quick by nature, she knew how to read the emperor's wishes and was skilled at adornment; whenever she designed a garment the world outside the palace copied it at once.

sentences.zh: 林靈素以技進，目為九華玉真安妃，省其像於神霄帝君之左。

translations.literal: Lin Lingsu advanced through his arts and styled her the Worthy Consort of Nine Splendors and Jade Truth; her image was placed to the left of the Sovereign Lord of the Divine Empyrean.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Lingsu rose through his arts and called her the Worthy Consort of Nine Splendors and Jade Truth; her image was placed to the left of the Sovereign Lord of the Divine Empyrean.

sentences.zh: 薨，年三十四。

translations.literal: She died, aged thirty-four.
translations.idiomatic: She died at the age of thirty-four.

sentences.zh: 初諡明節和文，旋用明達近比，加冊贈為皇后，葬其園之北隅。

translations.literal: At first her posthumous title was Mingjie Hewen; soon the near parallel Mingda was used, and she was enregistered and posthumously made empress and buried in the north corner of her garden.
translations.idiomatic: Her initial posthumous title was Mingjie Hewen; soon the comparable title Mingda was used, and she was canonized as empress and buried in the north corner of her garden.

sentences.zh: 帝悼之甚，後宮皆往唁，帝相與啜泣。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned her deeply; all the inner palaces went to condole, and the emperor wept with them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned her deeply. Women of the inner palace all came to condole, and the emperor wept with them.

sentences.zh: 崔妃獨左視無戚容，帝悲怒，疑其為厭蠱。

translations.literal: Consort Cui alone looked askance without a grieving countenance; the emperor was grieved and angry and suspected witchcraft.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Cui alone looked away without a grieving expression. The emperor was grieved and angry and suspected sorcery.

sentences.zh: 卜者劉康孫緣妃以進，喜妄談休咎，捕送開封獄。

translations.literal: The diviner Liu Kangsun advanced through the consort and delighted in reckless talk of fortune and calamity; he was seized and sent to the Kaifeng prison.
translations.idiomatic: The diviner Liu Kangsun had advanced through the consort and delighted in reckless talk of omens. He was arrested and sent to the Kaifeng prison.

sentences.zh: 醫曹孝忠竺疾無狀，閣內待王堯臣坐盜金珠及出金明池遊宴事，併鞫治。

translations.literal: The physician Cao Xiaozhong feigned illness without cause; the inner attendant Wang Yaochén was implicated for stealing gold and pearls and for going out to feast at Jinming Pool; all were jointly tried.
translations.idiomatic: The physician Cao Xiaozhong feigned illness without cause. The inner attendant Wang Yaochén was implicated for stealing gold and pearls and for going out to feast at Jinming Pool. All were tried together.

sentences.zh: 獄成，同日誅死。

translations.literal: When the case was concluded they were executed on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was concluded they were executed on the same day.

sentences.zh: 遂廢崔妃為庶人。

translations.literal: Consort Cui was then deposed to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Cui was then deposed to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 崔生王椿及帝姬五人云。

translations.literal: Cui bore Prince Wang Chun and five imperial princesses.
translations.idiomatic: Cui had borne Prince Wang Chun and five imperial princesses.

sentences.zh: 欽宗朱皇后，開封祥符人。

translations.literal: Empress Zhu of Emperor Qinzong was a native of Xiangfu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhu of Emperor Qinzong came from Xiangfu in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 父伯材，武康軍節度使。

translations.literal: Her father Bo Cai was military commissioner of Wukang Army.
translations.idiomatic: Her father, Bo Cai, served as military commissioner of Wukang Army.

sentences.zh: 欽宗在東宮，徽宗臨軒備禮，冊為皇太子妃。

translations.literal: While Qinzong was heir apparent, Huizong presided in person over the full rites and invested her as crown princess.
translations.idiomatic: While Qinzong was still heir apparent, Huizong personally presided at the full rites and invested her as crown princess.

sentences.zh: 欽宗即位，立為皇后。

translations.literal: When Qinzong acceded she was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Qinzong took the throne she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 追封伯材為恩平郡王。

translations.literal: Bo Cai was enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Enping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Cai was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Enping.

sentences.zh: 后既北遷，不知崩聞。

translations.literal: After the empress was taken north, news of her death was not known.
translations.idiomatic: After the empress was carried off northward, no word of her death reached the court.

sentences.zh: 慶元三年上尊號，諡仁懷，祔於太廟欽宗室，推恩后家十五人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qingyuan a superior title of honor was bestowed; her posthumous name was Renhuai; she was enshrined in the Ancestral Temple in Qinzong's shrine; favors were extended to fifteen members of the empress's family.
translations.idiomatic: In 1197 a superior honorific was conferred, her posthumous name was fixed as Renhuai, her spirit tablet was placed in Qinzong's shrine in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and fifteen of her kin received favors.

sentences.zh: 五年，奉安神禦于景靈宮。

translations.literal: In the fifth year her sacred spirit was lodged in Jingling Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later her spirit seat was installed in Jingling Palace.

sentences.zh: 兄二人：孝孫，靖康中以節鉞換授右金吾衛上將軍，卒贈開府含義同三同；

translations.literal: She had two elder brothers: Xiaosun, who during the Jingkang era exchanged his commissioner's credentials for appointment as Senior General of the Right Golden Crow Guards and who on death was posthumously given Defender-in-Chief with Honored Equal Treatment to the Three Excellencies;
translations.idiomatic: She had two elder brothers: Xiaosun, who during the Jingkang crisis surrendered his command for appointment as senior general of the Right Golden Crow Guards and who, when he died, was posthumously granted defender-in-chief with honors equal to the Three Excellencies;

sentences.zh: 孝章，一日孝莊，官至永慶軍承宣使，卒贈昭化軍節度使。

translations.literal: Xiaozhang—on one day called Xiaozhuang—rose to deputy commissioner of Yongqing Army and on death was posthumously made military commissioner of Zhaohua Army.
translations.idiomatic: and Xiaozhang—who was once known as Xiaozhuang—rose to deputy military commissioner of Yongqing Army and on his death was posthumously made military commissioner of Zhaohua Army.

sentences.zh: 高宗憲節邢皇后，開封祥符人。

translations.literal: Empress Xianjie Xing of Emperor Gaozong was a native of Xiangfu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xianjie of the Xing clan, consort of Emperor Gaozong, came from Xiangfu in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 父煥，朝請郎。

translations.literal: Her father Huan was a Gentleman for Court Consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Huan held the rank of Gentleman for Court Consultation.

sentences.zh: 高宗居康邸，以歸聘之，封嘉國夫人。

translations.literal: When Gaozong dwelt at the Prince of Kang's residence he took her in marriage and enfeoffed her Lady of Jiaguo.
translations.idiomatic: While Gaozong still lived at the Kang princely residence he married her and created her Lady of Jiaguo.

sentences.zh: 王出使，無人留居蕃衍宅。

translations.literal: When the prince went on a mission no one remained to dwell at the Fanyan Residence.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince went abroad on a mission, no one was left at the Fanyan Residence.

sentences.zh: 金人犯京師，夫人從三宮北遷。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens attacked the capital the lady followed the three palaces northward.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens attacked the capital she accompanied the three palaces in the northward flight.

sentences.zh: 上皇遣曹勳歸，夫人脫所禦金環，使內侍持付勳曰：「幸為吾白大王，願如此環，得早相見也。」

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor sent Cao Xun back; the lady removed the gold ring she wore and had an inner attendant carry it to Xun, saying: "Please tell the prince for me that, like this ring, I hope we may meet again soon."
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor sent Cao Xun back south. The lady took off the gold ring she wore and had a palace attendant give it to him, saying, "Please tell the prince for me that, like this ring, I hope we may meet again soon."

sentences.zh: 王憐之。

translations.literal: The prince pitied her.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was moved with pity for her.

sentences.zh: 及即位，遙冊為皇后，宮后親屬二十五人。

translations.literal: When he took the throne she was enregistered as empress from afar, and twenty-five of the empress's kin received favors.
translations.idiomatic: When he ascended the throne he invested her as empress from afar, and twenty-five of her relatives received favors.

sentences.zh: 紹興九年后崩于五國城，年三十四。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Shaoxing the empress died at Five States City at the age of thirty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In 1139 the empress died at Five States City, aged thirty-four.

sentences.zh: 金人秘之，高宗虛中宮以待者十六年。

translations.literal: The Jin kept her death secret; Gaozong left the central palace vacant in expectation for sixteen years.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin concealed her death, and Gaozong kept the main consort's seat empty while he waited for her return—a wait that lasted sixteen years.

sentences.zh: 顯仁太后回鑾，始得崩聞。

translations.literal: Only when Empress Dowager Xianren returned to the south did word of the empress's death reach the court.
translations.idiomatic: Not until Empress Dowager Xianren's own return south did the emperor learn that the empress had died.

sentences.zh: 上為輟朝，行釋服之祭，諡懿節，祔主於別廟。

translations.literal: The emperor suspended court, performed the rites of laying aside mourning garments, bestowed the posthumous title Yijie, and enshrined her tablet in a separate temple.
translations.idiomatic: He suspended court, performed the rites of released mourning, gave her the posthumous name Yijie, and enshrined her spirit tablet in a side temple.

sentences.zh: 紹興十二年八月，后梓宮至，攢于聖獻太后梓宮之西北。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twelfth year of Shaoxing the empress's coffin arrived and was laid to rest northwest of Empress Dowager Shengxian's coffin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of 1142 her coffin reached the capital and was buried northwest of Empress Dowager Shengxian's tomb.

sentences.zh: 帝思后，殊慘不樂，皇后吳氏知帝意，乃請為其侄珣、琚婚邢氏二女，以慰帝心。

translations.literal: The emperor's longing for the empress made him deeply desolate; Empress Wu, knowing his mind, then asked that her nephews Xun and Ju marry the two daughters of the Xing clan to console him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned her so keenly that he could scarcely be consoled; Empress Wu, perceiving his grief, asked that her nephews Xun and Ju marry two daughters of the Xing house to comfort him.

sentences.zh: 淳熙末，改諡憲節，祔高宗廟。

translations.literal: In the late Chunxi era her posthumous title was changed to Xianjie and she was enshrined in Gaozong's temple.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Chunxi reign her posthumous name was revised to Xianjie and she was enshrined in Gaozong's temple shrine.

sentences.zh: 憲聖慈烈吳皇后

translations.literal: Empress Xiansheng Cilie Wu
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiansheng Cilie of the Wu clan

sentences.zh: 憲聖慈烈吳皇后，開封人。

translations.literal: Empress Xiansheng Cilie Wu was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiansheng Cilie Wu came from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 父近，以后貴，累官武翼郎，贈太師，追封吳王，諡宣靖。

translations.literal: Her father Jin, because of his daughter's eminence, was repeatedly promoted to Martial Wings Gentleman, posthumously made Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed as Prince of Wu, and given the posthumous title Xuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Jin, raised by his daughter's rank, rose repeatedly in office to Martial Wings Gentleman, and after death was made grand preceptor, enfeoffed as Prince of Wu, and given the posthumous epithet Xuanjing.

sentences.zh: 近嘗夢至一亭，扁曰「侍康」；

translations.literal: Jin once dreamed he came to a pavilion whose plaque read "Serving Kang";
translations.idiomatic: Jin once dreamed that he reached a pavilion labeled "Serving Kang";

sentences.zh: 傍植芍藥，獨放一花，殊妍麗可愛，花下白羊一，近寤而異之。

translations.literal: beside it grew tree peonies, with a single blossom in extraordinary beauty; beneath the flower stood a white sheep; when he awoke he marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: peonies grew beside it, one bloom alone in surpassing beauty, and a white sheep stood beneath the flower; when he woke he was struck by the omen.

sentences.zh: 后以乙未歲生，方產時，紅光徹戶外。

translations.literal: The empress was born in the yiwei year; at the moment of birth red light filled the room outside the door.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was born in the yiwei cycle year; at her birth red light flooded the space beyond the door.

sentences.zh: 年十四，高宗為康王，被選入宮，人謂「侍康」之徵。

translations.literal: At fourteen, when Gaozong was Prince of Kang, she was chosen for the palace; people said it was the fulfillment of "Serving Kang."
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen she was selected for the palace when Gaozong was still Prince of Kang—taken as the fulfillment of the "Serving Kang" sign.

sentences.zh: 王即帝位，后常以戎服侍左右。

translations.literal: When the prince became emperor she often attended him in military dress.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took the throne she often waited on him in martial attire.

sentences.zh: 后頗知書，從幸四明，衛士謀為變，入問帝所在，后紿之以免。

translations.literal: The empress was quite learned and accompanied him to Siming; when guards plotted mutiny and came asking where the emperor was, she deceived them and he escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: She was well read and accompanied him to Siming; when guards plotted mutiny and asked where the emperor was, she deceived them and he escaped unharmed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，帝航海，有魚躍入禦舟，后曰：「此周人白魚之祥也。」

translations.literal: Before long the emperor put to sea; a fish leaped into the imperial boat; the empress said: "This is the Zhou people's omen of the white fish."
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the emperor went to sea; when a fish leaped into the imperial boat she said, "This is the auspice of the white fish from the Zhou rise to power."

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，封和義郡夫人。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and enfeoffed her as Lady of Heyi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and enfeoffed her as Lady of Heyi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 還越，進封才人。

translations.literal: On returning to Yue she was advanced to Talented Lady.
translations.idiomatic: After the return to Yue she was promoted to Talented Lady.

sentences.zh: 后益博習書史，又善翰墨，由是寵遇日至，與張氏並為婉儀，尋進貴妃。

translations.literal: The empress came to study books and history more broadly and was skilled at calligraphy; favor toward her increased day by day; she and Lady Zhang became Honored Ladies, then soon advanced to Imperial Consort.
translations.idiomatic: She deepened her study of history and excelled at calligraphy; imperial favor grew daily until she and Lady Zhang were both Honored Ladies and soon Imperial Consorts.

sentences.zh: 顯仁太后回鑾，亦愛后。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Xianren returned, she too loved the empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Xianren returned south she also cherished the future empress.

sentences.zh: 憲節皇后崩聞至，秦檜等累表請立中宮，太后亦為言。

translations.literal: When word came of Empress Xianjie's death, Qin Hui and others repeatedly memorialized to install a central empress, and the empress dowager spoke on her behalf as well.
translations.idiomatic: After news arrived of Empress Xianjie's death, Qin Hui and others repeatedly urged Gaozong to fill the main consort's seat, and the empress dowager spoke for her too.

sentences.zh: 紹興十三年，詔立貴妃為皇后。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Shaoxing an edict installed the imperial consort as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In 1143 an edict made the imperial consort empress.

sentences.zh: 帝御文德殿授冊，后即穆清殿廷受之。

translations.literal: The emperor invested her at Wende Hall and she received the register in Muqing Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor conducted the investiture at Wende Hall and she received the patent in Muqing Hall.

sentences.zh: 追王三代，親屬由後官者三十五人。

translations.literal: Her three generations were enfeoffed as kings; thirty-five kin who had gained office through her were promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations of her ancestors were enfeoffed as kings and thirty-five relatives who had entered service through her connections were promoted.

sentences.zh: 顯仁太后性嚴肅，后身承起居，順適其意。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xianren was stern by nature; the empress personally attended her in daily life and conformed to her wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xianren was severe by disposition; the empress waited on her in person day and night and adapted herself to her every wish.

sentences.zh: 嘗繪《古列女圖》，置坐中為鑒；

translations.literal: She once painted Illustrations of Ancient Exemplary Women and set them before her seat as a mirror;
translations.idiomatic: She once painted scenes from Exemplary Women of Antiquity and kept them before her as a moral mirror;

sentences.zh: 又取《詩序》之義，扁其堂曰「賢志」。

translations.literal: and taking the sense of the Classic of Poetry's prefaces, she inscribed her hall "Admirable Purpose."
translations.idiomatic: and, drawing on the moral prefaces of the Book of Songs, she named her hall "Admirable Resolve."

sentences.zh: 初，伯琮以宗子召入宮，命張氏育之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Bo Cong had been summoned into the palace as a clansman; the emperor ordered Lady Zhang to rear him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Bo Cong had been brought into the palace as an imperial clansman and the emperor charged Lady Zhang with raising him.

sentences.zh: 后時為才人，亦請得育一子，於是得伯玖，更名璩。

translations.literal: The empress was then a Talented Lady and also asked to rear a son; thereby she received Bo Jiu, who was renamed Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The empress, then still a Talented Lady, also asked to raise a prince; she was given Bo Jiu, later renamed Yu.

sentences.zh: 中外議頗籍籍。

translations.literal: Opinion inside and outside the court buzzed.
translations.idiomatic: Court and capital alike murmured at the arrangement.

sentences.zh: 張氏卒，並育於后，后視之無間。

translations.literal: When Lady Zhang died, both boys were raised by the empress, who treated them without distinction.
translations.idiomatic: After Lady Zhang died both boys were placed under the empress, who cared for them without favoritism.

sentences.zh: 伯琮性恭儉，喜讀書，帝與后皆愛之，封普安郡王。

translations.literal: Bo Cong was respectful and frugal and loved books; emperor and empress both cherished him and enfeoffed him as Prince of Pu'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Cong was respectful, frugal, and fond of study; emperor and empress alike loved him and made him Prince of Pu'an Commandery.

sentences.zh: 后嘗語帝曰：「普安，其天日之表也。」

translations.literal: The empress once told the emperor: "Pu'an shows the bearing of one illumined by heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The empress once told the emperor, "Pu'an has the bearing of a Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 帝意決，立為皇子，封建王。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was decided; he established him as heir apparent and enfeoffed him as Prince of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's mind was made up; he made him heir apparent and then Prince of Jian.

sentences.zh: 出璩居紹興。

translations.literal: Yu was sent out to reside at Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was sent to live at Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 高宗內禪，手詔后稱太上皇后，遷居德壽宮。

translations.literal: When Gaozong abdicated in the inner palace he personally issued an edict styling the empress Grand Empress and moved her residence to Deshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong abdicated, he personally issued an edict naming the empress Grand Empress and moved her to Deshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 孝宗即位，上尊號曰壽聖太上皇后。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong succeeded he bestowed the superior title Shousheng Grand Empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong took the throne he bestowed on her the superior title Shousheng Grand Empress.

sentences.zh: 月朔，朝上皇畢，入見后如宮中儀。

translations.literal: On the first of each month, after attending the retired emperor, he entered to see the empress with the rites used within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of each month, after attending the retired emperor, he visited the empress with the customary inner-palace rites.

sentences.zh: 加號壽聖明慈。

translations.literal: The additional title Shousheng Mingci was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: She received the additional title Shousheng Mingci.

sentences.zh: 以上皇行慶壽禮，復加壽聖齊明廣慈之號。

translations.literal: Because the retired emperor performed the Celebration of Longevity rite, she was again given the title Shousheng Qiming Guangci.
translations.idiomatic: When the retired emperor performed the Celebration of Longevity rite, she received the further title Shousheng Qiming Guangci.

sentences.zh: 十年，以后年七十，親屬推恩有差。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, because the empress was seventy, her kin received differentiated favors.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, when the empress turned seventy, her relatives received differentiated favors.

sentences.zh: 十二年，加尊號曰備德。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the superior title Beide was added.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year she received the additional honorific Beide.

sentences.zh: 上皇崩，遺詔改稱皇太后。

translations.literal: When the retired emperor died his testamentary edict changed her style to empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When the retired emperor died, his testament changed her title to empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 帝欲迎還大內，太后以上皇几筵在德壽宮，不忍舍去，因名所禦殿曰慈福，居焉。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to welcome her back to the Great Inner Palace, but the empress dowager, because the retired emperor's spirit seat was at Deshou Palace, could not bear to leave and therefore named the hall where she dwelled Cifu and lived there.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to bring her back to the main palace, but because the retired emperor's spirit seat remained at Deshou Palace she could not bear to leave. She named her hall Cifu and lived there.

sentences.zh: 光宗即位，更號壽聖皇太后，以壽皇故，不稱太皇太后也。

translations.literal: When Guangzong succeeded her title was changed to Shousheng Empress Dowager; because of the late emperor she was not styled grand empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong took the throne her title was changed to Shousheng Empress Dowager; out of regard for the late emperor she was not called grand empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗言及用人，后曰：「宜崇尚舊臣。」

translations.literal: When the emperor once spoke of appointing men, the empress said: "Old ministers should be honored and employed."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor once spoke of appointments, the empress said, "You should honor and employ the old ministers."

sentences.zh: 后壽八十，帝乃覲后，奉冊禮，加尊號曰隆慈備福。

translations.literal: When the empress reached eighty the emperor at last paid her a formal visit, performed the investiture rite, and added the superior title Longci Beifu.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress turned eighty the emperor at last paid her a formal visit, performed the investiture rite, and added the honorific Longci Beifu.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，帝率群臣行慶壽禮，嘉王侍側，后勉以讀書辨邪正、立綱常為先。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year the emperor led the hundred officials in the Celebration of Longevity rite with Prince Jia attending at his side; the empress urged him to put reading, distinguishing right from wrong, and establishing moral order first.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year the emperor led the court in the Celebration of Longevity with Prince Jia at his side. The empress urged him to put study, the discernment of right and wrong, and the establishment of moral order first.

sentences.zh: 夏，孝宗崩，始正太皇太后之號。

translations.literal: In summer, when Xiaozong died, she at last received the proper title of grand empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: That summer, when Xiaozong died, she at last received the proper title of grand empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 時光宗疾未平，不能執喪，宰臣請垂簾主喪事，后不可。

translations.literal: At this time Guangzong's illness had not yet eased and he could not preside over mourning; the chief ministers asked that the empress dowager curtain the court and oversee the funeral, which she refused.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzong's illness had not yet lifted and he could not conduct the mourning rites; the chief ministers asked the empress dowager to rule from behind a screen and manage the funeral, but she refused.

sentences.zh: 已而宰執請如唐肅宗故事，群臣發喪太極殿，成服禁中，許之。

translations.literal: Presently the chief ministers asked to follow the precedent of Tang Suzong; the officials would conduct the funeral at Taiji Hall, and mourning garments would be worn within the palace—this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers then proposed following the Tang Suzong precedent: the court would hold the public mourning at Taiji Hall while the palace observed private mourning, and she assented.

sentences.zh: 后代行祭尊禮。

translations.literal: The empress dowager performed the sacrificial rites of honor in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager herself carried out the honorary sacrifices on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 尋用樞密趙汝愚請，于梓宮前垂簾，宣光宗手詔，立皇子嘉王為皇帝。

translations.literal: Soon, at Privy Councillor Zhao Ruyu's request, she curtained before the coffin, proclaimed Guangzong's handwritten edict, and installed Crown Prince Prince Jia as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, at the request of Privy Councillor Zhao Ruyu, she drew the curtain before the coffin, read Guangzong's own edict, and installed Crown Prince Prince Jia as emperor.

sentences.zh: 翌日，冊夫人韓氏為皇后，撤簾。

translations.literal: The next day she invested Lady Han as empress and withdrew the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: The following day she invested Lady Han as empress and lifted the curtain.

sentences.zh: 慶元元年，加號光祐，遷居重華宮。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qingyuan she was given the honorific Guangyou and moved to Chonghua Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In 1195 she received the honorific title Guangyou and took up residence in Chonghua Palace.

sentences.zh: 汝愚後以謫死，中書舍人汪義端目汝愚為李林甫，欲並逐其党，太后聞而非之。

translations.literal: Zhao Ruyu later died in exile; Central Secretariat Drafter Wang Yiduan likened Zhao to Li Linfu and wished to purge his faction as well; on hearing this the empress dowager disapproved.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ruyu later died in disgrace; drafting officer Wang Yiduan compared him to Li Linfu and sought to drive out his allies too, but the empress dowager condemned the proposal.

sentences.zh: 三年十月，后寢疾，詔禱天地、宗廟、社稷，大赦天下，逾月而崩，年八十三。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year she took to her bed; an edict ordered prayer to Heaven, Earth, the ancestral temple, and the state altars; a great amnesty was proclaimed; after more than a month she died at the age of eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of 1197 she fell ill; the court ordered prayers at the temples and altars and proclaimed a general amnesty; a little over a month later she died, aged eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 遺誥：「太上皇帝疾未痊癒，宜於宮中承重；

translations.literal: Her testamentary edict read: "The retired emperor's illness is not yet fully healed; he should observe the chief mourning within the palace;
translations.idiomatic: Her final edict ran: "The Retired Emperor has not yet recovered; he should undertake the principal mourning duties within the palace;

sentences.zh: 皇帝服齊衰五月，以日易月。」

translations.literal: the emperor should wear qi mourning for five months, counting one day as one month."
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor should wear second-grade mourning for five months, reckoning each day as a month."

sentences.zh: 詔服期年喪。

translations.literal: An edict ordered observance of one year's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then required the full one-year mourning period.

sentences.zh: 諡曰憲聖慈烈，攢祔於永思陵。

translations.literal: Her posthumous title was given as Xiansheng Cilie; she was jointly enshrined at Yongsi Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: She received the temple name Xiansheng Cilie and was jointly enshrined at Yongsi Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 潘賢妃

translations.literal: Worthy Consort Pan
translations.idiomatic: Worthy Consort Pan

sentences.zh: 潘賢妃，開封人，元懿太子母也。

translations.literal: Worthy Consort Pan was a native of Kaifeng and mother of the Yuanyi Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy Consort Pan, from Kaifeng, was the mother of Heir Apparent Yuanyi.

sentences.zh: 父永壽，直翰林醫局官。

translations.literal: Her father Yongshou was a direct appointee in the Hanlin Medical Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Yongshou served as a physician in the Hanlin Medical Bureau.

sentences.zh: 高宗居康邸時納之，邢后北遷，妃未有位號，帝即位，將立為后，呂好問諫止之，立為賢妃。

translations.literal: When Gaozong dwelt at the Kang Princely Residence he took her in; when Empress Xing moved north the consort had no rank; on the emperor's accession he was about to install her as empress, but Lü Haowen remonstrated and stopped it; she was established as Worthy Consort.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong took her in while he still lived at the Kang residence. After Empress Xing was taken north, Pan had no formal title. When he became emperor he intended to make her empress, but Lü Haowen dissuaded him, and she was created Worthy Consort instead.

sentences.zh: 太子薨，從隆祐太后于江西，逾年還。

translations.literal: When the heir apparent died she followed Empress Dowager Longyou to Jiangxi; after more than a year she returned.
translations.idiomatic: After the crown prince died she accompanied Empress Dowager Longyou to Jiangxi and returned more than a year later.

sentences.zh: 紹興十八年薨。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Shaoxing she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 1148.

sentences.zh: 永壽，贈太子少師。

translations.literal: Yongshou was posthumously granted Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Yongshou was posthumously made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 張賢妃

translations.literal: Worthy Consort Zhang
translations.idiomatic: Worthy Consort Zhang

sentences.zh: 張賢妃，開封人。

translations.literal: Worthy Consort Zhang was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy Consort Zhang was from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，為才人，有寵，進婕妤。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyan she became a Talented Lady, won favor, and was advanced to Imperial Concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianyan era she entered the palace as a Talented Lady, won the emperor's favor, and was promoted to Imperial Concubine.

sentences.zh: 帝欲擇宗室子養禁中，輔臣問帝以宮中可付託者誰耶？

translations.literal: The emperor wished to select a son from the imperial clan to rear within the palace; a chief minister asked whom in the palace could be entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to adopt an imperial clansman to raise in the palace. A leading minister asked whom in the inner quarters might be trusted with such a charge.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「已得之矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I have already found him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "I have already found him."

sentences.zh: 意在婕妤。

translations.literal: His intention lay with the Imperial Concubine.
translations.idiomatic: He had the Imperial Concubine in mind.

sentences.zh: 已而伯琮入宮，年尚幼，婕妤與潘賢妃、吳才人方環坐，以觀其所向。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Bo Cong entered the palace; he was still young; the Imperial Concubine, Worthy Consort Pan, and Talented Lady Wu were seated in a circle to observe which way he would go.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Cong was then brought into the palace while still a child. Imperial Concubine Zhang, Worthy Consort Pan, and Talented Lady Wu sat around him to see whom he would approach.

sentences.zh: 時賢妃新失皇子，意忽忽不樂，婕妤手招之，遂向婕妤。

translations.literal: At that time Worthy Consort Pan had newly lost a prince and was dispirited; the Imperial Concubine beckoned with her hand, and he accordingly went toward the Imperial Concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy Consort Pan had just lost a son and was downcast. Imperial Concubine Zhang beckoned to the boy, and he went to her.

sentences.zh: 帝因命婕妤母之，是為孝宗。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon ordered the Imperial Concubine to mother him; this was Xiaozong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then had Imperial Concubine Zhang rear him as her son; this child became Emperor Xiaozong.

sentences.zh: 尋遷婉儀，十二年卒，上為輟朝二日，贈賢妃。

translations.literal: Soon she was promoted to Honored Lady; in the twelfth year she died; the emperor suspended court for two days and posthumously granted her Worthy Consort.
translations.idiomatic: She was soon promoted to Honored Lady. In the twelfth year of Shaoxing she died; the emperor halted court audiences for two days and posthumously ennobled her as Worthy Consort.

sentences.zh: 弟萃，閣門宣贊舍人，妃薨，遷秩二階。

translations.literal: Her younger brother Cui was a Gate-Ushers' Promoter; when the consort died his rank was raised two steps.
translations.idiomatic: Her younger brother Cui was a Gate-Ushers' Promoter; when she died his rank was raised two grades.

sentences.zh: 劉貴妃

translations.literal: Imperial Consort Liu
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Consort Liu

sentences.zh: 劉賢妃，臨安人。

translations.literal: Worthy Consort Liu was a native of Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy Consort Liu was from Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 入宮為紅霞帔，遷才人，累遷婕妤、婉容，紹興二十四年進賢妃。

translations.literal: She entered the palace as Hongxia Pei, was moved up to Talented Lady, and was successively promoted to Imperial Concubine and Graceful Lady; in the twenty-fourth year of Shaoxing she was advanced to Worthy Consort.
translations.idiomatic: She entered the palace as a Hongxia Pei attendant, became a Talented Lady, and rose through Imperial Concubine and Graceful Lady; in 1154 she was promoted to Worthy Consort.

sentences.zh: 頗恃寵驕侈，嘗因盛夏以水晶飾腳踏，帝見之，命取為枕，妃懼，撤去之。

translations.literal: She relied greatly on favor and was proud and extravagant; once in midsummer she decorated her footrest with crystal; when the emperor saw it he ordered it taken to be his pillow; the consort was afraid and had it removed.
translations.idiomatic: She was spoiled by favor and lived lavishly. One midsummer she inlaid her footrest with crystal. When the emperor saw it he had it taken for his pillow; alarmed, she had the ornament removed.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十四年薨。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Chunxi she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 1187.

sentences.zh: 父懋，累官昭慶軍節度使。

translations.literal: Her father Mao rose in office to Military Commissioner of the Zhaqing Army.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Mao eventually became military commissioner of the Zhaqing army.

sentences.zh: 金人南侵，獻錢二萬緡以助軍興費。

translations.literal: When the Jin invaded southward he presented twenty thousand strings of cash to assist military expenses.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens pushed south he donated twenty thousand strings of cash toward war costs.

sentences.zh: 懋子允升，紹興末為和州防禦使、知閣門事。

translations.literal: Mao's son Yun Sheng at the end of Shaoxing was Defense Commissioner of He Prefecture and Director of the Gate-Ushers' Office.
translations.idiomatic: Mao's son Yun Sheng, late in the Shaoxing era, served as defense commissioner of He Prefecture and director of the Gate-Ushers' Office.

sentences.zh: 奉使還，遷蘄州防物使、福州觀察使。

translations.literal: On returning from a mission he was transferred to Defense Commissioner of Qi Prefecture and Observation Commissioner of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After completing an embassy he was promoted to defense commissioner of Qi Prefecture and observation commissioner of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 劉婉儀

translations.literal: Honored Lady Liu
translations.idiomatic: Honored Lady Liu

sentences.zh: 劉婉儀，初入宮，封宜春郡夫人。

translations.literal: Honored Lady Liu, on first entering the palace, was enfeoffed as Lady of Yichun Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Honored Lady Liu first entered the palace she was enfeoffed as Lady of Yichun Commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋進才人，與劉婉容俱被寵，進婉儀。

translations.literal: Soon she was advanced to Talented Lady; she and Graceful Lady Liu alike received favor and were promoted to Honored Lady.
translations.idiomatic: She was soon made a Talented Lady. She and Graceful Lady Liu both won favor and were promoted to Honored Lady.

sentences.zh: 婉儀頗恃恩招，嘗遣人諷廣州蕃商獻明珠香藥，許以官爵。

translations.literal: Honored Lady Liu rather relied on grace to solicit gifts; once she sent someone to hint to Guangzhou foreign merchants to present pearls and aromatics, promising official rank in return.
translations.idiomatic: Honored Lady Liu used her influence to solicit tribute: she once had an intermediary suggest to Guangzhou maritime traders that they offer pearls and aromatics in exchange for official rank.

sentences.zh: 舶官林孝澤言於朝，詔止其獻。

translations.literal: The shipping superintendent Lin Xiaozhe reported to court; an edict halted such presentations.
translations.idiomatic: The shipping superintendent Lin Xiaozhe reported this to court, and an edict forbade the gifts.

sentences.zh: 金人將叛盟，劉錡主戰，幸醫王繼先從中沮之，因謀誅錡，帝不懌。

translations.literal: The Jin were about to break the treaty; Liu Qi advocated war; the favorite physician Wang Jixian obstructed it from within and thereby plotted to execute Qi; the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: As the Jin were about to renounce the peace treaty, Liu Qi urged war, but the emperor's favorite physician Wang Jixian worked behind the scenes to thwart him and even plotted Qi's death. The emperor was troubled.

sentences.zh: 一日，在婉儀位，有憂色。

translations.literal: One day, while at Honored Lady Liu's apartments, he wore a troubled look.
translations.idiomatic: One day, visiting Honored Lady Liu's quarters, he looked worried.

sentences.zh: 婉儀陰訪得其言，以寬譬帝意。

translations.literal: Honored Lady Liu secretly inquired and learned his words; she reassured him to ease the emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: She quietly found out what was weighing on him and spoke to calm him.

sentences.zh: 帝怪與繼先言合，詰之，婉儀急，具以實對。

translations.literal: The emperor wondered that it matched Wang Jixian's talk and questioned her; Honored Lady Liu was alarmed and told the whole truth.
translations.idiomatic: Surprised that her words matched Wang Jixian's, he pressed her; alarmed, she confessed everything.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，托以他過廢之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and, under pretext of another fault, deposed her.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, he deposed her on a pretext of other misconduct.

sentences.zh: 兄伉，累官和州防禦使、知閣門事，婉儀既廢，乃與祠罷歸。
