translations.literal: Her elder brother Kang rose in office to Defense Commissioner of He Prefecture and Director of the Gate-Ushers' Office; after Honored Lady Liu was deposed he was dismissed to a sacrificial appointment and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder brother Kang had served as defense commissioner of He Prefecture and director of the Gate-Ushers' Office; after her fall he was given a nominal temple post and sent home.

sentences.zh: 張貴妃

translations.literal: Imperial Noble Consort Zhang
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Noble Consort Zhang

sentences.zh: 張貴妃，開封祥符人。

translations.literal: Imperial Noble Consort Zhang was a native of Xiangfu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Noble Consort Zhang was from Xiangfu in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 初入宮，封永嘉郡夫人。

translations.literal: On first entering the palace she was enfeoffed as Lady of Yongjia Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When she first entered the palace she was enfeoffed as Lady of Yongjia Commandery.

sentences.zh: 乾道六年，進婉容。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qiandao she was advanced to Graceful Lady.
translations.idiomatic: In 1170 she was promoted to Graceful Lady.

sentences.zh: 淳熙七年，封太上皇淑妃。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Chunxi she was created Imperial Concubine to the Retired Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1180 she was created imperial concubine to the Retired Emperor.

sentences.zh: 十六年，進貴妃。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year she was advanced to Imperial Noble Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In 1189 she was promoted to imperial noble consort.

sentences.zh: 紹熙元年薨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxi she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 1190.

sentences.zh: 美人馮氏，才人韓氏、吳氏、李氏、王氏俱被寵倖，后皆廢。

translations.literal: Beautiful Lady Feng, Talented Ladies Han, Wu, Li, and Wang all received the emperor's favor; each was later deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Beautiful Lady Feng and Talented Ladies Han, Wu, Li, and Wang all enjoyed the emperor's favor, but each was later dismissed.

sentences.zh: 吳氏，中宮近屬也，紹興三十年，復故封。

translations.literal: Wu was related to the inner palace; in the thirtieth year of Shaoxing her former rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was kin to the empress's household; in 1160 her former title was restored.

sentences.zh: 李氏、王氏俱明豔，淳熙末，上皇愛之。

translations.literal: Li and Wang were both strikingly fair; toward the end of Chunxi the Retired Emperor favored them.
translations.idiomatic: Li and Wang were both renowned for their beauty; toward the end of the Chunxi era the Retired Emperor doted on them.

sentences.zh: 及崩，憲聖后見二才人，每感憤，孝宗即追告命，許自便。

translations.literal: At his death Empress Xiansheng, seeing the two Talented Ladies, was each time stirred to anger; Xiaozong at once pursued their patents of appointment and permitted them to go as they pleased.
translations.idiomatic: After his death Empress Xiansheng grew indignant whenever she saw the two talented ladies. Xiaozong immediately restored their patents and allowed them to leave court freely.

sentences.zh: 蓋非常制云。

translations.literal: This was altogether outside the usual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: This was an exceptional measure.

sentences.zh: 成穆郭皇后

translations.literal: Empress Chengmu Guo
translations.idiomatic: Empress Chengmu Guo

sentences.zh: 孝宗成穆郭皇后，開封祥符人。

translations.literal: Xiaozong's Empress Chengmu Guo was a native of Xiangfu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong's Empress Chengmu Guo was from Xiangfu in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 奉直大夫直卿之女孫，其六世祖為章穆皇后外家。

translations.literal: She was granddaughter of the Retired Attendant Zhiqing, Chamberlain for the Direct; her sixth-generation ancestor belonged to the maternal kin of Empress Zhangmu.
translations.idiomatic: She was a granddaughter of Zhiqing, a retired attendant of the Direct Service; her sixth-generation forebear came from the maternal family of Empress Zhangmu.

sentences.zh: 孝宗為普安郡王時納郭氏，封咸甯郡夫人。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong was Prince of Pu'an Commandery he took the Guo clan in marriage and enfeoffed her as Lady of Xianning Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong was Prince of Pu'an he married Guo and enfeoffed her as Lady of Xianning Commandery.

sentences.zh: 生光守及莊文太子、魏惠憲王愷、邵悼肅王恪。

translations.literal: She bore Guangshou as well as Crown Prince Zhuangwen, Prince Wei Hui Xian Kai, and Prince Shao Dao Su Ke.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Guangshou, Crown Prince Zhuangwen, Prince Wei Hui Xian (Kai), and Prince Shao Dao Su (Ke).

sentences.zh: 紹興二十六年薨，年三十一，追封淑國夫人。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Shaoxing she died at thirty-one and was posthumously enfeoffed Lady of Shuguo.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 1156 at thirty-one and was posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Shuguo.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，用明堂恩，贈福國夫人。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, using the Bright Hall grace, she was granted Lady of Fuguo.
translations.idiomatic: In 1161, by grace of the Bright Hall ceremony, she was advanced to Lady of Fuguo.

sentences.zh: 既建太子，追封皇太子妃。

translations.literal: Once the crown prince was established she was posthumously enfeoffed Crown Prince's Consort.
translations.idiomatic: After the crown prince was named she was posthumously made crown prince's consort.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，追冊為皇后，諡恭懷，尋改安穆。

translations.literal: Upon his receiving the abdication she was posthumously enshrined as empress with the title Gonghuai, soon changed to Anmu.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne she was posthumously enthroned as empress with the posthumous name Gonghuai, soon changed to Anmu.

sentences.zh: 及營阜陵，又改成穆，祔孝宗廟。

translations.literal: When Yongfu Mausoleum was planned it was again changed to Chengmu, and she was enshrined in Xiaozong's temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongfu Mausoleum was laid out the title was changed again to Chengmu, and she was enshrined in Xiaozong's ancestral shrine.

sentences.zh: 父瑊，累官昭慶軍承宣使，追封榮王。

translations.literal: Her father Jian rose in office to Commissary Envoy of the Zhaqing Army and was posthumously enfeoffed Prince Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Jian rose to commissary envoy of the Zhaqing army and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Rong.

sentences.zh: 孝宗待郭氏恩禮彌厚，然不假外戚以官爵。

translations.literal: Xiaozong treated the Guo clan with ever fuller grace and ritual, yet he did not grant titles and offices to the maternal kin.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong showed the Guo family ever greater honor, yet he did not shower offices on his wife's relatives.

sentences.zh: 后弟師禹、師元，官不過承宣使，師元不及建節而卒。

translations.literal: The empress's younger brothers Shiyu and Shiyuan never rose above Commissary Envoy; Shiyuan died before receiving a commandery commission.
translations.idiomatic: Her brothers Shiyu and Shiyuan never rose above commissary envoy; Shiyuan died before receiving a military commission.

sentences.zh: 將內禪，師禹始除節度使。

translations.literal: As inner abdication was impending, Shiyu was first appointed Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Just before Xiaozong's abdication, Shiyu was finally made a military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 光宗朝，官至太保，封永甯郡王。

translations.literal: Under Guangzong he reached Grand Protector and was enfeoffed Prince of Yongning Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under Guangzong he rose to grand protector and was enfeoffed as Prince of Yongning Commandery.

sentences.zh: 成恭夏皇后，袁州宜春人。

translations.literal: Empress Chenggong Xia was a native of Yichun in Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Chenggong Xia came from Yichun in Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖令吉，為吉水簿。

translations.literal: Her great-grandfather Lingji served as registrar of Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: Her great-grandfather Lingji had been registrar of Jishui.

sentences.zh: 夏氏初入宮，為憲聖太后閣中侍禦。

translations.literal: When the Xia clan woman first entered the palace she was an attendant in Empress Dowager Xiansheng's privy chamber.
translations.idiomatic: When she first entered the palace she served as an attendant in Empress Dowager Xiansheng's privy chamber.

sentences.zh: 普安郡王夫人郭氏薨，太后以夏氏賜王，封齊安郡夫人。

translations.literal: When Lady Guo, wife of the Prince of Pu'an Commandery, died, the empress dowager bestowed the Xia woman upon the prince and enfeoffed her Lady of Qi'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Lady Guo, wife of the Prince of Pu'an, died, the empress dowager gave the Xia woman to the prince and created her Lady of Qi'an Commandery.

sentences.zh: 即位，進賢妃。

translations.literal: When he took the throne she was advanced to Worthy Consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong ascended the throne she was promoted to Worthy Consort.

sentences.zh: 逾年，奉上皇命，立為皇后。

translations.literal: After more than a year, by order of the retired emperor, she was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later, on the retired emperor's order, she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 謁家廟，親屬推恩十一人。

translations.literal: She visited the family temple and favors were extended to eleven kinsmen.
translations.idiomatic: She worshipped at the family temple and eleven of her relatives received favors.

sentences.zh: 三年崩，諡安恭。

translations.literal: In the third year she died; her posthumous title was Angong.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the third year of the reign and received the posthumous title Angong.

sentences.zh: 甯宗時，改諡成恭。

translations.literal: In the Ningzong era her posthumous title was changed to Chenggong.
translations.idiomatic: Under Ningzong her posthumous title was changed to Chenggong.

sentences.zh: 初，后之生也，有異光穿室，父協奇之，及長，以姿納宮中。

translations.literal: At first, when the empress was born, a strange light pierced the room; her father Xie regarded it as marvel; when she grew up she was admitted to the palace for her beauty.
translations.idiomatic: At her birth a strange light filled the room; her father Xie took it as an omen. When she grew up she entered the palace for her looks.

sentences.zh: 久之，父居益困，及歸，客袁之僧舍，號夏翁。

translations.literal: After a long while her father's circumstances grew ever harder; when he returned he lodged as a guest at a monastery in Yuan and was styled Old Man Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Her father later fell on hard times. After leaving the capital he stayed at a monastery in Yuan and called himself Old Man Xia.

sentences.zh: 翁亡，后始貴。

translations.literal: When the old man died the empress first rose to eminence.
translations.idiomatic: Only after he died did the empress rise to high standing.

sentences.zh: 訪得其弟執中，補承信郎、閣門祗候。

translations.literal: She sought out and found her younger brother Zhizhong and appointed him Gentlemen for Fidelity and Gate-Ushers' Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: She tracked down her younger brother Zhizhong and appointed him gentleman for fidelity and gate-ushers' attendant.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷右武郎、閣門宣贊舍人，累遷奉國軍節度使，提舉萬壽觀。

translations.literal: Before long he was moved to Right Military Gentleman and Gate-Ushers' Promoter, and was successively promoted to Military Commissioner of the Fengguo Army and Superintendent of Wanshou Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became right military gentleman and gate-ushers' promoter, then rose to military commissioner of the Fengguo army and superintendent of Wanshou Abbey.

sentences.zh: 甯宗即位，加少保。

translations.literal: When Ningzong succeeded to the throne he was given the additional title Junior Protector.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningzong ascended the throne he was made junior protector.

sentences.zh: 逾年，卒於家。

translations.literal: After more than a year he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he died at home.

sentences.zh: 初，執中與其微時妻至京，宮人諷使出之，擇配貴族，欲以媚后，執中弗為動。

translations.literal: At first Zhizhong and the wife of his humble years came to the capital; palace women hinted that he should divorce her and choose a noble match, wishing to please the empress; Zhizhong would not be moved.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Zhizhong and the wife he had married in poverty came to the capital. Palace women urged him to divorce her and take a noble bride to please the empress, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 他日，后親為言，執中誦宋弘語以對，后不能奪。

translations.literal: Another day the empress spoke to him in person; Zhizhong recited Song Hong's words in reply, and the empress could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Later the empress spoke to him herself; he answered with Song Hong's saying on not abandoning one's wife, and she could not sway him.

sentences.zh: 既貴，始從師學，作大字頗工，復善騎射。

translations.literal: Once elevated he began to study under masters, wrote large characters with considerable skill, and was also adept at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: After he rose in rank he took up formal study, wrote large script with real skill, and excelled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 高宗行慶壽禮，近戚爭獻珍環，執中獨大書「一人有慶，萬壽無疆」以獻。

translations.literal: When Gaozong performed the celebratory longevity rites, near kin vied to present precious rings; Zhizhong alone wrote in large characters "When one man has blessing, myriad years know no bound" and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaozong's birthday celebration, close kin competed to offer jeweled rings; Zhizhong alone presented a large inscription reading, "When one man has blessing, myriad years know no bound."

sentences.zh: 高宗喜，錫賚甚渥。

translations.literal: Gaozong was pleased and bestowed rewards very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong was delighted and rewarded him lavishly.

sentences.zh: 嘗為館伴副使，連射皆命中，金人駭服。

translations.literal: Once as deputy mission escort he hit the mark with every shot in succession; the Jurchens were awed into submission.
translations.idiomatic: Serving once as deputy escort on a diplomatic mission, he hit every target in a row of shots and awed the Jurchen envoys.

sentences.zh: 孝宗聞其才，將召用之，謝曰：「他日無累陛下，保全足矣。」

translations.literal: Xiaozong heard of his talent and was about to summon and employ him; he declined, saying: "That on another day I may not burden Your Majesty is enough; mere preservation suffices.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong heard of his ability and meant to summon him to office; he declined, saying, "It is enough that I not burden Your Majesty later; mere safety is all I ask."

sentences.zh: 人以此益賢之。

translations.literal: People for this reason esteemed him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: People admired him all the more for this.

sentences.zh: 成肅謝皇后

translations.literal: Empress Chengsu Xie
translations.idiomatic: Empress Chengsu Xie

sentences.zh: 成肅謝皇后，丹陽人。

translations.literal: Empress Chengsu Xie was a native of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Chengsu Xie was from Danyang.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，鞠于翟氏，因冒姓焉。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, she was reared by the Zhai clan and therefore took their surname.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in childhood, she was raised by the Zhai family and took their surname.

sentences.zh: 及長，被選入宮。

translations.literal: When grown she was selected to enter the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When she came of age she was chosen for the palace.

sentences.zh: 憲聖太后以賜普安郡王，封咸安郡夫人。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xiansheng bestowed her on the Prince of Pu'an Commandery, and she was enfeoffed Lady of Xian'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xiansheng gave her to the Prince of Pu'an, and she was enfeoffed as Lady of Xian'an Commandery.

sentences.zh: 王即位，進婉容。

translations.literal: When the prince ascended the throne she was advanced to Graceful Lady.
translations.idiomatic: When he became emperor she was promoted to Graceful Lady.

sentences.zh: 逾年，進貴妃。

translations.literal: After more than a year she was advanced to Imperial Noble Consort.
translations.idiomatic: A year later she was made imperial noble consort.

sentences.zh: 成恭皇后崩，中宮虛位。

translations.literal: When Empress Chenggong died the central palace stood vacant.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Chenggong died the empress's seat remained empty.

sentences.zh: 淳熙三年，妃侍帝，過德壽宮，上皇諭以立后意。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunxi the consort attended on the emperor and passed De Shou Palace; the Retired Emperor instructed her regarding the intention to establish an empress.
translations.idiomatic: In 1176, while attending the emperor on a visit to De Shou Palace, the Retired Emperor told her of his plan to install an empress.

sentences.zh: 尋遣張去為傳旨，立貴妃為皇后，復姓謝氏。

translations.literal: Soon Zhang Qu was sent to convey the decree: the Imperial Noble Consort was established as empress and her surname Xie was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qu was soon dispatched with the decree: she was enthroned as empress and her surname Xie was restored.

sentences.zh: 親屬推恩者十人。

translations.literal: Ten kinsmen received grace by extension.
translations.idiomatic: Ten relatives received honors by extension.

sentences.zh: 光宗受禪，上尊號壽成皇后。

translations.literal: When Guangzong received the abdication her honorific was raised to Empress Shoucheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong took the throne she was given the title Empress Shoucheng.

sentences.zh: 孝宗崩，尊為皇太后。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong died she was honored as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiaozong's death she was honored as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 慶元初，加號惠慈。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingyuan additional titles Hui and Ci were added.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Qingyuan era she received the additional epithets Hui and Ci.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰二年，加慈佑太皇太后。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiatai she was given the additional title of Grand Empress Dowager Ciyou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1202 she was elevated to Grand Empress Dowager Ciyou.

sentences.zh: 三年崩，諡成肅，攢錡於永阜陵。

translations.literal: In the third year she died; her posthumous title was Chengsu; she was jointly enshrined at Yongfu Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 1203; her posthumous name was Chengsu, and she was jointly enshrined at Yongfu Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 后性儉慈，減膳羊，每食必先以進禦。

translations.literal: The empress's nature was frugal and compassionate; she reduced mutton from the diet and at every meal would first have it presented to the emperor's table.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was frugal and kindly: she cut back on lamb at court and at each meal had food sent first to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 服汗濯衣，有數年不易者。

translations.literal: She wore sweat-washed garments; some went unchanged for years.
translations.idiomatic: She wore plain washed clothes; some pieces she kept for years without replacing.

sentences.zh: 弟淵，以后貴，授武翼郎。

translations.literal: Her younger brother Yuan, on account of the empress's eminence, was appointed Wu Yi Lang.
translations.idiomatic: Her younger brother Yuan, owing to his sister's rank, was appointed gentleman at arms in the Wu Yi office.

sentences.zh: 后嘗戒之曰：「主上化行恭儉，吾亦躬服汗濯，爾宜崇謙抑，遠驕侈。」

translations.literal: The empress once admonished him, saying: "The sovereign's transformation proceeds in reverence and frugality; I too personally wear sweat-washed garments—you ought to hold humility in esteem and keep far from arrogance and extravagance."
translations.idiomatic: The empress once warned him: "The emperor's court is marked by reverence and thrift; I myself wear plain washed clothes. You should cultivate humility and shun pride and luxury."

sentences.zh: 后曆閣門宣贊舍人、帶禦器械。

translations.literal: Yuan successively served as palace gate announcer and retainer, bearer of imperial apparatus.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan served in turn as palace gate announcer and retainer, then as bearer of the imperial apparatus.

sentences.zh: 光宗朝，遷果州團練使。

translations.literal: Under Guangzong's reign he was transferred to regiment commander of Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During Guangzong's reign he was promoted to regiment commander of Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 甯宗立，轉萊州防禦使，擢知閣門事，仍幹辦皇城司。

translations.literal: When Ningzong was established he was transferred to defensive commissioner of Lai Prefecture, promoted to manager of palace gate affairs, and still oversaw the Imperial City Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningzong acceded, Yuan became defensive commissioner of Lai Prefecture, was elevated to overseer of palace gate affairs, and continued to direct the Imperial City Bureau.

sentences.zh: 三遷至保信軍節度使，尋加太尉、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: After three promotions he reached military commissioner of the Baoxin Army; soon he was further given grand marshal and grand preceptor of state with palatine equipage equal to the three top councils.
translations.idiomatic: After three further promotions he became military commissioner of the Baoxin Army, then received the ranks of grand marshal and grand preceptor of state with palatine honors equal to the three top councils.

sentences.zh: 成肅皇后崩，遺誥賜淵錢十萬緡、金二千兩、田十頃，僦緡日十千。

translations.literal: When Empress Chengsu died her testamentary edict granted Yuan one hundred thousand strings of cash, two thousand taels of gold, ten qing of fields, and ten thousand strings per day in rent monies.
translations.idiomatic: At Empress Chengsu's death her testament granted Yuan one hundred thousand strings of cash, two thousand taels of gold, ten qing of land, and a daily income of ten thousand strings from rents.

sentences.zh: 后累升三少，封和國公。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted through the three junior ranks and enfeoffed as Duke of the He State.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the three junior ranks in succession and was enfeoffed as Duke of He.

sentences.zh: 嘉定四年薨，贈太保。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiading he died; posthumously he was given grand guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1211 and was posthumously made grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 蔡貴妃

translations.literal: Imperial Noble Consort Cai
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Noble Consort Cai

sentences.zh: 初入宮，為紅霞帔，封和義郡夫人，進婉容。

translations.literal: On first entering the palace she wore the red cloud mantle and was enfeoffed Lady of Heyi Commandery, then advanced to Graceful Countenance.
translations.idiomatic: When she first entered the palace she wore the red cloud mantle, was created Lady of Heyi Commandery, and was promoted to Graceful Countenance.

sentences.zh: 冬，拜貴妃。

translations.literal: In winter she was invested as Imperial Noble Consort.
translations.idiomatic: That winter she was made Imperial Noble Consort.

sentences.zh: 十二年秋薨。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the twelfth year she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the autumn of the twelfth year of the reign.

sentences.zh: 父滂，宜春觀察使。

translations.literal: Her father Pang was surveillance commissioner of Yichun.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Pang served as surveillance commissioner of Yichun.

sentences.zh: 李賢妃

translations.literal: Worthy Consort Li
translations.idiomatic: Worthy Consort Li

sentences.zh: 李賢妃，初入宮，為典字，轉通義郡夫人，進婕妤。

translations.literal: Worthy Consort Li, on first entering the palace, served as keeper of characters; she was transferred to Lady of the Tongyi Commandery, then advanced to talented lady.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy Consort Li first entered the palace as a keeper of characters, became Lady of Tongyi Commandery, and was promoted to talented lady.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十年卒，贈賢妃。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chunxi she died; posthumously she was given worthy consort.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 1183 and was posthumously named worthy consort.

sentences.zh: 時李燾在經筵，嘗諫省後宮費。

translations.literal: At that time Li Tao was at the classics lecture and once remonstrated to reduce inner-palace expenses.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Tao served on the classics lecture and once urged curbing expenditures of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕老矣，安有是？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I am old—how could there be such a thing?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "I am an old man—when would there be anything like that?

sentences.zh: 近葬李妃用三萬緡耳。」

translations.literal: Lately the burial of Lady Li used only thirty thousand strings."
translations.idiomatic: The recent funeral of Lady Li cost only thirty thousand strings."

sentences.zh: 帝雖在位久，後宮寵倖，無著聞者。

translations.literal: Although the emperor had long been on the throne, no notable instances of favor and indulgence in the inner palace were heard of.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor had reigned for many years, no noteworthy scandals of inner-palace favoritism were ever recorded.

sentences.zh: 慈懿李皇后

translations.literal: Empress Ciyi Li
translations.idiomatic: Empress Ciyi Li

sentences.zh: 光宗慈懿李皇后，安陽人，慶遠軍節度使、贈太尉道之中女。

translations.literal: Guangzong's Empress Ciyi Li, a native of Anyang, was the middle daughter of Dao, military commissioner of the Qingyuan Army and posthumously grand marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzong's Empress Ciyi Li came from Anyang; she was the middle daughter of Dao, military commissioner of the Qingyuan Army, posthumously grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 初，后生，有黑鳳集道營前石上，道心異之，遂字后曰鳳娘。

translations.literal: At first when the empress was born a dark phoenix alighted on a stone before Dao's camp; Dao's heart regarded it as extraordinary, and he styled the empress Fengniang.
translations.idiomatic: When she was born a dark phoenix settled on a stone before her father's camp; Dao took it as an omen and gave her the childhood name Fengniang ("Little Phoenix").

sentences.zh: 道帥湖北，聞道士皇甫坦善相人，乃出諸女拜坦。

translations.literal: Dao commanded Hubei; hearing that the Taoist Huangfu Tan was skilled at physiognomy, he brought out his daughters to bow before Tan.
translations.idiomatic: When Dao commanded Hubei he heard that the Taoist Huangfu Tan excelled at reading faces and presented his daughters to Tan.

sentences.zh: 坦見后，驚不敢受拜，曰：「此女當母天下。」

translations.literal: Tan saw the empress, startled and not daring to receive her bow, saying: "This woman shall mother all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was astonished at the sight of her and refused her bow, saying: "This girl is destined to rule the empire as empress."

sentences.zh: 坦言于高宗，遂聘為恭王妃，封榮國夫人，進定國夫人。

translations.literal: Tan spoke to Gaozong, and she was then betrothed as princess of Gong, ennobled Lady of the Rong State, and advanced to Lady of the Ding State.
translations.idiomatic: Tan reported this to Gaozong; she was betrothed to the Prince of Gong, titled Lady of Rong, and promoted to Lady of Ding.

sentences.zh: 乾道四年，生嘉王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qiandao she bore the Prince of Jia.
translations.idiomatic: In 1168 she gave birth to the Prince of Jia.

sentences.zh: 七年，立為皇太子妃。

translations.literal: In the seventh year she was established as crown princess.
translations.idiomatic: In 1171 she was made crown princess.

sentences.zh: 性妒悍，嘗訴太子左右于高、孝二宮，高宗不懌，謂吳后曰：「是婦將種，吾為皇甫坦所誤。」

translations.literal: Her nature was jealous and fierce; she once complained of the crown prince's attendants to the palaces of Gaozong and Xiaozong; Gaozong was displeased and said to Empress Wu: "That woman's stock will bear ruin—I was misled by Huangfu Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Jealous and fierce by nature, she once denounced the crown prince's attendants to the retired palaces of Gaozong and Xiaozong. Gaozong was displeased and told Empress Wu: "That woman comes of violent stock; Huangfu Tan deceived me."

sentences.zh: 孝宗亦屢訓后：「宜以皇太后為法，不然，行當廢汝。」

translations.literal: Xiaozong also repeatedly admonished the empress: "You ought to take the empress dowager as your model; otherwise you will presently be deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong too repeatedly warned her: "Take the empress dowager as your model, or you will be deposed."

sentences.zh: 后疑其說出於太后。

translations.literal: The empress suspected these words came from the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The princess suspected these warnings came from the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 及太子即位，冊為皇后。

translations.literal: When the crown prince acceded he installed her as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince became emperor she was enthroned as empress.

sentences.zh: 光宗欲誅宦者，近習皆懼，遂謀離間三宮。

translations.literal: Guangzong wished to execute the eunuchs; the intimate attendants were all afraid and therefore plotted to estrange the three palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzong intended to purge the eunuchs; his intimates, fearing for themselves, plotted to drive a wedge between the three palaces.

sentences.zh: 會帝得習疾，孝宗購得良藥，欲因帝至宮授之。

translations.literal: It happened that the emperor contracted a chronic illness; Xiaozong purchased excellent medicine and wished to have it presented when the emperor came to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell into a chronic illness; Xiaozong obtained good medicine and planned to give it to him on a palace visit.

sentences.zh: 宦者遂訴於后曰：「太上合藥一大丸，俟宮車過即投藥。

translations.literal: The eunuchs then complained to the empress, saying: "The Retired Emperor has compounded a large pill of medicine; when the imperial carriage passes he will at once cast in the medicine.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs told the empress: "The Retired Emperor has prepared a large pill of medicine and will throw it into the carriage when it passes.

sentences.zh: 萬一有不虞，其奈宗社何？」

translations.literal: If by any chance there were mishap, what would become of the altars of state?"
translations.idiomatic: If anything went wrong, what would become of the dynasty?"

sentences.zh: 后覘藥實有。

translations.literal: The empress observed and verified the medicine in fact existed.
translations.idiomatic: The empress investigated and found the medicine was real.

sentences.zh: 心銜之。

translations.literal: In her heart she bore resentment.
translations.idiomatic: She harbored a deep grudge.

sentences.zh: 頃之，內宴，后請立嘉王為太子，孝宗不許。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, at an inner banquet, the empress requested establishing the Prince of Jia as crown prince; Xiaozong did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, at a private banquet, the empress asked that the Prince of Jia be named heir; Xiaozong refused.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「妾六禮所聘，嘉王，妾親生也，何為不可？」

translations.literal: The empress said: "Your servant was betrothed with the six rites—the Prince of Jia is your servant's own flesh and blood—why may it not be?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress protested: "I was wed by the full six rites; the Prince of Jia is my own son—why should that not be allowed?"

sentences.zh: 孝宗大怒。

translations.literal: Xiaozong was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 后退，持嘉王泣訴於帝，謂壽皇有廢立意。

translations.literal: The empress withdrew, took the Prince of Jia and weeping complained to the emperor, saying Shouhuang had the intention to depose them.
translations.idiomatic: She withdrew with the Prince of Jia in tears and told the emperor that the Retired Emperor meant to displace them.

sentences.zh: 帝惑之，遂不朝太上。

translations.literal: The emperor was bewildered by this and therefore did not attend court upon the Retired Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Believing her, he stopped visiting his father at the retired palace.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗宮中浣手，睹宮人手白，悅之。

translations.literal: The emperor once washed his hands in the palace and, seeing a palace woman's hands white, was pleased with them.
translations.idiomatic: Once while washing his hands in the palace he admired a maid's fair hands.

sentences.zh: 他日，后遣人送食合於帝，啟之，則宮人兩手也。

translations.literal: Another day the empress sent someone to deliver a food box to the emperor; opening it, it contained the palace woman's two hands.
translations.idiomatic: On another day the empress sent him a food box; inside were the maid's severed hands.

sentences.zh: 又黃妃有寵，因帝親郊，宿齋宮，后殺之，以暴卒聞。

translations.literal: Moreover Imperial Consort Huang had favor; because the emperor personally performed the suburban sacrifice and lodged at the purification palace, the empress killed her and reported it as sudden death.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Consort Huang also enjoyed his favor; while the emperor was lodging at the purification palace during his personal performance of the suburban sacrifice, the empress had her killed and announced a sudden death.

sentences.zh: 是夕風雨大作，黃壇燭盡滅，不能成禮。

translations.literal: That evening great wind and rain arose; the yellow altar's candles were all extinguished, and the rites could not be completed.
translations.idiomatic: That night a storm blew out every candle on the yellow altar, and the rites could not be completed.

sentences.zh: 帝疾由是益增劇，不視朝，政事多決於后矣。

translations.literal: The emperor's illness thereby grew more severe; he did not hold audience; state affairs were largely decided by the empress.
translations.idiomatic: His illness worsened; he stopped holding court, and government passed increasingly into the empress's hands.

sentences.zh: 后益驕奢，封三代為王，家廟逾制，衛兵多於太廟。

translations.literal: The empress grew more arrogant and extravagant; she enfeoffed three generations as kings; the clan temple exceeded regulations; guard troops were more numerous than at the grand temple.
translations.idiomatic: She grew ever more arrogant and extravagant: she enfeoffed three generations of her family as kings, built a clan temple in violation of statute, and stationed more guards at it than at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 后歸謁家廟，推恩親屬二十六人、使臣一百七十二人，下至李氏門客，亦奏補官。

translations.literal: When the empress returned to worship at the clan temple she extended grace to twenty-six kinsmen and one hundred seventy-two envoy-officers; down even to the Li family's gate guests, offices were also memorialized for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: On a visit to her clan temple she extended favors to twenty-six relatives and one hundred seventy-two envoy-officers; even Li family clients received appointments by memorial.

sentences.zh: 中興以來未有也。

translations.literal: Since the Restoration there had been nothing like it.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing comparable had been seen since the dynasty's restoration.

sentences.zh: 是時，帝久不朝太上，中外疑駭。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor had long not attended upon the Retired Emperor; within and without the court were suspicion and alarm.
translations.idiomatic: By then the emperor had not visited the retired palace for a long time, and court and country were troubled by suspicion.

sentences.zh: 紹熙四年九月重明節，宰執、侍從，台諫連章請帝過宮。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Shaoxi, on the Chongming Festival, grand councilors, attendants, and censorial remonstrators sent successive memorials asking the emperor to visit the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the Chongming Festival in the ninth month of 1193, grand councilors, attendants, and remonstrance officials submitted repeated memorials urging the emperor to visit the retired palace.

sentences.zh: 給事中謝深甫言：「父子至親，天理昭然。

translations.literal: Supervising secretariat drafter Xie Shenfu said: "Father and son are utmost kin; Heaven's principle is manifestly clear.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary drafter Xie Shenfu said: "The bond between father and son is the closest in nature, and Heaven's law is plain to see.

sentences.zh: 太上之愛陛下，亦猶陛下之愛嘉王。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor's love for Your Majesty is also like Your Majesty's love for the Prince of Jia.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor loves you as you love the Prince of Jia.

sentences.zh: 太上春秋高，千秋萬歲後，陛下何以見天下？」

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor's years are high; after a thousand autumns and ten thousand years, how will Your Majesty face all under Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: His years are advanced; when he is gone, how will you face the world?"

sentences.zh: 帝感悟，趣命駕朝重華宮。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved to understanding and urgently ordered his carriage to attend court at Chonghua Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by this, the emperor at once ordered his carriage to Chonghua Palace.

sentences.zh: 是日，百官班列俟帝出，至禦屏，后挽留帝入，曰：「天寒，官家且飲酒。」

translations.literal: That day the hundred officials stood in formation awaiting the emperor's emergence; reaching the imperial screen, the empress detained the emperor to enter, saying: "The sky is cold—Your Majesty, drink wine for the moment.
translations.idiomatic: That day officials waited in formation for him to emerge; at the imperial screen the empress detained him, saying: "It is cold—stay and have wine."

sentences.zh: 百僚、侍衛相顧莫敢言。

translations.literal: The hundred officials and guards looked at one another and dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and guards looked at one another in silence, none daring to speak.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人陳傅良引帝裾請毋入，因至屏後，后叱曰：「此何地，爾秀才欲所頭邪？」

translations.literal: Secretariat drafter Chen Fuliang seized the emperor's robe pleading that he not enter; going thus to behind the screen, the empress rebuked, saying: "What place is this—you scholar, do you wish to lose your head here?"
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat drafter Chen Fuliang seized the emperor's robe and begged him not to go in; following to behind the screen, the empress shouted: "What place is this—do you want your head cut off, scholar?"

sentences.zh: 傅良下殿慟哭，后復使人問曰：「此何理也。」

translations.literal: Fuliang descended the hall weeping bitterly; the empress again sent someone to ask: "What principle is this?"
translations.idiomatic: Chen descended the hall in tears; the empress sent someone to ask: "What sort of behavior is this?"

sentences.zh: 傅良曰：「子諫父不聽，則號泣而隨之。」

translations.literal: Fuliang said: "When the son remonstrates and the father does not heed, he wails and follows along."
translations.idiomatic: Chen replied: "When a son remonstrates with his father and is not heeded, he weeps and follows after him."

sentences.zh: 后益怒，遂傳旨罷還宮。

translations.literal: The empress grew angrier and thereupon transmitted an edict to dismiss and return to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The empress grew angrier still and issued an order to turn back to the palace.

sentences.zh: 其後孝宗崩，帝不能親執喪。

translations.literal: Thereafter Xiaozong died; the emperor could not personally observe the mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong died afterward, the emperor could not personally perform the mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 宰相趙汝愚謀內禪，立甯宗，尊后曰太上皇后，上尊號曰壽仁。

translations.literal: Chief councilor Zhao Ruyu plotted inner abdication, establishing Ningzong; the empress was honored as retired empress; her elevated honorific was Shouren.
translations.idiomatic: Chief councilor Zhao Ruyu engineered an inner abdication, enthroned Ningzong, and honored her as retired empress with the title Shouren.

sentences.zh: 慶元六年崩，年五十六，諡慈懿。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qingyuan she died, age fifty-six; posthumous title Ciyi.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 1200 at fifty-six; her posthumous name was Ciyi.

sentences.zh: 黃貴妃

translations.literal: Imperial Consort Huang
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Consort Huang

sentences.zh: 黃貴妃，淳熙末在德壽宮，封和義郡夫人。

translations.literal: Imperial Consort Huang, late in Chunxi was at De Shou Palace and was enfeoffed Lady of the Heyi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Consort Huang was in De Shou Palace in the late Chunxi era and was titled Lady of Heyi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 光宗為皇太子，傍無侍姬，上皇以夫人賜之，遂專寵。

translations.literal: Guangzong as crown prince had no attendant concubines at his side; the Retired Emperor bestowed this lady upon him, and she thereafter monopolized favor.
translations.idiomatic: As crown prince Guangzong had no concubines; the retired emperor gave her to him, and she thereafter enjoyed his exclusive favor.

sentences.zh: 即位，拜貴妃。

translations.literal: Upon accession she was appointed imperial consort.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne she was made imperial consort.

sentences.zh: 紹熙二年冬十一月，為皇后李氏所殺。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter in the second year of Shaoxi she was killed by Empress Li.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter 1191 she was killed by Empress Li.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而成疾。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of it and fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing of it the emperor fell ill.

sentences.zh: 又有張貴妃，亦舊侍東宮，次婕妤符氏，后出嫁於民間。

translations.literal: There was also Imperial Consort Zhang, likewise formerly attendant in the Eastern Palace; next Talented Lady Fu—the empress married them off among the common people.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Imperial Consort Zhang, another former eastern-palace attendant, and Talented Lady Fu; the empress married them off to commoners.

sentences.zh: 恭淑韓皇后

translations.literal: Empress Gongshu Han
translations.idiomatic: Empress Gongshu Han

sentences.zh: 甯宗恭淑韓皇后，相州人，其六世祖為忠獻王琦。

translations.literal: Ningzong's Empress Gongshu Han, a native of Xiang Prefecture—her sixth-generation ancestor was the Loyal and Offering King Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Ningzong's Empress Gongshu Han came from Xiang Prefecture; her sixth-generation ancestor was the Loyal and Offering King Han Qi.

sentences.zh: 初，后與姊俱被選入宮，后能順適兩宮意，遂歸平陽郡邸，封新安郡夫人，進崇國夫人。

translations.literal: At first the empress and elder sister were both selected into the palace; the empress could accommodate the intentions of both palaces and was therefore sent to the Pingyang princely residence, enfeoffed Lady of Xin'an Commandery, advanced to Lady of the Chong State.
translations.idiomatic: She and her elder sister were first selected for the palace; she won favor at both palaces and was sent to the Prince of Pingyang's residence, titled Lady of Xin'an, then Lady of Chong.

sentences.zh: 王受禪，冊夫人為皇后。

translations.literal: When the prince received the abdication the lady was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince accepted the abdication she was enthroned as empress.

sentences.zh: 后父同卿，由知泰州升揚州觀察使；

translations.literal: The empress's father Tongqing, from administrator of Tai Prefecture was elevated to surveillance commissioner of Yang Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Her father Tongqing rose from prefect of Tai Prefecture to surveillance commissioner of Yang Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 母莊氏，封安國夫人。

translations.literal: her mother, the Zhuang clan, was enfeoffed Lady of the An State.
translations.idiomatic: her mother, Lady Zhuang, was titled Lady of An.

sentences.zh: 慶元六年崩，諡恭淑。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qingyuan she died; posthumous title Gongshu.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 1200; her posthumous name was Gongshu.

sentences.zh: 同卿累遷慶遠軍節度使，加太尉。

translations.literal: Tongqing was repeatedly transferred to military commissioner of the Qingyuan Army and given grand marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Tongqing was eventually promoted to military commissioner of the Qingyuan Army and made grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 慶元五年卒，贈太師，諡恭靖。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qingyuan he died; posthumously given grand preceptor; posthumous title Gongjing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1199 and was posthumously named grand preceptor with the epithet Gongjing.

sentences.zh: 同卿季父侂胄，自以有定策功，聲勢熏灼。

translations.literal: Tongqing's younger uncle by the same father, Yuozhou, regarded himself as having merit in fixing the succession; his power and prestige blazed.
translations.idiomatic: Tongqing's uncle Han Yuozhou, claiming credit for securing the succession, wielded overwhelming influence.

sentences.zh: 同卿每懼滿盈，不敢幹政。

translations.literal: Tongqing always feared fullness and overflow and did not dare interfere in government.
translations.idiomatic: Tongqing always feared excess and refused to meddle in politics.

sentences.zh: 時天下皆知侂胄為后族，不知同卿乃后父也。

translations.literal: At the time all under Heaven knew Yuozhou as the empress's kin but did not know Tongqing was the empress's father.
translations.idiomatic: At the time everyone knew Han Yuozhou as the empress's relation, not realizing Tongqing was her father.

sentences.zh: 同卿沒一年而后崩，侂胄竟敗，人始服其善遠權熱去。

translations.literal: Tongqing died and within a year the empress died; Yuozhou ultimately was ruined—people then submitted to his having been good at keeping far from power's heat.
translations.idiomatic: Tongqing died a year before the empress; when Han Yuozhou fell at last, people came to admire how wisely he had kept his distance from factional heat.

sentences.zh: 同卿子竢，后兄也，官至承宣使。

translations.literal: Tongqing's son Si, the empress's elder brother, reached the office of commissioner for the propagation of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Tongqing's son Si, the empress's elder brother, rose to commissioner for the propagation of edicts.

sentences.zh: 恭聖仁烈楊皇后

translations.literal: Empress Gongsheng Renlie Yang
translations.idiomatic: Empress Gongsheng Renlie Yang

sentences.zh: 恭聖仁烈楊皇后，少以姿容選入宮，忘其姓氏，或云會稽人。

translations.literal: Empress Gongsheng Renlie Yang, in youth on account of bearing and appearance was selected into the palace; her surname was forgotten—some say she was from Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Gongsheng Renlie Yang entered the palace young for her beauty; her original surname was lost, though some said she was from Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 慶元元年三月，封平樂郡夫人。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Qingyuan she was enfeoffed Lady of the Pingle Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 1195 she was titled Lady of Pingle Commandery.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，進封婕妤。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year she was advanced and enfeoffed as talented lady.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of 1197 she was promoted to talented lady.

sentences.zh: 有楊次山者，亦會稽人，后自謂其兄也，遂姓楊氏。

translations.literal: There was one Yang Cishan, also from Kuaiji; the empress herself declared him her elder brother and thereupon took the surname Yang.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Yang Cishan, also from Kuaiji, claimed to be her brother; she adopted the Yang surname.

sentences.zh: 五年，進婉儀。

translations.literal: In the fifth year she was advanced to graceful lady.
translations.idiomatic: In 1199 she was promoted to graceful lady.

sentences.zh: 六年，進貴妃。

translations.literal: In the sixth year she was advanced to imperial consort.
translations.idiomatic: In 1200 she was made imperial consort.

sentences.zh: 恭淑皇后崩，中宮未有所屬，貴妃與曹美人俱有寵。

translations.literal: When Empress Gongshu died the central palace had no established occupant; the imperial consort and Lady Cao both had favor.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Gongshu's death the empress's seat was vacant; both the imperial consort and Lady Cao enjoyed favor.

sentences.zh: 韓侂胄見妃任權術，而曹美人性柔順，勸帝立曹。

translations.literal: Han Yuozhou saw the consort rely on schemes of power, while Lady Cao's nature was gentle and compliant—he urged the emperor to establish Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yuozhou saw that the consort was adept at intrigue while Lady Cao was meek; he urged the emperor to make Lady Cao empress.

sentences.zh: 而貴妃頗涉書史，知古今，性復機警，帝竟立之。

translations.literal: Yet the imperial consort had considerable acquaintance with books and histories, knew past and present, and her nature was moreover alert—the emperor ultimately established her.
translations.idiomatic: But the consort was well read, knew history, and was quick-witted; the emperor installed her after all.

sentences.zh: 次山客王夢龍知其謀，密以告后，后深銜之，與次山欲因事誅侂胄。

translations.literal: Cishan's guest Wang Menglong knew of this plot and secretly reported to the empress; the empress deeply bore resentment and with Cishan wished to take occasion to execute Yuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Cishan's client Wang Menglong learned of the scheme and secretly informed the empress; she deeply resented Han Yuozhou and plotted with Cishan to destroy him at the first opportunity.

sentences.zh: 會侂胄議用兵中原，俾皇子曮入奏：「侂胄再起兵端，將不利於社稷。」

translations.literal: It happened that Yuozhou discussed using troops in the Central Plains; he had the imperial prince Yan enter memorial: "Yuozhou again raises the edge of war—it will be inauspicious for the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: When Han Yuozhou pressed for war to recover the Central Plains, he had Prince Yan memorialized: "Han Yuozhou is reopening hostilities that will harm the realm."

sentences.zh: 帝不答。

translations.literal: The emperor did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made no reply.

sentences.zh: 后從傍贊之甚力，亦不答。

translations.literal: The empress from the side strongly seconded it; he likewise did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The empress strongly supported the memorial from his side; he still did not answer.

sentences.zh: 恐事泄，俾次山擇廷臣可任者，與共圖之。

translations.literal: Fearing the affair would leak out, she had Cishan select court ministers who could be entrusted and together plot it.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing exposure, she had Yang Cishan choose trustworthy ministers and plot with them against Han Yuozhou.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎史彌遠，素與侂胄有隙，遂欣然奉命。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Shi Miyuan had long borne a rift with Tuozhou and so gladly accepted the commission.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Miyuan, Vice Minister of Rites, had long been at odds with Han Tuozhou and accepted the assignment with alacrity.

sentences.zh: 參知政事錢象祖，嘗諫用兵貶信州，彌遠乃先告之。

translations.literal: Vice Director Qian Xiangzu had once remonstrated against using troops and been demoted to Xin Prefecture; Miyuan thereupon first informed him.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Xiangzu, Vice Director of the Secretariat, who had once opposed going to war and been banished to Xin Prefecture, was brought into the plot by Miyuan beforehand.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書衛涇、著作郎王居安、前右司郎官張鎡皆預其謀。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Wei Jing, Authoring Academician Wang Ju'an, and former Right Office Gentleman Zhang Zhen all took part in the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Wei Jing, Authoring Academician Wang Ju'an, and the former Right Office Gentleman Zhang Zhen all joined the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 開禧三年十一月三日，侂胄方早朝，彌遠密遣中軍統制夏震伏兵六部橋側，率健卒擁侂胄至玉津園，槌殺之。

translations.literal: On the third day of the eleventh month of the third year of Kaixi, while Tuozhou was at early court, Miyuan secretly sent Central Army Commandant Xia Zhen to set troops in ambush beside the Liubu Bridge; leading stalwart soldiers he seized Tuozhou, took him to Jade Ford Garden, and beat him to death.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the eleventh month in the third year of Kaixi, while Han Tuozhou was attending early court, Miyuan secretly dispatched the Central Army commandant Xia Zhen to lie in wait beside the Liubu Bridge; Xia led picked troops, seized Tuozhou, dragged him to Jade Ford Garden, and clubbed him to death.

sentences.zh: 復命彌遠。

translations.literal: He returned to report to Miyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He then reported back to Miyuan.

sentences.zh: 象祖等俱赴延和殿，以殛侂胄聞，帝不之信，越三日，帝猶謂其未死。

translations.literal: Xiangzu and the others all went to the Yenhe Hall and reported that Tuozhou had been executed; the emperor did not believe it, and after three days he still thought him not dead.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangzu and the others went together to the Yenhe Hall to announce Tuozhou's execution, but the emperor refused to believe them; three days later he still thought Tuozhou alive.

sentences.zh: 蓋是謀悉出中宮及次山等，帝初不知也。

translations.literal: For this plot had all come from the inner palace and Cishan and the rest—the emperor at first did not know.
translations.idiomatic: The whole scheme had issued from the inner palace and from Yang Cishan and his circle; the emperor had known nothing of it at the outset.

sentences.zh: 后既誅侂胄，彌遠日益貴用事。

translations.literal: After the empress had executed Tuozhou, Miyuan daily grew more eminent and wielded power.
translations.idiomatic: Once the empress had brought about Tuozhou's death, Miyuan grew ever more powerful and dominant in affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十四年，帝以國嗣未定，養宗室子貴和，立為皇子，賜名竑。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Jiading, because the succession was unsettled, the emperor adopted the imperial-clan child Guihe, established him as prince, and bestowed the name Hong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Jiading, with the imperial succession still unsettled, the emperor adopted the clansman Guihe, named him heir apparent, and granted him the personal name Hong.

sentences.zh: 彌遠為丞相，既信任於后，遂專國政，竑漸不能平。

translations.literal: Miyuan as chief councilor, having gained the empress's trust, then monopolized state affairs, and Hong gradually could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: As chief councilor Miyuan, secure in the empress's trust, came to monopolize government; Hong grew increasingly unable to stomach it.

sentences.zh: 初，竑好琴，彌遠買美人善琴者納之，而私厚美人家，令伺皇子動靜。

translations.literal: At first Hong loved the zither; Miyuan bought a beautiful woman skilled at the zither and sent her in, while privately enriching the beauty's household and ordering her to watch the prince's movements.
translations.idiomatic: Hong had a passion for the zither, so Miyuan purchased a skilled female player and presented her to him, while secretly rewarding the woman's family and instructing her to spy on the prince's every move.

sentences.zh: 竑嬖之，一日，竑指輿地圖示美人曰：「此瓊崖州也，他日必置史彌遠於此地。」

translations.literal: Hong doted on her; one day Hong pointed at the map on the carriage screen and said to the beauty, "This is Qiongya Prefecture—one day I shall surely place Shi Miyuan here."
translations.idiomatic: Hong became infatuated with her. One day he pointed to the map on his carriage screen and told her, "This is Qiongya Prefecture—one day I shall banish Shi Miyuan to this very place."

sentences.zh: 美人以告彌遠。

translations.literal: The beauty reported it to Miyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The woman reported his words to Miyuan.

sentences.zh: 竑又書字於幾曰：「彌遠當決配八千里。」

translations.literal: Hong also wrote characters on the table, saying, "Miyuan ought surely to be sentenced to exile eight thousand li."
translations.idiomatic: Hong also wrote on his table, "Miyuan deserves banishment eight thousand li away."

sentences.zh: 竑左右皆彌遠腹心，走白彌遠。

translations.literal: Those about Hong were all Miyuan's trusted agents; they ran to tell Miyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Every attendant around Hong was Miyuan's planted agent, and they hurried off to inform him.

sentences.zh: 彌遠大懼，陰蓄異志，欲立他宗室子昀為皇子，遂陰與昀通。

translations.literal: Miyuan was greatly afraid; he secretly harbored a different design, wished to establish another imperial-clan child Yun as prince, and so secretly communicated with Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Miyuan was terrified. He secretly formed another plan—to set up the clansman Yun as heir—and began covert dealings with him.

sentences.zh: 十七年閏八月丁酉，帝大漸，彌遠夜召昀入宮，后尚未知也。

translations.literal: On the dingyou day of the intercalary eighth month of the seventeenth year, as the emperor grew critically ill, Miyuan summoned Yun into the palace at night—the empress did not yet know.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingyou day of the intercalary eighth month in the seventeenth year, as the emperor lay dying, Miyuan summoned Yun into the palace by night, before the empress had learned of it.

sentences.zh: 彌遠遣后兄子谷及石以廢立事白后，后不可曰：「皇子先帝所立，豈敢擅變？」

translations.literal: Miyuan sent the empress's elder brother's sons Gu and Shi to inform her of deposing and establishing; the empress refused, saying, "The prince was established by the late emperor—how dare one change this on one's own authority?"
translations.idiomatic: Miyuan sent the empress's nephews Gu and Shi to inform her of the plan to depose Hong and enthrone Yun. She refused: "The heir was appointed by the late emperor—how dare we alter that on our own?"

sentences.zh: 是夜，凡七往反，后終不聽。

translations.literal: That night they went back and forth seven times; the empress in the end would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: That night they shuttled back and forth seven times, but the empress would not yield.

sentences.zh: 穀等乃拜泣曰：「內外軍民皆已歸心，苟不立之，禍變必生，則楊氏無唯類矣。」

translations.literal: Gu and the others then bowed and wept, saying, "Within and without, army and people have already turned their hearts—if he is not enthroned, calamity and revolt will surely arise, and then the Yang clan will have no survivor."
translations.idiomatic: Gu and the others bowed and wept, saying, "Soldiers and civilians alike have already given him their hearts. If he is not enthroned, disaster will surely follow, and the Yang house will be wiped out to the last."

sentences.zh: 后默然良久，曰：「其人安在？」

translations.literal: After long silence the empress said, "Where is that person?"
translations.idiomatic: After a long silence she asked, "Where is the man?"

sentences.zh: 彌遠等召昀入，后拊其背曰：「汝今為吾子矣！」

translations.literal: Miyuan and the others summoned Yun in; the empress patted his back and said, "You are now my son!"
translations.idiomatic: Miyuan and his allies brought Yun in. The empress patted his back and said, "You are my son now!"

sentences.zh: 遂矯詔廢竑為濟王，立昀為皇子，即帝位，尊皇后曰皇太后，同聽政。

translations.literal: They then forged an edict deposing Hong as Prince of Ji, establishing Yun as prince; he immediately took the throne, honoring the empress as empress dowager to share in government.
translations.idiomatic: They forged an edict deposing Hong as Prince of Ji, installing Yun as heir apparent. Yun ascended the throne at once, and the empress was honored as empress dowager with joint authority over government.

sentences.zh: 寶慶二年十一月戊寅，加尊號壽明。

translations.literal: On the wuyin day of the eleventh month of the second year of Baoqing, the honorific title Shouming was added.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin day of the eleventh month in the second year of Baoqing, the honorific Shouming was conferred.

sentences.zh: 紹定元年正月丙子，復加慈睿。

translations.literal: On the bingzi day of the first month of the first year of Shaoding, Ciren was again added.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingzi day of the first month in the first year of Shaoding, Ciren was added as well.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，后壽七十，帝率百官朝慈明殿，加尊號壽明仁福慈睿皇太后。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, when the empress reached seventy, the emperor led the hundred officials to pay court at Ciming Hall and added the honorific Shouming Renfu Ciren Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year, when the empress dowager turned seventy, the emperor led the entire bureaucracy to Ciming Hall and bestowed the full honorific Shouming Renfu Ciren Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 十二月辛巳，后不豫，詔禱祠天地、宗廟、社稷、宮觀，赦天下。

translations.literal: On the xinsi day of the twelfth month the empress fell ill; an edict ordered prayer at Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, the altars of soil and grain, and palace abbeys, and a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day of the twelfth month she fell ill. An edict ordered prayers at Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, the altars of soil and grain, and the palace chapels, together with a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 五年十二月壬午，崩於慈明殿。

translations.literal: On the renwu day of the twelfth month of the fifth year she died at Ciming Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the renwu day of the twelfth month in the fifth year she died in Ciming Hall.

sentences.zh: 壽七十有一，諡恭聖仁烈。

translations.literal: Her age was seventy-one; posthumous title Gong Sheng Renlie.
translations.idiomatic: She was seventy-one. Her posthumous title was Gong Sheng Renlie.

sentences.zh: 次山官至少保，封永陽郡王。

translations.literal: Cishan's office reached Junior Guardian and he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yongyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Cishan rose to Junior Guardian and was enfeoffed as Prince of Yongyang.

sentences.zh: 次山二子：谷封新安郡王，石永甯郡王。

translations.literal: Cishan's two sons: Gu was enfeoffed Prince of Xin'an commandery, Shi Prince of Yongning commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Cishan's two sons were enfeoffed as well: Gu as Prince of Xin'an and Shi as Prince of Yongning.

sentences.zh: 自有傳。

translations.literal: Each has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Each has a separate biography in these annals.

sentences.zh: 侄孫鎮，尚理宗女周漢公主，官至左領軍衛將軍、附馬都統。

translations.literal: Nephew-grandson Zhen married Princess Zhou Han of Emperor Lizong; his office reached Left Army Guard General and Commandant of the Son-in-Law's Escort.
translations.idiomatic: His grand-nephew Zhen married Emperor Lizong's daughter, Princess Zhou Han, and rose to Left Army Guard General and Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Escort.

sentences.zh: 宗族鳳孫等，皆任通顯云。

translations.literal: Clansmen such as Fengsun all held prominent posts, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Other kinsmen, including Fengsun, all held high and conspicuous office, or so it is recorded.

sentences.zh: 理宗 謝皇后

translations.literal: Emperor Lizong — Empress Xie
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xie of Emperor Lizong

sentences.zh: 理宗謝皇后，諱道清，天臺人。

translations.literal: Empress Xie of Emperor Lizong, taboo name Daoqing, was a native of Tiantai.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xie of Emperor Lizong, whose personal name was Daoqing, came from Tiantai.

sentences.zh: 父渠伯，祖深甫。

translations.literal: Her father Qu Bo, grandfather Shenfu.
translations.idiomatic: Her father was Qu Bo; her grandfather, Shenfu.

sentences.zh: 后生而黧黑，瞖一目。

translations.literal: At birth she was dark-complexioned, with one eye clouded.
translations.idiomatic: She was born with a dark complexion and a clouded eye.

sentences.zh: 渠伯早卒，家產益破壞。

translations.literal: Qu Bo died early and the family property grew ever more ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Bo died young, and the family's fortunes sank further.

sentences.zh: 后嘗躬親汲飪。

translations.literal: The empress once personally drew water and cooked food.
translations.idiomatic: As a girl she drew water and cooked meals with her own hands.

sentences.zh: 初，深甫為相，有援立楊太后功，太后德之。

translations.literal: At first Shenfu had been chief councilor and had the merit of supporting Empress Dowager Yang's installation; the empress dowager was grateful.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Shenfu had served as chief councilor, he had helped install Empress Dowager Yang, and she remained in his debt.

sentences.zh: 理宗即位，議擇中宮，太后命選謝氏諸女。

translations.literal: When Lizong took the throne, they deliberated on choosing the central palace; the empress dowager ordered selection among the daughters of the Xie clan.
translations.idiomatic: After Lizong's accession, the court debated the choice of empress. Empress Dowager Yang ordered the daughters of the Xie family brought forward for selection.

sentences.zh: 后獨在室，兄弟欲納入宮，諸父攑伯不可，曰：「即奉詔納女，當厚奉資裝，異時不過一老宮婢，事奚益？」

translations.literal: The empress alone remained at home; her brothers wished to send her into the palace, but her father's younger brother Qianbo would not allow it, saying, "Even if we obey the edict and present a daughter, we ought richly to furnish her dowry—yet in time she will be no more than an old palace attendant; what good is the affair?"
translations.idiomatic: Daoqing alone was still unmarried at home. Her brothers wanted to send her to the palace, but her uncle Qianbo objected: "Even if we obey the edict and present a daughter with a lavish trousseau, in the end she will be nothing but an old palace servant. What is the use of it?"

sentences.zh: 會元夕，縣有鵲來巢燈山，眾以為后妃之祥。

translations.literal: It happened to be Lantern Festival; in the county a magpie came to nest on the lantern hill, and the multitude took it as an omen of empress and consort.
translations.idiomatic: It happened to be the Lantern Festival, when a magpie nested on the lantern hill in the county seat. Everyone took it as an omen that a consort would rise from their house.

sentences.zh: 攑伯不能止，乃供送后就道。

translations.literal: Qianbo could not stop them and so supplied funds to send the empress on her way.
translations.idiomatic: Qianbo could not prevail and supplied the means to send her on her way to court.

sentences.zh: 后旋病疹，良已，膚蛻，瑩白如玉；

translations.literal: The empress soon took measles; when fully recovered her skin sloughed off, lustrous and white as jade;
translations.idiomatic: She soon fell ill with measles. When she recovered, her skin peeled away, leaving a complexion lustrous and white as jade;

sentences.zh: 醫又藥去目瞖。

translations.literal: physicians also treated and removed the clouded film in her eye.
translations.idiomatic: and physicians treated away the clouding in her eye as well.

sentences.zh: 時賈涉女有殊色，同在選中。

translations.literal: At the time the daughter of Jia She had exceptional beauty and was likewise among the selected.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Jia She's daughter, a woman of extraordinary beauty, was also among the candidates.

sentences.zh: 及入宮，理宗意欲立賈。

translations.literal: On entering the palace Lizong's heart inclined toward establishing Jia.
translations.idiomatic: Once they entered the palace, Lizong's inclination was to make Jia his empress.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「謝女端重有福，宜正中宮。」

translations.literal: The empress dowager said, "The Xie girl is dignified and possesses good fortune—she ought to occupy the central palace."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Yang said, "The Xie girl is dignified and blessed—she is fit for the central palace."

sentences.zh: 左右亦皆竊語曰：「不立真皇后，乃立假皇后邪！」

translations.literal: Those about the emperor also all whispered, saying, "If you do not establish the true empress, will you establish a false empress then?"
translations.idiomatic: Those around the emperor whispered among themselves as well: "Will you pass over the true empress and install a counterfeit one?"

sentences.zh: 帝不能奪，遂定立后。

translations.literal: The emperor could not prevail and so fixed the establishment of the empress.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not override her, and the choice of Xie was settled.

sentences.zh: 初封通義郡夫人，寶慶三年九月，進貴妃，十二月，冊為皇后。

translations.literal: At first she was enfeoffed Lady of Tongyi commandery; in the ninth month of the third year of Baoqing she was advanced to Noble Consort, and in the twelfth month was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: She was first enfeoffed as Lady of Tongyi. In the ninth month of the third year of Baoqing she was promoted to Noble Consort, and in the twelfth month she was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 后既立，賈貴妃專寵；

translations.literal: After the empress was established, Noble Consort Jia held exclusive favor;
translations.idiomatic: After Xie was enthroned, Noble Consort Jia held the emperor's exclusive favor;

sentences.zh: 貴妃薨，閻貴妃又以色進。

translations.literal: when the noble consort died, Imperial Consort Yan entered by her beauty.
translations.idiomatic: and when Jia died, Imperial Consort Yan won her way in by beauty.

sentences.zh: 后處之裕如，略不介懷。

translations.literal: The empress bore this with ample ease and scarcely took it to heart.
translations.idiomatic: The empress bore it all with composure and scarcely minded at all.

sentences.zh: 太后深賢之，而帝禮遇益加焉。

translations.literal: The empress dowager deeply esteemed her, and the emperor's ceremonial regard ever increased.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Yang admired her deeply, and the emperor's courtesy toward her only grew.

sentences.zh: 開慶初，大元兵渡江，理宗議遷都平江、慶元，后諫不可，恐搖動民心，乃止。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiqing, when Great Yuan troops crossed the Yangzi, Lizong deliberated moving the capital to Pingjiang and Qingyuan; the empress remonstrated that it could not be done, fearing to shake popular hearts, and so it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Kaiqing, when Yuan forces crossed the Yangzi, Lizong considered moving the capital to Pingjiang or Qingyuan. The empress dissuaded him, fearing that flight would unsettle the people, and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 理宗崩，度宗立。

translations.literal: Lizong died and Duzong succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Lizong died, Duzong ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 尊為皇太后，號壽和聖福。

translations.literal: She was honored as empress dowager with the title Shouhe Shengfu.
translations.idiomatic: She was honored as empress dowager with the title Shouhe Shengfu.

sentences.zh: 進封三代：父渠伯，魏王；

translations.literal: Three generations were advanced in rank: her father Qu Bo was made Prince of Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Three generations were ennobled: her father Qu Bo became Prince of Wei;

sentences.zh: 祖深甫、曾祖景之，皆魯王。

translations.literal: her grandfather Shenfu and great-grandfather Jingzhi were both made Princes of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: and her grandfather Shenfu and great-grandfather Jingzhi both became Princes of Lu.

sentences.zh: 宗族男女各進秩賜封賞賚有差。

translations.literal: Male and female clansmen each received promotions, enfeoffments, rewards, and gifts according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Male and female relatives each received promotions, titles, rewards, and gifts according to rank.

sentences.zh: 度宗崩，瀛國公即位，尊為太皇太后。

translations.literal: When Duzong died and the Lord of Ying succeeded, she was honored as grand empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Duzong died and the Lord of Ying took the throne, she was honored as grand empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 太后年老且疾，大臣屢請垂簾同聽政，強之乃許。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was old and ill; the great ministers repeatedly asked her to curtain the court and share in government, and only when pressed did she consent.
translations.idiomatic: Old and ill, she repeatedly refused the ministers' requests to rule from behind a screen until they pressed her and she consented.

sentences.zh: 加封五代。

translations.literal: Five generations received additional enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations of her family received additional enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: 太后以兵興費繁，痛自裁節，汰慈元殿提舉已下官，省泛索錢緡月萬。

translations.literal: The empress dowager, because military expenses were heavy in the emergency, painfully cut her own expenditures, dismissed officials from Director of Ciyuan Hall and below, and saved ten thousand strings of routine monthly requests.
translations.idiomatic: With war driving costs up, the empress dowager cut her own household spending sharply, eliminated posts in Ciyuan Hall from director downward, and saved ten thousand strings of cash in routine monthly demands.

sentences.zh: 平章賈似道兵潰，陳宜中上疏請正其罪。

translations.literal: Chief Councilor Jia Sidao's army collapsed; Chen Yizhong memorialized requesting punishment according to his crime.
translations.idiomatic: When Chief Councilor Jia Sidao's army collapsed, Chen Yizhong memorialized demanding that his crimes be punished.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「似道勤勞三朝，豈宜以一旦罪而失遇大臣禮？」

translations.literal: The empress dowager said, "Sidao labored diligently through three reigns—how can one for a single day's fault lose the ritual due a great minister?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "Sidao has served three reigns with tireless labor—how can a single day's fault justify stripping a great minister of every courtesy due him?"

sentences.zh: 先削其官，后乃置法貶死。

translations.literal: First his offices were stripped; afterward the law was applied and he was demoted to death.
translations.idiomatic: His offices were removed first; only afterward was the law invoked and he condemned to exile and death.

sentences.zh: 京朝官聞難，往往避匿遁去。

translations.literal: Capital and court officials, hearing of the crisis, often hid themselves and fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the crisis, capital and court officials often hid themselves and fled.

sentences.zh: 太后命揭榜朝堂曰：「我國家三百年，待士大夫不薄。

translations.literal: The empress dowager ordered a placard posted in the court hall, saying, "Our house of three hundred years has treated scholar-officials generously.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager ordered a placard posted in the court hall: "For three hundred years our dynasty has treated its scholar-officials generously.

sentences.zh: 吾與嗣君遭家多難，爾小大臣不能出一策以救時艱，內則畔官離次，外則委印棄城，避難偷生，尚何人為？

translations.literal: I and the successor lord meet many family hardships—yet you petty and great ministers cannot offer one strategy to save the time's extremity; within you desert your posts, without you surrender your seals and abandon cities, fleeing difficulty to save your lives—of what sort of persons are you still?
translations.idiomatic: The heir and I now face calamity upon calamity, yet you great and small cannot offer a single plan to save the realm. Within, you abandon your posts; without, you surrender your seals and desert your cities, fleeing to save your skins. What sort of men are you?

sentences.zh: 亦何以見先帝於地下乎？

translations.literal: How moreover will you face the late emperor beneath the earth?
translations.idiomatic: How will you face our late emperors in the world below?

sentences.zh: 天命未改，國法尚存。

translations.literal: Heaven's mandate is not yet changed; the state's law still exists.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's mandate has not yet shifted; the laws of the state still stand.

sentences.zh: 凡在官守者，尚書省即與轉一次；

translations.literal: As for all who hold office and guard their posts, the Department of State Affairs shall at once advance them one rank;
translations.idiomatic: Every official who remains at his post shall receive one promotion step from the Department of State Affairs;

sentences.zh: 負國逃者，御史覺察以聞。」

translations.literal: those who betray the state and flee, the Censorate shall detect and report."
translations.idiomatic: and anyone who betrays the state and flees shall be detected and reported by the Censorate."

sentences.zh: 六月朔，日食既，太后削「聖福」以應天變。

translations.literal: On the first day of the sixth month, at the completion of a solar eclipse, the empress dowager removed "Shengfu" from her title to respond to the heavenly omen.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the sixth month, when a solar eclipse reached totality, the empress dowager dropped "Shengfu" from her title to answer the heavenly warning.

sentences.zh: 丞相王爚老病，陳宜中、留夢炎庸懦無所長，日坐朝堂相爭戾。

translations.literal: Chief Councilor Wang Yan was old and ill; Chen Yizhong and Liu Mengyan were mediocre, timid, and without special ability; day after day they sat in court quarreling bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Wang Yan was old and ill. Chen Yizhong and Liu Mengyan were mediocre and timid men of no special talent, and day after day they quarreled in court.

sentences.zh: 而張世傑兵敗于焦山，宜中棄官去。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Zhang Shijie's army was defeated at Jiaoshan and Yizhong abandoned his office and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shijie's army was defeated at Jiaoshan, and Yizhong abandoned his post and fled.

sentences.zh: 太后累召不至，遺書宜中母，使勉之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager repeatedly summoned him but he did not come; she sent a letter to Yizhong's mother to urge him on.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager summoned him repeatedly, but he would not return. She sent a letter to Yizhong's mother urging her to persuade him.

sentences.zh: 十月，始還朝。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he at last returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he finally returned to court.

sentences.zh: 太后又親為書召夏貴等兵，曰：「吾母子不足念，獨不報先帝德乎？」

translations.literal: The empress dowager again personally wrote to summon the troops of Xia Gui and others, saying: "My son and I are not worth considering—but will you not repay the late emperor's kindness?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager personally wrote again to summon the forces under Xia Gui and others, saying, "My son and I are not worth your concern—but will you not repay the kindness of the late emperor?"

sentences.zh: 貴等亦罕有至者。

translations.literal: Few of Xia Gui's men came either.
translations.idiomatic: Few of Xia Gui's troops came either.

sentences.zh: 是月，大元兵破常州，太后遣陸秀夫等請和，不從。

translations.literal: That month Great Yuan troops took Changzhou; the empress dowager sent Lu Xiufu and others to sue for peace—they did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: That month Yuan forces took Changzhou. The empress dowager sent Lu Xiufu and others to sue for peace, but the enemy refused.

sentences.zh: 宜中即率公卿請遷都，太后不許，宜中痛哭固請，不得已從之。

translations.literal: Yizhong then led the dukes and ministers to request moving the capital; the empress dowager would not permit it; Yizhong wept and firmly pressed the request, and when there was no choice she assented.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yizhong then led the chief ministers in begging to move the capital. The empress dowager refused. Yizhong wept and pressed his plea until, with no alternative, she consented.

sentences.zh: 明日當啟行，而宜中倉卒失奏，於是宮車已駕，日且暮而宜中不至，太后怒而止。

translations.literal: The next day they were to set out, but Yizhong in haste lost his memorial; thus the imperial carriage was already yoked, the sun near setting, and Yizhong had not arrived—the empress dowager in anger stopped the move.
translations.idiomatic: They were to depart the next day, but Yizhong, in his haste, failed to present his memorial. The imperial carriage was already harnessed, the sun was setting, and Yizhong had not appeared. In anger the empress dowager called the move off.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，更命宜中使軍中，約用臣禮。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year she again ordered Yizhong to go to the army and negotiate, using ministerial ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year she again ordered Yizhong to the enemy camp to negotiate, on terms that treated the Yuan as a sovereign state.

sentences.zh: 宜中難之，太后涕泣曰：「苟存社稷，臣，非所較也。」

translations.literal: Yizhong found it difficult; the empress dowager wept and said, "If only the altars of state survive, minister or not is no matter for weighing."
translations.idiomatic: Yizhong balked. The empress dowager wept and said, "If the altars of state can be preserved, whether we stand as their subjects is not worth disputing."

sentences.zh: 未幾，大元兵薄皋亭山，宜中宵遁，文武百官亦潛相引去。

translations.literal: Before long Great Yuan troops pressed Gaoting Mountain; Yizhong fled by night, and civil and military officials also secretly led one another away.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yuan forces closed on Gaoting Mountain. Yizhong fled by night, and civil and military officials quietly slipped away after one another.

sentences.zh: 二月辛丑，大軍駐錢塘，宋亡。

translations.literal: On the xinchou day of the second month the great army encamped at Qiantang; Song perished.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou day of the second month the main Yuan army encamped at Qiantang, and the Song fell.

sentences.zh: 瀛國公與全后入朝，太后以疾留杭。

translations.literal: The Duke of Ying and Empress Quan entered court; the empress dowager remained at Hangzhou on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Ying and Empress Quan went to the Yuan court, while the empress dowager, citing illness, remained at Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 是年八月，至京師，降封壽眷郡夫人。

translations.literal: That year in the eighth month she reached the capital and was demoted and enfeoffed Lady of Shoujuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of that year she reached the Yuan capital and was demoted to Lady of Shoujuan.

sentences.zh: 越七年終，年七十四，無子。

translations.literal: Seven years later she died, aged seventy-four, without sons.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years later she died at seventy-four, leaving no sons.

sentences.zh: 兄奕，宋時封郡王。

translations.literal: Her elder brother Yi was enfeoffed a commandery prince in Song times.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder brother Yi had been enfeoffed as a commandery prince under the Song.

sentences.zh: 侄堂，兩浙鎮撫大使，尚榮郡公主；

translations.literal: Nephew Tang, Grand Pacification Commissioner of the Two Zhes, married the Princess of Rong commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Her nephew Tang, Grand Pacification Commissioner of the Two Zhes, married the Princess of Rong;

sentences.zh: 暨、𡌴並節度使，端平初，頗干國政云。
