translations.literal: Ji and Mao were both military commissioners; at the beginning of Duanping they were quite interfering in state affairs, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Mao both held military commissioner posts and, in the early Duanping era, were said to have meddled heavily in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 全皇后

translations.literal: Empress Quan
translations.idiomatic: Empress Quan

sentences.zh: 度宗全皇后，會稽人，理宗母慈憲夫人侄孫女也。

translations.literal: Empress Quan of Emperor Duzong was a native of Kuaiji, a grand-niece of Empress Dowager Cixian.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Quan of Emperor Duzong came from Kuaiji and was a grand-niece of Empress Dowager Cixian, Lizong's mother.

sentences.zh: 略涉書史，幼從父昭孫知岳州。

translations.literal: She had slight acquaintance with books and histories; in youth she followed her father Zhaosun when he governed Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: She had some acquaintance with books and histories. As a girl she accompanied her father Zhaosun when he served as prefect of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 開慶初，秩滿歸，道潭州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiqing, when his term ended he returned; the route passed Tan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Kaiqing, when his term ended, they returned home by way of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時大元兵自羅鬼入破全、衡、永、桂，圍潭州，人有見神人衛城者，已而潭獨不下。

translations.literal: At that time Great Yuan troops entered from Luogui, took Quan, Heng, Yong, and Gui, and besieged Tan Prefecture; some saw a divine man guarding the city, and afterward Tan alone did not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan forces had entered through Luogui, overrun Quan, Heng, Yong, and Gui, and laid siege to Tanzhou. Some reported seeing a divine being guard the walls, and in the end Tanzhou alone held out.

sentences.zh: 逾年事平，至臨安。

translations.literal: After more than a year affairs were settled and they reached Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later, when the fighting subsided, they reached Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 會忠王議納妃。

translations.literal: It happened that Prince Zhong deliberated taking a consort.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Prince Zhong was choosing a consort.

sentences.zh: 初，丁大全請選知臨安府顧嵓女，已致聘矣；

translations.literal: At first Ding Daquan had requested selection of the daughter of the prefect of Lin'an Gu Yan, and betrothal gifts had already been sent;
translations.idiomatic: Ding Daquan had first proposed the daughter of Gu Yan, prefect of Lin'an, and betrothal gifts had already been sent;

sentences.zh: 大全敗，嵓亦罷去。

translations.literal: when Daquan fell, Yan was also dismissed and left.
translations.idiomatic: but when Daquan fell, Gu Yan was dismissed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 台臣論嵓大全黨，宜別選名族以配太子。

translations.literal: Censorial officials argued that Yan was of Daquan's faction and another eminent clan ought to be chosen to match the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials argued that Gu Yan belonged to Daquan's faction and that another eminent family ought to be chosen for the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 臣僚遂言全氏侍其父昭孫，往返江湖，備嘗艱險；

translations.literal: The ministers then said the Quan lady, attending her father Zhaosun going back and forth on the rivers and lakes, had fully tasted hardship;
translations.idiomatic: Ministers then pointed out that the Quan girl, traveling with her father Zhaosun up and down the rivers and lakes, had known every sort of hardship;

sentences.zh: 其處貴富，必能盡警戒相成之道。

translations.literal: placed in rank and wealth she would surely be able to fulfill the way of mutual vigilance and support.
translations.idiomatic: and that once raised to wealth and rank she would surely practice mutual vigilance and support as a consort should.

sentences.zh: 理宗以母慈憲故，乃詔后入宮，問曰：「爾父昭孫，昔在寶祐間沒于王事，每念之，令人可哀。」

translations.literal: Lizong because of his mother Cixian therefore issued an edict for the empress to enter the palace and asked, "Your father Zhaosun, who in the Baoyou era died in the king's service—I often think of it and it is deeply pitiable."
translations.idiomatic: Out of regard for his mother Cixian, Lizong summoned the Quan girl to court and said to her, "Your father Zhaosun died in the state's service during the Baoyou era. Whenever I think of it, my heart grieves."

sentences.zh: 后對曰：「妾父可念，淮、湖之民尤可念也。」

translations.literal: The empress replied, "My father is worth remembering, but the people of Huai and the lakes are even more worth remembering."
translations.idiomatic: She replied, "Your Majesty's grief for my father is fitting—but the people of the Huai region and the lake districts are even more deserving of pity."

sentences.zh: 帝深異之，詔大臣曰：「全氏女言辭甚令，宜配塚嫡，以承祭祀。」

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply struck, and issued an edict the great ministers, "The Quan woman's words are very fitting—she ought to be matched to the legitimate heir to receive sacrificial service."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply impressed and told his ministers, "The Quan girl's words are admirable. She should be matched to the legitimate heir to carry on the ancestral sacrifices."

sentences.zh: 景定二年十一月，詔封永嘉郡夫人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year of Jingding, an edict enfeoffed her Lady of Yongjia commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the second year of Jingding an edict enfeoffed her as Lady of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 十二月，冊為皇太子妃。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month she was installed as heir apparent's consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month she was installed as the heir apparent's consort.

sentences.zh: 弟永堅等補承信郎、直秘閣。

translations.literal: Her younger brothers Yongjian and others were appointed Supplementary Gentleman and Direct Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Her younger brothers Yongjian and others were appointed Supplementary Gentleman and Direct Gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 度宗立，鹹淳三年正月，冊為皇后。

translations.literal: When Duzong was enthroned, in the first month of the third year of Xianchun she was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Duzong took the throne, she was made empress in the first month of 1267.

sentences.zh: 追贈三代，賜家廟、第宅。

translations.literal: Three generations of her forebears were posthumously honored, and a family temple and residence were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations of her ancestors received posthumous honors, and the court granted her clan a family temple and a mansion.

sentences.zh: 弟清夫、庭輝等一十五人，各轉一官。

translations.literal: Her brothers Qingfu, Tinghui, and fourteen others were each promoted one rank in office.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen of her brothers, including Qingfu and Tinghui, were each promoted one step in rank.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，后歸寧，推恩姻族五十六人，進一秩。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year the empress returned to her parents' home, and favors were extended to fifty-six affinal kin, each advanced one rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 1269 she paid a visit to her parents' home, and fifty-six relatives by marriage were each raised one rank in office.

sentences.zh: 咸平郡夫人全氏三十二人，各特封有差。

translations.literal: Thirty-two women of the Quan clan were specially enfeoffed as Ladies of Xianping Commandery, each according to a different grade.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-two women of the Quan clan received special enfeoffment as Ladies of Xianping Commandery, each at a different level.

sentences.zh: 后生子不育，次生瀛國公。

translations.literal: The empress's first son did not survive; her second son was made Duke of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Her first son died in infancy; her second son became Duke of Ying.

sentences.zh: 十年，度宗崩，瀛國公立，冊為皇太后。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Duzong died, the Duke of Ying was enthroned, and she was installed as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In 1274 Duzong died, her son the Duke of Ying succeeded, and she was made empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 宋亡，從瀛國公入朝於燕京。

translations.literal: When Song fell she followed the Duke of Ying to pay court at Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Song she accompanied the Duke of Ying to Yanjing to submit to the Yuan court.

sentences.zh: 后為尼正智寺而終。

translations.literal: The empress became a nun at Zhengzhi Temple and died there.
translations.idiomatic: She took the tonsure at Zhengzhi Temple and ended her life there as a nun.

sentences.zh: 楊淑妃

translations.literal: Imperial Concubine Yang Shu
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Concubine Yang Shu

sentences.zh: 楊淑妃，初選入宮為美人。

translations.literal: Imperial Concubine Yang Shu was first selected to enter the palace as a Beautiful Lady.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Concubine Yang Shu first entered the palace through selection as a Beautiful Lady.

sentences.zh: 咸淳三年，進封淑妃。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianchun she was advanced to Imperial Concubine.
translations.idiomatic: In 1267 she was promoted to Imperial Concubine.

sentences.zh: 推恩親屬幼節等三十四人進秩有差。

translations.literal: Favors were extended to her kin, including Youjie and thirty-three others, each promoted in rank according to a different grade.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-four of her relatives, including Youjie, received promotions at varying levels.

sentences.zh: 生建國公昰。

translations.literal: She bore Duke of Jianguo Shi.
translations.idiomatic: She gave birth to Shi, later Duke of Jianguo.

sentences.zh: 宋亡，是走溫州，又走福州。

translations.literal: When Song fell he fled to Wenzhou and then to Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Song he fled first to Wenzhou and then to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 眾推為主，冊妃為太后；

translations.literal: The multitude acclaimed him as ruler and installed the consort as empress dowager;
translations.idiomatic: The loyalists proclaimed him emperor and made the consort empress dowager;

sentences.zh: 封弟昺衛王。

translations.literal: her younger son Bing was enfeoffed as Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: and enfeoffed her younger son Bing as Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 昺，修容俞氏所生也。

translations.literal: Bing was born to Lady Yu, a Cultivated Lady.
translations.idiomatic: Bing was the son of Cultivated Lady Yu.

sentences.zh: 至元十四年，大軍圍昰於海上。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan the great army besieged Shi at sea.
translations.idiomatic: In 1277 the Yuan armies cornered Shi on the open sea.

sentences.zh: 明年四月，昰卒，昺代立。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the following year Shi died, and Bing succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following spring, and Bing took his place as ruler.

sentences.zh: 十六年春二月，昺投海死，妃聞之大慟，曰：「我艱關忍死者，正為趙氏祭祀尚有可望爾，今天命至此，夫復何言！」

translations.literal: In the second month of spring in the sixteenth year Bing threw himself into the sea and died. When the consort heard it she grieved greatly and said, "I endured hardship and clung to life only because the sacrifices of the Zhao house still held some hope—now Heaven's mandate has reached this pass; what more is there to say!"
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of 1279 Bing leaped into the sea and drowned. When she heard the news she wailed and said, "I endured every hardship and refused death only because the Zhao line still had a flicker of hope—now Heaven's mandate is ended. What more can I say!"

sentences.zh: 遂赴海死。

translations.literal: She then went into the sea and died.
translations.idiomatic: She too threw herself into the sea and died.

sentences.zh: 其將張世傑葬之海濱。

translations.literal: Her general Zhang Shijie buried her on the seashore.
translations.idiomatic: Her general Zhang Shijie buried her on the shore.
